title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Shared combinational divider with fused subtract and compare
motivation:
The baseline scores 12.12 at a median 5.442 MHz, and its reported worst
path crosses forwarding and the ALU with 156 cells and 199.837 ns arrival
time. The ALU describes signed and unsigned division and remainder with
separate / and % expressions. Their combinational implementation is the
strongest suspected source of the very deep arithmetic path, even when
CoreMark executes few divisions. The history contains only the baseline
and there is no LESSONS.md or previous divider optimization to reuse.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU datapath with one explicitly
shared, combinational unsigned quotient-and-remainder array, surrounded
by RV32M sign conversion and exceptional-result selection. Keep the ALU
interface, zero-cycle combinational latency, pipeline registers, stalls,
forwarding, multiplier, and all non-division operations unchanged. This
is an arithmetic circuit optimization, with no iterative execution unit
or additional pipeline stage.

Use 32 statically elaborated restoring steps, from quotient bit 31 down
to bit 0. Start R at the unsigned dividend magnitude. At quotient bit k,
set W=32-k and subtract divisor[W-1:0] from R[31:k] using an explicitly
unsigned W+1-bit subtraction. Accept the subtraction only when its
borrow bit is clear and all divisor bits above W-1 are zero; the latter
guard is constant true at W=32. Set quotient[k] to that decision and,
when accepted, replace R[31:k] with the low W difference bits while
preserving R[k-1:0]. Use elaboration-time special cases for empty slices.
After the last step R is the remainder. This computes quotient and
remainder together, narrows early steps, and uses the subtraction's own
borrow instead of a separate relational comparator followed by another
subtraction. Do not calculate the remainder through a serial q*divisor
multiplication, or leave any real / or % operators in the new datapath.

To shorten the serial subtraction chain, implement the trial subtractors
with four-bit carry-lookahead groups and a balanced prefix over group
generate/propagate terms, using a + ~b + 1 at exactly W+1 bits. Derive
the unsigned no-borrow decision and difference from the same carry
network. Share divisor upper-bit-zero guards as suffix reductions. The
intended timing benefit is reduced carry depth per division step; the
shared signed/unsigned quotient/remainder engine also reduces area and
routing pressure. Sharing alone is not sufficient evidence of success,
since synthesis might already merge some original arithmetic operators.

For DIV and REM, form unsigned 32-bit magnitudes using modular two's
complement; restore quotient sign from a[31]^b[31] and remainder sign
from a[31]. DIVU and REMU use operands without sign conversion. Preserve
division by zero (quotient all ones, remainder original a) and signed
INT_MIN/-1 (quotient INT_MIN, remainder zero), including INT_MIN as a
valid unsigned magnitude. Keep every RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS expression and
constant unchanged and exclude the real divider from that branch.

Validate real arithmetic with the existing ALU suite plus directed and
randomized division tests, then run the unchanged formal and cosimulation
gates and canonical CoreMark CRC/marker checks. Evaluate only vendor
Gowin timing: expect unchanged CoreMark cycles and a higher median Fmax.
A score must exceed 12.67752 to clear the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold.
The main uncertainty is whether Gowin maps the explicit carry network
better than its inferred divider; extra prefix wiring could offset the
shallower logic, or the existing implementation may already share work.
A Python model of the proposed restoring recurrence and sign handling
matched an independent integer reference on 57,672 signed/unsigned cases
spanning boundary operands and fixed-seed random pairs. This validates
the algorithm only; no candidate RTL or Gowin timing has been measured.

title: Replace combinational division with a bounded multicycle execute unit
motivation:
The baseline scores 12.12 iterations/s at a median 5.442 MHz. Its reported
worst path traverses forwarding and the execute ALU, with 156 cells and
199.837 ns arrival time. The ALU currently contains combinational signed
and unsigned division and remainder operators, making a fully unrolled
divider the leading explanation for this extreme depth. Such hardware
constrains the clock even when executing other instructions. The local
history contains only the baseline and has no prior structural attempts
or LESSONS.md. Removing this deep arithmetic path is more promising than
improving instruction throughput while keeping the same clock limit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Introduce one shared, blocking multicycle DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU unit in EX.
Use unsigned restoring division, computing eight quotient bits per cycle
with eight bounded subtract/select steps and registering the partial
remainder and quotient between groups. Four recurrence cycles replace
the current 32-step combinational operation. Capture forwarded operands
once, prepare magnitudes for signed operations, and register final sign
correction separately. Bound the schedule to eight EX service cycles:
capture, magnitude preparation, four recurrence cycles, sign correction,
and acceptance into EX/MEM. The existing liveness check triggers at
cycle 10 and requires the next retirement by cycle 20; this schedule
leaves room for pipeline bubbles, including a preceding taken branch.
Do not add extra handoff states or change any formal depth. Check the
bound on the complete pipeline as well as on the divider in isolation.
DIV and REM share quotient/remainder state; return the selected result
with RV32M divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 semantics. Leave multiplication
and ordinary integer execution unchanged.

Hold fetch and ID/EX while the division is pending, but let older MEM/WB
instructions drain. An empty EX/MEM bubble must have both valid and all
side-effect controls cleared; holding a consumed EX/MEM instruction would
repeat stores or retirement. An older stalled memory request instead
keeps EX/MEM stable under the existing dmem stall priority. Latch the
division's post-forward operands and RVFI source values before its older
forwarding producers disappear. Hold a completed result until EX/MEM
accepts it, insert it exactly once, then release the younger instruction
so dependent ALU, branch and store consumers use normal forwarding.
Reset clears pending work. Invalid instructions must never launch a unit
operation. Preserve nret=1, all top-level ports, trap checks and ordering.

Ensure the core's instantiated fast ALU has no synthesized / or % logic;
an output mux alone is not an adequate structural removal. A static
parameter/generate branch may retain the existing combinational ALU
interface for its unchanged standalone arithmetic tests while disabling
that branch in the core. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, route the exact
existing substitute formulas through the same operand capture, busy,
result-hold and completion schedule as real division. Add direct real
divider tests and integration checks so ALTOPS and the legacy standalone
ALU tests cannot conceal a broken sequential implementation.

The expected Fmax and area benefit should outweigh the added cycles of
division, but dynamic divide frequency and the next critical path remain
uncertainties. Evaluate unchanged CoreMark CRCs and timing markers under
the prescribed instruction/data stalls and compare median Gowin Fmax
times iterations/cycle. With the recorded 4,491,485-cycle baseline, the
required improvement is Fnew/5.442 * 4491485/Cnew > 1.046, with Fnew in
MHz. This is a structural execution-latency hypothesis, not a predictor,
cache, multiplier redesign or evaluation-contract change.

title: Fetch-stage bimodal prediction with immediate-derived targets
motivation:
The baseline predicts sequential execution and flushes fetch/decode for
every taken conditional branch and every JAL/JALR. Despite the five-stage
description, IF/ID is combinational: each redirect discards one younger
fetch slot. CoreMark's repeated loops and biased conditional branches
should provide enough predictable transfers to reduce measured cycles.
There are no predictor attempts in experiments/log.jsonl and no LESSONS.md.
The recorded 199.837 ns critical path runs through forwarding and the ALU,
so this proposal targets iterations/cycle, with approximately unchanged
Fmax. The added predictor must remain small to limit placement disruption.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact fetch-stage next-PC predictor: a 64-entry, two-bit
saturating bimodal direction table indexed by PC[7:2], combined with
targets decoded directly from the fetched B/J immediate. Initialize all
counters to weakly not-taken (01); their MSB predicts conditional-branch
direction. Recognize only legal BRANCH funct3 values and JAL. Predict JAL
taken unconditionally when its target is eligible; JALR and all other
instructions predict PC+4. Use full 32-bit PC-relative arithmetic and
restrict speculative taken targets to word-aligned addresses in main
memory [0x00000000, 0x00100000). An ineligible target predicts fall-through
and is resolved normally in EX. Keep the table inside if_stage.sv, with
128 counter bits and no tags, target array, global history, or return stack.

Form predictions from the raw imem_data and fetch PC, independently of
the flush-masked IF/ID instruction, to avoid combinational feedback.
Carry the exact predicted next PC with the instruction through IF/ID
and ID/EX. Only apply a prediction when the instruction is accepted:
imem is ready, no load-use/data-memory hold exists, and no older EX
correction squashes it. Prediction itself must not flush its instruction
or its correctly predicted successor. Hold the captured prediction with
the rest of ID/EX during data-memory stalls.

In EX, compute resolved_next_pc using the existing forwarded comparison,
JAL/JALR targets, and misalignment/trap behavior. Change redirect to
in.valid && !stall && (resolved_next_pc != in.predicted_next_pc), and use
resolved_next_pc as the correction target. This recovers both predicted
not-taken/actually-taken and predicted taken/actually-not-taken cases.
Compare against the captured prediction, never a fresh table lookup or
the current fetch PC. RVFI pc_wdata remains the actual resolved next PC;
JAL/JALR still write PC+4, and misaligned transfers retain the existing
trap and fall-through behavior.

Train the counter at the resolving instruction's PC only for a valid,
legal, non-faulting conditional branch advancing from EX to EX/MEM.
Increment on taken and decrement on not-taken, saturating at 11 and 00.
Do not train on bubbles, squashed instructions, or repeated cycles of a
held branch. Prediction state never changes architectural state. Reset
overrides everything; an advancing EX correction overrides fetch stalls;
a data-memory stall holds EX and defers both correction and training
until it releases. Preserve the existing MEM/WB forwarding retention.

The expected gain is from removing most warm predictable taken-branch
bubbles and aligned direct-JAL bubbles without adding a pipeline stage.
Direction aliasing and new fetch/control routing are the main risks.
An estimated 8% fitness increase is unmeasured; acceptance still requires
more than 4.6% improvement over 12.12 using the existing stalled CoreMark
run and median Gowin Fmax. Preserve nret=1, decoder legality, memory
side-effect discipline, retirement order, and every existing eval gate.

title: Halve divider recurrence depth with parallel radix-4 trial subtraction
motivation:
The champion reaches 68.55 CoreMark iterations/s at 30.789 MHz after
replacing combinational division with an eight-cycle execution unit.
Its recorded worst path is now entirely inside div_unit, from a divisor
register to a remainder register, with 37.205 ns arrival time. Each
recurrence cycle currently chains eight 33-bit subtract/select steps.
The earlier micro_opt attempt to share a fully combinational divider
regressed by 14.03 percent; arithmetic sharing and hand-written carry
logic alone did not solve its serial dependency depth. The next local
opportunity is to shorten the existing registered recurrence without
increasing division latency or changing the pipeline.

replacing combinational division with an eight-cycle execution unit.
Its recorded worst path is now entirely inside div_unit, from a divisor
register to a remainder register, with 37.205 ns arrival time. Each
recurrence cycle currently chains eight 33-bit subtract/select steps.
The earlier micro_opt attempt to share a fully combinational divider

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the eight radix-2 restoring steps inside each STEP0..STEP3
cycle with four radix-4 restoring steps. Compute two quotient bits per
step using parallel trial subtractions by D, 2D and 3D, then select the
largest multiple that does not exceed the trial remainder. This halves
the number of serial subtract/select boundaries while retaining four
recurrence cycles and the existing capture, PREP, SIGN and DONE states.
This is a local arithmetic implementation change: preserve the module
interface, handshake, instruction latency, pipeline and nret=1 contract.

In PREP, compute the unsigned dividend and divisor magnitudes exactly
as today and register the divisor multiples. Use explicit unsigned
34-bit D, 2D and 3D values; shifts must be widened before shifting and
3D must be calculated from the new magnitude, not the old divisor
register. Register the multiples before STEP0 so calculating 3D is not
repeated in each recurrence's critical path. Keep quotient initialized
to the dividend magnitude and remainder initialized to zero.

Each of the four combinational radix-4 steps forms the 34-bit trial
T = {R[31:0], Q[31:30]}. Calculate three independent unsigned 35-bit
differences {1'b0,T} - {1'b0,kD}, for k=1,2,3. Their high bits are
borrow indicators. Select digit 3 if 3D fits, else 2 if 2D fits, else
1 if D fits, else 0. Select the corresponding low 32 difference bits
(or T[31:0] for digit 0) as the next remainder, and shift Q left two
bits while appending the two-bit digit. Express mutually exclusive
digit enables and a parallel result mux, avoiding a subtract followed
by a second comparator or a serial cascade of three subtractors.
After four such steps register Q and R, then repeat for four cycles.
For D != 0, R < D guarantees the selected remainder fits 32 bits.

Preserve original operands, sign flags, RV32M quotient/remainder sign
correction, INT_MIN/-1 behavior and the final divide-by-zero override.
The zero-divisor case must still return quotient 0xffffffff or original
dividend as remainder; its internal recurrence need not satisfy R<D.
Do not use real / or % operators. Keep the RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas,
constants and cycle-by-cycle handshake unchanged, excluding the real
datapath in ALTOPS as before. DONE must hold the result until accepted,
reset must cancel execution, and the unchanged formal liveness window
must still pass. Retain all existing correctness checks.

Validate the sequential divider directly with real arithmetic and
signed/unsigned edge and randomized cases; the standalone ALU's legacy
combinational division tests do not exercise this unit. Run the existing
pipeline, formal, cosimulation and canonical CoreMark checks unchanged.
With identical latency, CoreMark cycles should remain 4,491,485 under
the same stalls. The acceptance target is fitness above 71.7033, or
median Gowin Fmax above approximately 32.2053 MHz at unchanged cycles.
The expected gain comes from shorter arithmetic depth; the main risks
are routing and area from parallel subtractors, PREP's magnitude/3D
path, and another CPU path becoming the clock limit. Measure vendor
timing rather than assuming a twofold Fmax gain from halving the steps.

A width-accurate Python model of this recurrence and sign correction
matched an independent integer reference on 122,608 operation cases
across 30,652 operand pairs. These included boundary cross-products,
values around D/2D/3D and 20,000 fixed-seed random pairs. Every modeled
intermediate remainder with a nonzero divisor satisfied 0 <= R < D
and fit 32 bits. This checks the proposed arithmetic algorithm only;
candidate RTL simulation and Gowin timing have not been performed.

title: Retiming the divider into five-step recurrence cycles
motivation:
The winning structural attempt removed combinational division and raised
median Gowin Fmax to 30.789 MHz, but the new worst path still lies wholly
inside u_div: divisor to remainder, with 37.205 ns reported arrival time
and 239 cells. Its recurrence chains eight full-width subtract/select
steps between registers. The previous shared combinational-divider
attempt regressed, so sharing arithmetic without breaking dependency
depth is insufficient. The measured CoreMark bracket remained exactly
4,491,485 cycles after introducing the sequential divider. Shortening
its register-to-register path is therefore the strongest remaining
structural opportunity. Simply adding recurrence cycles would conflict
with the existing bounded-progress checks.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition the existing blocking divider across its existing eight EX
service edges. Replace capture, PREP, four eight-bit recurrence cycles,
SIGN, acceptance with: capture/magnitude preparation/first two quotient
bits together, six five-bit recurrence cycles, then sign correction and
EX/MEM acceptance together. This computes 2 + 6*5 = 32 quotient bits and
reduces the repeated full-width dependency chain from eight restoring
steps to five without increasing instruction latency. This is one
structural change to execution-stage register placement and scheduling.

At the launch edge, use the already forwarded operands to capture the
original a/b/op, magnitude divisor, quotient/remainder sign flags, and
result selection. Also consume magnitude-dividend bits 31 and 30 into
the initial quotient/remainder state. Implement this prologue as two
explicitly narrow trial subtractions: the first shifted remainder has
one significant bit, the second has two. At each step reject subtraction
if any magnitude-divisor bits above that width are nonzero; otherwise
use a width+1 subtraction and its borrow bit. Preserve the unconsumed
dividend bits in the shifted quotient register. This avoids placing
two unnecessary 33-bit subtractors after the forwarded-operand mux and
magnitude negation on the launch path. The magnitude of INT_MIN remains
the unsigned value 0x80000000.

On each of the next six edges, advance five ordinary restoring steps
using the registered divisor, partial remainder and quotient. Retain
the current explicitly unsigned 33-bit subtract/borrow semantics and
register the selected remainder and quotient after each group. After
the sixth group, enter DONE and assert result_valid. Thus result_valid
first appears after service edge seven, exactly as in the current unit.
Never add an extra PREP, SIGN, or completion handoff cycle.

Form result combinationally from the now-registered final quotient or
remainder, captured sign flags and captured exceptional-case operands.
The existing EX/MEM register captures this corrected result on service
edge eight. This moves the small sign-correction stage onto the existing
acceptance path instead of dedicating a divider cycle/register to it.
Freeze every result source throughout DONE, so result remains stable
for arbitrarily delayed acceptance. Preserve quotient all ones and
original dividend remainder on divide by zero, signed INT_MIN/-1,
truncation toward zero, and signed remainder semantics. Keep the unit's
start/busy/result_valid/result_accept interface and existing EX operand
capture, forwarding, stalls, bubbles and single-retirement behavior.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, retain the exact current four substitute
formulas and constants over captured original operands, and run the
identical new state/count schedule and completion handshake. The core
ALU must still statically exclude combinational division. Preserve all
existing tests, including edge-seven result availability, edge-eight
acceptance, the pipeline's maximum nine-cycle ready-bus retirement gap,
and the unchanged formal trigger-10/check-20 liveness window. Reset
cancels all pending work; busy or held-DONE starts cannot overwrite it.
Preserve nret=1, decoder legality, RVFI source values and contiguous
order, and every memory and benchmark invariant.

The expected gain is higher Fmax with unchanged CoreMark cycles, with
roughly 40 MHz corresponding to a 30 percent fitness improvement.
Launch-time magnitude conversion, the new sign-correction acceptance
path, multiplication, or routing may become the next clock limit; the
five-step chain does not imply a proportional whole-core speedup.
Validate real and ALTOPS arithmetic/handshakes and the unchanged formal,
cosim, canonical CRC and marker gates, then measure median vendor Gowin
Fmax. Acceptance requires fitness above 71.7033, or approximately
32.206 MHz if bracket cycles remain unchanged. The forecast is an
architectural estimate; no candidate RTL timing has been measured.
A Python model of the narrow two-bit prologue, six five-bit groups and
final sign/exception correction matched an independent integer RV32M
reference on 212,496 cases, including power-of-two boundaries and
fixed-seed random operands. This checks the arithmetic decomposition,
not the RTL handshake, formal progress, or physical timing.

title: Tagged next-PC prediction for branches and repeated indirect jumps
motivation:
The current core fetches sequentially and discards one younger fetch slot
whenever EX resolves a taken branch or jump; IF/ID is combinational, so
the penalty is one slot rather than two registered front-end stages.
The prior predictor hyp-20261003-003-r1s2 reduced measured CoreMark cycles
from 4,491,485 to 4,201,766, a 6.45% reduction. It was evaluated on the
old combinational-divider baseline at 5.359 MHz, not on the current
30.789 MHz multicycle-divider champion. Its regression classification
does not show that prediction loses throughput on the champion.
LESSONS.md identifies removal of combinational division as the major
clock improvement; preserve that implementation completely. The current
worst path remains inside the registered divider, leaving a plausible
timing budget for a compact predictor. Predicting cached targets also
covers repeated JALR targets that the previous B/J-only design missed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 64-entry direct-mapped tagged next-PC predictor inside if_stage.
Each entry stores a valid bit, source-PC tag, aligned target word
address, conditional/unconditional kind, and a two-bit saturating
conditional-direction counter. Index with PC[7:2]. Restrict lookup and
allocation to word-aligned source PCs and targets in the architectural
main-memory region [0x00000000, 0x00100000). With a separate upper-PC
range check, PC[19:8] is a complete 12-bit tag for eligible source PCs;
store target[19:2] and reconstruct {12'b0, target_word, 2'b00}.
Total logical state is 2,176 bits. Reset valid bits; tag/target data can
remain unreset behind validity to permit efficient memory inference.
Initialize counter and kind on every allocation before marking valid.
Use generic synthesizable arrays and no new source-list dependency.

A valid tag hit predicts its cached target for unconditional transfers
or when a conditional counter's MSB is one; otherwise predict PC+4.
JAL and JALR share unconditional entries, with JALR using its last
resolved target. Misses predict PC+4 and learn in EX. Prediction is a
function of the registered fetch PC and table state, independent of
raw or flush-masked instruction data. There is no instruction-to-target
adder in the fetch path, no speculative history, and no return stack.
Keep imem_addr driven solely by the PC register. Advance it using the
prediction only when that fetched instruction enters ID/EX: imem ready,
no load-use hold, no dmem hold, no execute_wait, and no older correction.
Carry that exact chosen predicted_next_pc in IF/ID and ID/EX, holding
it with the instruction under stalls. Define same-edge lookup/training
behavior consistently: PC selection and captured prediction must see
the same pre-edge table contents; do not add a write-through bypass.

In EX form actual_next_pc with the existing forwarded branch comparison,
JAL/JALR target calculation, JALR bit-zero clearing, and trap handling.
Misaligned transfers retain their existing trap, suppressed link write,
and PC+4 behavior. An instruction advances only when in.valid && !stall
&& !execute_wait. Assert correction only on such advancement and when
actual_next_pc differs from the captured predicted_next_pc. Check every
instruction, not just decoded control transfers, so even a stale entry
for a replaced instruction recovers to its actual successor. RVFI
pc_wdata is actual_next_pc and JAL/JALR link data remains PC+4.
Flush the younger slot only on a correction; a correct taken prediction
must keep its successor. Correction overrides imem/load-use fetch holds.
An older dmem stall holds EX and defers both correction and training;
divider wait also forbids either action until the instruction advances.

Train once per advancing valid legal non-faulting control transfer.
For a matching conditional entry, retain its PC-relative branch target
and saturating-increment/decrement the current stored counter on the
actual outcome. Allocate a missing conditional entry only on taken,
initializing to weakly taken (10); a not-taken miss already predicts
correctly and must not evict a useful target. For matching stale kind
or changed-target entries, replace metadata using the current decode
and resolved target, initializing direction from the actual outcome.
For JAL/JALR cache the resolved target and mark unconditional, updating
the target when it changes. Allocate only eligible source/target pairs.
Invalidate a matching stale entry when its source resolves as a
non-control instruction, illegal instruction, faulting transfer, or
transfer to an ineligible target. Do not invalidate another PC's entry
on an index collision. No updates on bubbles, squashes, reset, held
instructions, or unfinished divisions. Prediction errors may cost a
fetch slot but cannot authorize memory side effects or retirement.

The single optimization is cached next-PC prediction, with expected
fitness improvement of 10% from fewer control-transfer bubbles. The
preceding predictor's measured cycle saving supports the direction;
additional JALR hits are plausible but unmeasured. Capacity collisions,
multi-caller returns, and table mux/routing delay are the main risks.
Preserve the existing divider, arithmetic, nret=1, top-level ports,
decoder legality, stall generators, RVFI ordering, and all eval gates.
Run existing unit tests, formal and stalled CoreMark cosim with all
canonical CRCs and timing markers, then vendor median-Fmax evaluation.
Acceptance requires Fnew/30.789 * 4,491,485/Cnew > 1.046, equivalently
fitness above approximately 71.70 iter/s; cycle improvement alone is
insufficient. At the previous 4,201,766-cycle result the design would
need more than 30.13 MHz, so clock preservation matters.

title: Remove redirect from decode payload paths with validity-only flushing
motivation:
The champion scores 102.93 iterations/s at 46.231 MHz with 4,491,485
measured CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path now runs from the
MEM/WB destination register through forwarding, EX branch resolution,
IF instruction masking and hazard logic to an ID/EX operand register
(27.462 ns reported arrival, 37 cells). Divider retiming has exposed a
control path through wide decode data: IF replaces the entire instruction
with a NOP on redirect, and ID clears its entire bundle on flush. Earlier
micro_opt divider experiments improved arithmetic depth but did not
produce the current champion. The strongest new local opportunity is
removing this late redirect signal from decode payload muxes and enables.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make pipeline bubbles depend on the existing ID/EX valid bit rather than
clearing or masking the whole decode payload. This is a local control
factoring optimization: retain the pipeline stages, branch resolution
cycle, forwarding priorities, memory handshake and divider schedule.

In if_stage, drive out.instr directly from imem_data even on flush or
redirect. Retain out.valid = !(flush || redirect), the current PC update
priorities, and the unchanged imem address interface. Decoding invalid
or wrong-path instruction bits is harmless only when validity guards
every downstream consumer with architectural or interlock effects.

In id_stage, separate the ID/EX valid register update from every other
payload field. Keep reset initialization. Update pc, instruction, source
values/addresses, immediate, destination and decoded controls only when
!stall; flush must not clear, select, or inhibit these payload updates.
Update valid with reset/flush priority over stall: clear on reset or
flush, hold on stall, otherwise capture in.valid. In particular a
load-use bubble clears valid while retaining the stalled old payload;
a redirect can capture arbitrary raw wrong-path payload with valid=0.
Do not introduce an in.valid-conditioned payload mux that recreates the
same redirect-to-data path. Do not change the decoder's default-illegal
discipline or its interpretation of any instruction encoding.

Qualify the hazard unit's ID/EX load indication with id_ex_w.valid at
the core connection. This is essential because an invalid bubble may
now retain mem_read=1 and a nonzero destination from an earlier load.
Keep raw IF instruction source fields independent of redirect; their
incidental matches during an unavailable fetch cannot advance the PC
because imem_ready already stalls it. Keep redirect priority over PC
stall. Preserve dmem/execute hold priority over ID flushing. Audit every
consumer of ID/EX controls: EX already qualifies division and redirect
with in.valid, and clears the entire EX/MEM bundle on !in.valid when
not stalled. Retain that EX/MEM bubble clearing, since memory requests
and forwarding use its controls. Leave MEM/WB's retained forwarding
payload under dmem backpressure and retirement qualification unchanged.

The intended physical change is removal of redirect from the 32-bit
fetch instruction mux, regfile read-address path, load-use comparison
path and wide ID/EX flush muxes. Redirect still kills valid and updates
PC in the same cycle. This should raise Fmax without adding a branch
bubble or changing the CoreMark instruction/cycle schedule. A different

title: Separate pipeline validity from payload to cut redirect feedback
motivation:
The two successful structural attempts removed combinational division and
retimed its recurrence, reaching 102.93 iterations/s at 46.231 MHz with
4,491,485 measured CoreMark cycles. The latest reported worst path has
moved out of the divider: MEM/WB rd through u_fwd, u_ex, u_if, u_hazard
and into an ID/EX rs2-value register, with 37 cells and 27.462 ns arrival.
In the current topology a forwarded branch decision replaces the fetch
instruction with a NOP. Its bits then feed source-address comparisons,
decode and register-file reads, while flush clears the entire ID/EX
bundle. This couples late execute control to younger instruction data.
Prior predictor attempts improved cycles but lost to clock limitations;
the new opportunity is removing this feedback from the pipeline payload.

validity and payload state. A squash changes whether an instruction may
execute; it need not rewrite that instruction or its operand data. Keep

divider service schedule. The single architectural change is separating
token validity from payload transport and its hazard-control consumers.

a permitted redirect or load-use bubble clears only validity. Otherwise

when advancing. Keep the existing precedence: dmem backpressure and a
pending division retain the active ID/EX instruction, while load-use
inserts a bubble when not overridden by those holds. Payload registers
may capture raw decode and register-file values whenever the stage is
not held, including a squash edge, or retain old values while held.
Do not put redirect, flush or fetch-valid in their data muxes, reset
terms or clock enables. Initialization on reset may remain. Their bits
are architecturally irrelevant while ID/EX.valid is zero.

Rebuild the load-use dependency from raw instruction source fields and
independently available state: ID/EX.valid, its load control and nonzero

signal already includes redirect, nor use an instruction masked by a
redirect. Compute load-use, dmem hold and execute hold independently;
merge redirect only into the validity-kill decision and PC redirect.
Preserve the existing conservative source-field comparison behavior so
this change adds no speculative execution, stage or dependency latency.

Audit every consumer of an invalid ID/EX payload. In particular qualify
its load hazard with valid, keep division launch and branch redirect
qualified by valid, and retain EX's existing all-zero EX/MEM bubble when
ID/EX is invalid or division is waiting. Thus stale decoded controls
never become memory operations, register writes, forwarding producers
or retirements. Keep the downstream zero-control bubbles and the current
MEM/WB forwarding retention on dmem stalls: its valid bit can be zero
while its prior result is still needed by a held EX operand. Do not
simply gate that retained bypass source with retirement-valid. Preserve
nret=1, RVFI operands and order, trap discipline, memory acceptance and
all real/ALTOPS arithmetic and bounded-progress checks.

This should remove the serial redirect-to-instruction-to-hazard/read
path and reduce squash fanout without adding a taken-branch penalty or

iterations/s; at 4,491,485 cycles for ten iterations this is approximately

and marker checks, then compare median vendor Gowin timing and actual
bracket cycles. Inspect that the old redirect-to-decode payload path has
disappeared rather than relying on place-and-route noise.

title: Bimodal direct-transfer prediction with direction-only recovery
motivation:
Sequential fetch currently discards one younger fetch slot on each taken
branch or jump; IF/ID is combinational, so this is a one-slot penalty.
Prior predictor hyp-20261003-003-r1s2 reduced measured CoreMark cycles
from 4,491,485 to 4,201,766 (6.45%). The tagged target predictor in
hyp-20261003-003-r2s2 reached 4,186,330 cycles (6.79%), only a small
additional saving. Both were evaluated before the current five-step
divider retiming. Their regression labels do not establish that
prediction would lose fitness on the current 46.231 MHz champion.
LESSONS.md supports preserving the winning divider schedule completely.
The champion's reported worst path now runs through forwarding, EX,
IF, hazard control and ID. A full next-PC equality check and a redirect
dependent instruction mask would put extra work on this sensitive path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 64-entry, two-bit bimodal predictor for direct conditional
branches and JAL, using the actual fetched instruction's immediate for
the target. Couple this predictor to direction-only EX recovery and
valid/flush-based squash control. This is one direct-transfer predictor
design: its recovery and squash plumbing must preserve the timing gains
of the existing divider. Do not add a BTB, JALR predictor, return stack,
global history, extra pipeline stage or arithmetic-unit changes.

Index the 128-bit counter table with fetch PC[7:2], initialize all
counters to weakly not-taken (01), and use the MSB as the conditional
direction prediction. Predecode raw imem_data, recognizing only BRANCH
funct3 values 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 and 7, or JAL. JAL predicts taken. Form the
sign-extended B/J immediate and add it to the full 32-bit fetch PC.
Allow a taken prediction only for word-aligned source and target PCs
in [0x00000000, 0x00100000); detect range after the full addition, without
truncating or wrapping addresses into memory. Otherwise predict PC+4.
JALR and all non-control or reserved encodings predict fall-through.
Keep imem_addr driven by the PC register. Select a prediction only when
the fetched instruction is accepted into ID/EX: imem ready, no load-use
hold, no dmem hold, no execute_wait and no older EX correction. Reset
wins first, then advancing EX correction, then fetch hold, then the
predicted successor. An advancing correction wins over imem unready.

Carry only a predicted_taken bit with the instruction in IF/ID and
ID/EX, holding it with the instruction on stalls. It records the actual
gated choice, not merely the direction counter MSB. A direct target is
always derived from this exact instruction and PC at fetch and EX;
therefore checking the direction suffices without storing or comparing
a 32-bit predicted next PC. Counter aliasing can affect direction but
cannot supply another instruction's target. Both the PC choice and
captured bit use pre-edge counter state, with no training bypass.

In EX define actual_taken as a legal branch with a true forwarded
comparison, or a legal jump, with the existing target-misalignment
suppression applied. Define ex_advance as in.valid && !stall &&
!execute_wait. Assert correction on ex_advance &&
(actual_taken != in.predicted_taken). JALR is always predicted false,
so a legal aligned JALR corrects normally. A taken prediction followed
by an actually untaken branch corrects to in.pc+4. Other corrections
select the existing resolved branch/JAL/JALR target. Use the existing
actual next-PC expression for RVFI, including fall-through on traps;
keep link writes, JALR bit-zero clearing and trap write suppression.
A direction mismatch may harmlessly flush even if target equals PC+4.
Do not create a wide target comparison in the correction-enable cone.
Correctly predicted transfers retain their younger successor.

Make squash control independent of the instruction bits used by the
predictor, decoder, register-file read addresses and load-use compares.
Pass raw imem_data through the IF/ID instruction field rather than
multiplexing it to NOP on redirect. Suppress acceptance with valid and
ID/EX flush instead. Compute load-use dependencies from these raw
source fields, independently of redirect and flush-masked validity.
When ID accepts an invalid fetch, clear the entire ID/EX bundle,
including controls; clearing only valid would let invalid memory or
forwarding controls leak into downstream logic. Keep older dmem and
divider holds above fetch invalidation, and retain the existing
load-use bubble and correction-flush priorities. A spurious dependency
in the squashed raw instruction must never defeat a correction.
This removes the EX-correction -> IF instruction mask -> hazard/decode
serial path while leaving correction on the explicit register flush
and PC-selection controls. Preserve MEM/WB forwarding retention.

Train the indexed counter exactly once for an advancing legal,
non-faulting conditional branch: saturating increment for taken and
decrement for not-taken. Use the current stored counter at the resolving
PC, not a stale counter snapshot carried through stalls. Do not train
on JAL/JALR, bubbles, squashed instructions, held EX cycles or incomplete
divisions. Reset overrides training. A dmem-held branch defers both
training and correction until it advances; prediction has no authority
to commit side effects or retire instructions.

The forecast is an unmeasured 10% fitness gain, based on recovering the
earlier direct predictor's approximately 6.45% cycle reduction and
avoiding the newly exposed correction-control timing bottleneck. Fetch
immediate addition, counter selection and placement remain timing
risks; direction-only recovery does not guarantee higher Fmax. At
4,201,766 cycles, beating the 102.93 iter/s champion by more than 4.6%
requires median Fmax above approximately 45.24 MHz (fitness >107.665).
Validate the existing unit, formal and stalled CoreMark cosimulation
gates, all canonical CRCs and marker timing, then measure vendor median
Fmax and the actual product. Preserve nret=1, core ports, the divider,
decoder legality, architectural address rules and every eval invariant.

title: Mixed-radix trials shorten the five-bit divider recurrence
motivation:
The current champion achieves 114.45 CoreMark iterations/s at 48.089 MHz
and 4,201,740 measured cycles. Its reported worst path is entirely in
div_unit, from quotient to remainder, with 163 cells and 26.115 ns
arrival time. Each of the six recurrence cycles currently chains five
full-width restoring subtract/select steps. This arithmetic depth costs
clock frequency even when the executed instruction is not a division.
LESSONS.md and the micro_opt history show that parallel radix-4 trials
previously raised Fmax from 30.789 to 42.390 MHz at unchanged cycles;
that candidate lost to a separately retimed 46.231 MHz divider. Apply
that demonstrated arithmetic optimization to the winning five-bit
grouping, retaining its two launch bits and eight-edge service schedule.

LESSONS.md and the micro_opt history show that parallel radix-4 trials

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real divider's five serial radix-2 steps per STEP0
through STEP5 cycle with two radix-4 restoring steps followed by one
radix-2 restoring step. Each cycle still consumes exactly five dividend
bits. Keep the current launch edge's two narrow steps, six recurrence
edges, and final corrected EX/MEM acceptance edge. This is a local
combinational arithmetic replacement with unchanged interface, state
schedule, instruction latency, pipeline, predictor and bus handshakes.
The mechanism is five dependent subtract/select boundaries becoming
three, with the three candidate subtractions of each radix-4 step
evaluated in parallel.

At launch compute unsigned dividend and divisor magnitudes exactly as
today. Retain the current quotient/remainder initialization after the
top two dividend bits. Also register 3D from the new divisor magnitude,
using explicitly widened 34-bit operands before shifting or adding.
D is the registered 32-bit divisor; form 34-bit D and 2D by zero
extension and wiring, and hold the registered 34-bit 3D for the entire
operation. Do not derive 3D from the previous divisor register, compute
it on the recurrence path, or add a preparation cycle. The launch
magnitude-to-3D adder is a timing risk to check in Gowin.

For each radix-4 step form unsigned T={R[31:0],Q[31:30]} at 34 bits.
In parallel compute 35-bit differences {1'b0,T}-{1'b0,D34},
{1'b0,T}-{1'b0,D2_34}, and {1'b0,T}-{1'b0,D3_34}. Each high bit is
an unsigned borrow. Choose digit 3 when 3D fits, else digit 2 when
2D fits, else digit 1 when D fits, otherwise digit 0. Express exclusive
digit enables and a parallel masked-OR result selection so a priority
cascade of wide muxes does not replace the removed arithmetic depth.
The next remainder is the selected difference's low 32 bits, or
T[31:0] for digit 0; shift Q left two bits and append the selected
two-bit digit. For nonzero D, R<D proves the chosen remainder fits
32 bits even when the unselected trial or multiples do not.

After two such steps, apply one existing radix-2 step: subtract
{1'b0,D} from {R,Q[31]} at 33 bits; a clear borrow selects the
difference and appends quotient bit 1, otherwise retain the shifted
trial and append 0. Register that fifth bit's quotient and remainder
in the existing state registers. Six groups consume the remaining
30 bits after launch, so no counter or completion timing changes.
Internal remainder bounds need not hold for D=0; preserve the final
architectural override returning all-ones quotient or original a.

Retain signed magnitude conversion and quotient/remainder sign
restoration, including INT_MIN/-1, INT_MIN magnitudes and all four
DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU encodings. Preserve the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS
formulas and cycle-by-cycle control schedule; compile the real
datapath out under ALTOPS. Keep DONE result stability under arbitrary
backpressure, reset cancellation, captured forwarded operands and
once-only acceptance unchanged. Do not introduce real / or % hardware.

Validate real sequential arithmetic directly, since default formal
uses ALTOPS and the standalone ALU tests exercise a different divider.
Add boundary and randomized cases stressing quotient digits 0..3,
D/2D/3D comparisons, large unsigned divisors and register boundaries
between five-bit groups. Preserve existing latency, backpressure,
reset and pipeline-progress tests and run unchanged formal/cosim
gates plus the canonical stalled CoreMark CRC and marker checks.
CoreMark cycles should remain exactly 4,201,740 with identical inputs
and stalls. Measure median vendor Gowin Fmax and its product with
iterations/cycle; success requires fitness above 119.7147, or roughly
50.301 MHz at unchanged cycles, to exceed the 4.6 percent threshold.
The forecast is an unmeasured 15 percent fitness improvement. Extra
trial-adder routing, launch 3D generation, or a newly dominant multiply
or fetch path could cap the gain. Preserve nret=1, all core ports and
every correctness invariant and evaluation file.

A width-accurate Python model checked 49,266 operand pairs across all
four RV32M division/remainder operations, giving 197,064 matching
results against an independent integer reference. It also matched
the current radix-2 recurrence at every one of the six register
boundaries, checked nonzero-divisor remainder bounds, and exercised
all four quotient digits across 1,182,384 radix-4 steps. Cases include
signed extremes, zero divisors, near-multiple thresholds and 40,000
fixed-seed random pairs with both small and full-width divisors.
This validates the proposed arithmetic algorithm only; candidate
RTL simulation and Gowin timing have not been performed.

title: Decouple fetch with a two-entry fall-through instruction queue
motivation:
The champion achieves 114.45 iterations/s at 48.089 MHz and 4,201,740
measured CoreMark cycles. Structural divider retiming was successful,
while the later validity/payload split reached only 49.295 MHz before
prediction was added. The champion again reports a divider critical
path. A further front-end timing cleanup therefore has an uncertain
clock benefit. There is also a structural throughput bottleneck: the
current fetch PC stops on every load-use interlock, data-memory stall,
and pending divide. Instructions available during those cycles are
discarded, and a later independent instruction-bus stall cannot be
served from a buffer. The approximately 22 percent stalls on each bus
make overlapping these waits a promising source of useful throughput.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion achieves 114.45 iterations/s at 48.089 MHz and 4,201,740
measured CoreMark cycles. Structural divider retiming was successful,
while the later validity/payload split reached only 49.295 MHz before
prediction was added. The champion again reports a divider critical
path. A further front-end timing cleanup therefore has an uncertain
clock benefit. There is also a structural throughput bottleneck: the
current fetch PC stops on every load-use interlock, data-memory stall,
and pending divide. Instructions available during those cycles are
discarded, and a later independent instruction-bus stall cannot be
served from a buffer. The approximately 22 percent stalls on each bus
make overlapping these waits a promising source of useful throughput.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the lockstep combinational fetch/decode connection with one
two-entry, fall-through instruction queue. Decouple instruction fetch
acceptance from ID/EX acceptance so fetch can run ahead while decode
waits for a load, data memory, or the existing divider. Buffered tokens
can subsequently feed decode even when io_imemReady is low. Keep the
empty-queue combinational bypass so an available instruction can still
enter ID/EX on its first fetch edge, including immediately after a
redirect. This is a single structural front-end buffering change;
retain the current predictor, arithmetic units, issue/retirement width,
execution latency, and branch resolution stage.

Store complete fetch tokens: PC, raw instruction, and the actual
predicted_taken decision. Use two small flop entries with an occupancy
count and explicit enqueue/dequeue logic. When occupied, present only
the oldest stored token to decode. When empty, present the current raw
bus token directly, valid only when io_imemReady is high. Compute the
queue-head data independently of redirect/flush so a correction never
masks instruction bits before decoder, register-file addresses, or
dependency comparison. Kill and acceptance controls determine whether
this data has architectural significance.

Use conservative capacity control: request/capture a new fetch only
when occupancy is below two and io_imemReady is high, except reset or
an EX correction. Do not feed same-cycle decode readiness into full-
queue fetch readiness; a full queue may dequeue without replacing its
last slot that edge. At occupancy zero, an accepted bus token consumed
by decode bypasses storage; otherwise enqueue it. At occupancy one,
concurrent dequeue/enqueue replaces the head with the new bus token.
At occupancy two, permit dequeue and hold the fetch PC. A downstream
hold never overwrites the queue head. Advance the fetch PC exactly once
per accepted bus token, whether enqueued or directly bypassed, never
merely because an old queued token was decoded. Keep the request
address stable while no new token is accepted, apart from correction.

Drive the existing direct-branch/JAL prediction from the raw bus
instruction and fetch PC, not the queue head. On bus-token acceptance,
use exactly the same pre-edge prediction to update the fetch PC and
capture that token's predicted_taken bit. Remove downstream load-use,
dmem, and divider holds from prediction eligibility when the queue has
space. Once stored, the prediction bit remains unchanged through
stalls and counter training. Preserve the current full-width target
calculation, address/alignment eligibility, counter initialization,
once-per-advancing-branch training, and direction-only EX correction.
Prediction changes when instructions are fetched, not their semantics.

A permitted EX correction wins over all queue operations: invalidate
both entries, cancel any same-edge enqueue/dequeue, set the fetch PC
to redirect_target even if imemReady is low, and flush the younger

title: Prediction-driven issue of load-dependent branches with late verification
motivation:
The champion already has immediate-derived direct targets and a 64-entry
bimodal direction predictor, scoring 114.45 iterations/s at 48.089 MHz
and 4,201,740 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md favors retaining
its direction-only recovery and the retimed divider. The previous tagged
next-PC predictor saved only about 0.4% more cycles than direct prediction.
A fresh architectural trace of the unchanged canonical 2K/10-iteration
binary reproduced all five CRCs and the validation message. Inside the
markers it contains 529,588 conditional branches and 135,320 immediately
load-dependent branches. Sequential trace replay of the current bimodal
policy estimates 51,857 total direction misses, only 7,199 on these
load-dependent branches. A 64x8 local-history/256x2 pattern predictor saved
just 4,109 direction misses, too little to justify its extra lookup logic.
The stronger opportunity is using the existing approximately 94.7% accurate
predictions on load-dependent branches to avoid their mandatory issue
bubble. These trace counts are analytical evidence, not a cycle simulation
or a measurement of the proposed circuit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Let a legal conditional branch immediately following a load enter ID/EX
without the normal load-use bubble, follow its existing predicted successor,
and defer that branch's condition verification to MEM. This is one predictor
mechanism: using control speculation to hide load-to-branch latency while
verifying every outcome before younger instructions can affect memory or
retire. Keep the existing 64-entry bimodal direction policy, direct target
calculation and range/alignment eligibility checks. Do not add a larger
direction table, BTB, return stack, load-value predictor or arithmetic changes.

Exempt only raw, positively decoded legal BRANCH encodings from the interlock
when the valid load currently in EX has a nonzero destination matching rs1
or rs2. The load must actually advance and the branch must actually be
accepted before any deferred state is captured. All other load consumers
retain the existing interlock. Alongside the accepted branch, latch a
deferred-verification bit and two source-needs-load bits. Keep the existing
predicted_taken bit; direct targets still derive from this branch's own
instruction and PC. Imem unready, older dmem holds, divider waits, reset and
flush retain their normal acceptance priorities. No prediction is evidence
that an unready load has completed.

In EX, a deferred branch does not resolve, redirect, train, or apply a
conditional-target misalignment trap using unavailable operands. Carry its
branch operation, target, prediction, pending-source mask and forwarded
operands into EX/MEM. Ordinary branches and JAL/JALR retain EX resolution.
For a pending source, explicitly reject the older load's EX/MEM address
as a forwarded value. Capture a fallback operand using forwarding from
older completed writers or the ID/EX source value, excluding that pending
load. In particular, retain the older MEM/WB writer's value when applicable.
This fallback is needed if the load eventually traps and suppresses its
register write; do not substitute a faulting load's data or effective address.

In MEM, the preceding load has reached MEM/WB. For each pending source,
use its completed, sign/zero-extended WB value only when the WB instruction
actually writes the matching nonzero register; otherwise use the captured
fallback. Resolve the branch condition and actual next PC from these exact
operands, applying the existing taken-target misalignment trap policy.
Patch the branch's MEM/WB RVFI source values, actual pc_next and trap fields
accordingly. Never retire a predicted outcome or an unresolved branch.
Older dmem stalls hold the branch in EX until the load is accepted, preserving
the current retained MEM/WB forwarding behavior. Once the branch occupies
MEM it has no data-memory request and cannot wait on io_dmemReady.

A correct prediction lets the younger EX instruction advance normally.
On a late mismatch, redirect to the actual branch target or PC+4, flush
fetch/ID, and kill the younger instruction currently in EX by inserting a
zero-control invalid EX/MEM entry. The late correction is older and must
override any simultaneous younger EX correction, branch feedback, load-use
indication or execute_wait. Gate divider start and result acceptance for
the squashed younger instruction and ensure its execute_wait cannot block
the squash. Because the deferred branch is immediately ahead of that
instruction, a younger division cannot have launched before this check;
prevent its same-edge launch rather than letting wrong-path divider state
persist. Do not kill the resolving branch's MEM/WB entry or its older load.
Younger stores have not reached MEM and must never issue a memory request.
Correction still overrides an unready instruction bus.

Keep a single predictor write port by moving all conditional-branch training
to MEM advancement. Ordinary branches carry their EX-computed outcome;
deferred branches supply the outcome verified in MEM. Train the current
counter at the branch's own PC exactly once only for a valid, legal,
non-faulting branch. This avoids two simultaneous table writes when a late
branch is followed by an ordinary branch. Do not train killed younger work,
held entries, JAL/JALR or bubbles. Preserve pre-edge lookup/update semantics;
accept that regular-branch training is one cycle later, without a bypass
from MEM comparison to fetch prediction. Keep predictor state nonarchitectural.

The forecast is a low-confidence 5% fitness gain, aiming for approximately
2.5% fewer cycles together with approximately 2.5% higher median Fmax.
The trace suggests at most about 128,121 net saved issue slots before bus
overlap and predictor-update timing, since a late miss costs an extra
younger slot. It does not establish a 5% cycle gain. A measured result near
4,100,000 cycles would need median Fmax above 49.083 MHz to exceed 119.7147
iterations/s, the champion plus 4.6%. This clock increase is unproven; late
correction fanout, additional metadata and placement could instead lower
Fmax. Keep the new comparator separate from arithmetic and existing direct
branch recovery, and avoid adding wide predicted-PC comparison or a new
load-data-to-EX combinational forwarding path. Evaluate the actual product
with vendor timing rather than claiming acceptance from predictor accuracy.

Preserve nret=1, every core port, decoder legality, full architectural
address arithmetic, trap/link semantics, contiguous RVFI retirement order,
and the eight-service-edge divider schedule. Run existing unit, formal and
stalled cosimulation gates and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks.
Specifically retain the unchanged formal liveness window: a late correction
immediately followed by DIV/REM must still make progress without relaxing
a checker, depth or evaluation contract.

title: Two-level radix-8/radix-4 lookahead for each divider recurrence
motivation:
The champion scores 120.53 iterations/s at 48.333 MHz and 4,010,178
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path remains inside
div_unit, crossing five dependent restoring subtract/select steps.
The micro_opt history shows that radix-4/radix-4/radix-2 grouping in
hyp-20261003-001-r4s0 raised median Fmax from 48.089 to 50.635 MHz
without changing cycles. It lost the round to the fetch-queue candidate,
whose queue is now present but whose divider still uses radix-2 steps.
There is evidence for arithmetic lookahead, but merely reproducing
50.635 MHz leaves little margin over today's 4.6 percent threshold.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real divider's five serial radix-2 restoring steps
per STEP0..STEP5 cycle with one radix-8 step followed by one radix-4
step. Each group still consumes exactly five dividend bits. This
reduces the dependent trial-subtraction/selection boundaries from
five to two, going beyond the previous candidate's three boundaries.
Preserve the two narrow launch steps, six recurrence edges, corrected
EX/MEM acceptance on service edge eight, and all external handshakes.
This is one local combinational arithmetic optimization, with no new
pipeline stage, execution policy, prediction or memory mechanism.

At launch retain the current unsigned magnitude conversion and the
quotient/remainder initialization after two dividend bits. Register
35-bit unsigned 3D, 5D and 7D from the NEW divisor magnitude D, using
independent widened expressions D+(D<<1), D+(D<<2), and (D<<3)-D.
Zero-extend D to 35 bits before shifting or adding. Derive D, 2D and
4D from the registered divisor by wiring, and 6D by shifting registered
3D. Do not cascade the odd-multiple adders, use the previous operation's
divisor, infer a general multiplier, or calculate multiples along the
recurrence path. Keep all multiples stable until completion.

The radix-8 step forms the 35-bit unsigned trial T={R,Q[31:29]}.
Compute seven 36-bit differences {1'b0,T}-{1'b0,kD} in parallel,
for k=1..7. Define fit[k] as the inverse of each difference's top
borrow bit. Decode mutually exclusive digit enables: e[0]=!fit[1],
e[k]=fit[k]&&!fit[k+1] for k=1..6, and e[7]=fit[7]. The selected
digit is the largest fitting multiple. Select T[31:0] for digit 0
or the selected difference's low 32 bits otherwise, and shift Q
left three bits, appending the three-bit digit. Use a balanced
masked-OR mux for remainder and digit selection, not seven cascaded
wide priority muxes. Monotonic fit predicates make the enables
exclusive, including D=0 where digit 7 wins.

Feed that result into one radix-4 step: form the 34-bit unsigned
trial {R,Q[31:30]}, perform three parallel 35-bit trial subtractions
by exact 34-bit D, 2D and 3D, and select digit 0..3 with the same
exclusive-enable construction. Register its remainder and quotient
in the existing registers. For nonzero D, R<D at each boundary
proves every selected remainder fits 32 bits even when unselected
trials and multiples do not. Never truncate a trial or a multiple
before computing borrow. Six groups consume the remaining 30 bits.

Preserve original operands, modular signed magnitudes, quotient and
remainder sign correction, INT_MIN/-1 behavior and divide-by-zero
results. Keep the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas and control
schedule, compiling the new arithmetic out under ALTOPS. Retain
DONE result stability under arbitrary backpressure, reset cancellation,
captured forwarded operands and once-only acceptance. Preserve the
nret=1 IO/RVFI contract, existing correctness checks and formal depths.

Validate the real sequential divider against exact integer RV32M
references and the current radix-2 recurrence at every five-bit
register boundary. Exercise all radix-8 digits and threshold values
near every kD, including large divisors whose multiples exceed 32
bits. Run existing unit, formal and cosimulation gates and canonical
stalled CoreMark CRC/marker checks unchanged. With identical inputs
and stalls, CoreMark bracket cycles should remain 4,010,178.

Forecast a 7 percent fitness gain from Fmax. Acceptance
requires fitness above 126.07438 iterations/s, approximately 50.56
MHz at unchanged cycles. Judge the median vendor Gowin result, not
nominal arithmetic depth. Seven parallel first-step trials increase
area and routing; launch magnitude-to-multiple adders and the known
register-file/ALU path may become the limit. These are material risks
to the forecast, and implementation details can affect placement.

An isolated scratch RTL prototype of this exact radix-8/radix-4
replacement was measured with the unchanged core_bench_si wrapper,
stall generator, constraints and vendor Gowin flow. Placement options
0/1/2 achieved 46.691/51.708/51.708 MHz, giving a 51.708 MHz median;
the reported option-0 worst path moved from the divider to the
register-file/ALU path. Option-0 area was 3,769 LUT4 and 987 FF,
with six DSPs, six BSRAMs and eight LUT-RAMs. The unchanged CoreMark
evaluator accepted the prototype's canonical CRCs, validation text,
completion, in-bounds accesses and timing markers, reporting exactly
4,010,178 bracket cycles for ten iterations with both stall streams.
Their product is 128.94191 iterations/s, 6.9791 percent above 120.53.
This is prototype evidence, not an official tournament acceptance.

All three existing divider cocotb tests passed in both real and
ALTOPS builds, including exact service latency, delayed acceptance
and reset cancellation. Selftest and all three random RVFI programs
passed the unchanged ISS comparison both with and without bus stalls.
A width-accurate numerical model additionally matched 69,572 RV32M
results over 17,393 operand pairs and the original radix-2 recurrence
at 208,716 group boundaries; it exercised all radix-8 and radix-4
digits and checked nonzero-divisor remainder bounds. Formal proofs
were not rerun for this proposal and remain required implementation
gates. Only the hypothesis file is delivered; the prototype and its
build artifacts were kept outside the repository RTL.

title: Balance the M-extension execution pipeline with registered partial arithmetic
motivation:
The champion scores 120.53 iterations/s at 48.333 MHz and 4,010,178
bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md and the structural r1s1/r2s1
experiments show that registering long arithmetic paths is effective.
Current timing alternates between two limits: five serial restoring
steps in div_unit and the register-file/forwarding/ALU path that still
contains combinational multiplication. The r4s0 divider-only change
reached 50.635 MHz with its worst path moving to the ALU. Removing both
long M-operation cones through balanced execution registers offers more
clock headroom than changing only the current worst path.

An architectural replay of the unchanged canonical 2K, ten-iteration,
-O3 binary counted 93,960 MUL instructions and no DIV/REM instructions
between markers, and reproduced the five expected CRC values. Thus one
additional service cycle per multiply has a nominal cost of only 2.34
percent of current cycles. This is trace evidence, not candidate timing
or a stalled pipeline simulation.

experiments show that registering long arithmetic paths is effective.
Current timing alternates between two limits: five serial restoring
steps in div_unit and the register-file/forwarding/ALU path that still
contains combinational multiplication. The r4s0 divider-only change
reached 50.635 MHz with its worst path moving to the ALU. Removing both
long M-operation cones through balanced execution registers offers more
clock headroom than changing only the current worst path.

An architectural replay of the unchanged canonical 2K, ten-iteration,
-O3 binary counted 93,960 MUL instructions and no DIV/REM instructions
between markers, and reproduced the five expected CRC values. Thus one
additional service cycle per multiply has a nominal cost of only 2.34
percent of current cycles. This is trace evidence, not candidate timing
or a stalled pipeline simulation.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition M-extension execution around registered partial arithmetic.
Give multiplication a two-service-edge execution path and rebalance
division within its existing eight-service-edge path. Ordinary integer
instructions retain their current single-cycle EX path. This is one
structural register-placement and scheduling change to the M backend:
both existing arithmetic bottlenecks must be bounded for a substantial
clock gain. Keep single issue, the current stage topology, fetch queue,
predictor, load-use discipline and retirement width.

Remove all real multiplication logic statically from the core's fast ALU,
just as combinational division is already excluded. Keep default ALU
parameters compatible with standalone tests. Add a blocking mul_unit
with start, busy, result_valid, result and result_accept. At the first
service edge, capture four 16-bit-limb partial products directly from
the forwarded operands, plus operation/sign-selection and RVFI source
snapshots. At the second service edge, EX/MEM accepts their recombined
result. There must be a real register boundary between limb products
and recombination; registering the completed original 32x32 product
leaves its long forwarding-to-multiply path intact.

One exact decomposition uses signed 17-bit limbs. Low limbs are
{1'b0,a[15:0]} and {1'b0,b[15:0]}. High limbs are
{signed_a && a[31],a[31:16]} and {signed_b && b[31],b[31:16]}.
Set signed_a for MULH/MULHSU and signed_b for MULH; MUL/MULHU can
use unsigned limbs. Register the four signed 34-bit products LL, LH,
HL and HH, which should fit the FPGA's small DSP multipliers. Recombine
P = LL + (LH << 16) + (HL << 16) + (HH << 32), modulo 2^64, with
explicit sign extension to 64 bits before shifting. Select P[31:0]
for MUL and P[63:32] for the three high-product operations. Avoid a
serial chain of three wide carry-propagating additions: compress the
four aligned terms with two carry-save layers and one final carry
propagation, exploiting constant low/high bits. No new sign-correction
cycle is needed. Preserve full architectural operand widths and do not
specialize multiplication to CoreMark operand values.

result_valid becomes true after the partial-product capture edge; the
result is then a combinational function solely of frozen partials and
captured operation. EX/MEM accepts it on service edge two if not held.
Keep partials, operation and captured source values stable for arbitrarily
delayed acceptance. Reset cancels pending work; busy starts cannot
overwrite it. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, return the exact existing four
substitute formulas over captured original operands through the same
two-edge handshake and wait behavior. Test the sequential unit directly;
the legacy combinational ALU tests alone cannot validate this new path.

Repartition div_unit's existing 2 + 6*5 restoring steps into
6 + 6*4 + 2 steps, without changing its eight service edges. Launch
captures forwarded operands, magnitudes and signs while consuming the
first six dividend bits. Implement those six prologue trials at their
actual widths of one through six bits: subtract only the low W divisor
bits using W+1 bits and accept only when the borrow is clear and all
divisor bits above W-1 are zero. Share upper-bit-zero reductions. This
avoids putting six full-width subtractors after magnitude conversion.
Then each of the six existing recurrence edges consumes four bits with
the existing unsigned 33-bit subtract/borrow semantics, registering the
quotient/remainder after each group. Those edges finish 30 total bits.

In DONE, perform the final two restoring trials combinationally from
the frozen registered partial state, then apply quotient/remainder
selection, sign correction and architectural exceptional results. The
existing EX/MEM acceptance edge captures the fully completed result on
service edge eight. result_valid still first asserts after edge seven;
it denotes the final two-step-plus-correction result, not the unfinished
30-bit state. This balances launch, recurrence and acceptance logic while
reducing the repeated full-width chain from five steps to four. Do not
insert PREP, SIGN or handoff states. Preserve division by zero, INT_MIN/-1,
signed truncation/remainder semantics, exact ALTOPS formulas and the same
control schedule for real and ALTOPS builds. DONE sources remain frozen
under backpressure, so the combinational final result remains stable.

Generalize EX's existing blocking-divider control to either M unit.
A valid legal instruction owns ID/EX until its selected result is accepted.
Capture post-forward source values at launch before older producers drain.
During M wait, allow older MEM/WB instructions to drain, inserting a
zero-control EX/MEM bubble unless an older dmem hold requires retaining
EX/MEM. Dmem backpressure retains highest priority. Forward an accepted
M result through the normal EX/MEM and MEM/WB paths; never advertise an
unfinished product as a register value. Preserve retained WB forwarding
across holds, once-only stores/retirement, redirect and predictor-training
qualification, reset cancellation, traps and contiguous RVFI order.
The existing fetch queue may continue filling during execution waits.
Preserve nret=1 and every top-level memory/RVFI port.

Forecast a 12 percent fitness improvement with medium confidence. A
simple non-overlap estimate adds 93,960 multiply cycles, giving 4,104,138
cycles. At that count, approximately 55.40 MHz would deliver the forecast;
acceptance above 126.07438 iterations/s requires more than 51.743 MHz.
Actual stalled cycles must be measured: fetch overlap and changed bus
phases can alter this estimate. Principal risks are DSP inference, the
wider launch prologue, the two-step divider completion plus negation,
multiplier recombination, and a new non-M critical path. Check vendor
timing for the mapped partial-product registers and all three divider
register boundaries; arithmetic step counts alone do not establish Fmax.

A Python model checked the signed-limb/carry-save product decomposition
on 49,083 signedness/product cases and the 6+6*4+2 divider decomposition
on 65,444 RV32M quotient/remainder cases, including boundary values and

candidate RTL correctness, handshakes and Gowin timing are unmeasured.
Run all existing unit, unchanged formal and stalled cosimulation gates,
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks, and vendor median Fmax. Keep
every existing divider latency and branch-followed-by-division progress
assertion, including the nine-cycle ready-bus retirement-gap bound and
unchanged formal liveness depth. Exercise mixed dependent M instructions
so the new multiplier cannot create an extra divider launch bubble.

title: Load-to-branch speculation with sidecar checks and validity-only recovery
motivation:
The champion scores 120.53 iter/s at 48.333 MHz and 4,010,178 timed
CoreMark cycles. The prior predictor attempt hyp-20261003-003-r4s2
eliminated load-to-branch interlocks through delayed verification,
reducing its parent's cycles from 4,201,740 to 4,070,414, but its
47.211 MHz clock did not beat the winning fetch queue. Its worst path
crossed ID, the EX ALU and EX control. A fresh architectural trace of
the canonical binary confirms 135,320 immediate load-dependent branches
among 529,588 conditional branches. A marker-local sequential replay of
the current 64-counter policy misses 7,198 of those dependent branches;
only 13,735 returns leave little headroom for a return predictor. The
complete program's UART contains all five canonical CRCs and the required
validation message. Preserve the champion's fetch queue and try a narrow
verification sidecar with validity-only recovery. Its late correction
must not mux ordinary ID/EX or EX/MEM payloads. The trace and predictor
replay do not model stalls, speculative fetches or delayed training.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Use the existing bimodal prediction to issue an immediately load-dependent
conditional branch without its load-use bubble. Defer only the condition
check to a small branch verification sidecar parallel to MEM. This is
one predictor mechanism: speculation across load-to-branch latency with
mandatory verification and squash before younger architectural effects.
Preserve the existing prediction table, direct targets, fetch FIFO,
divider schedule, arithmetic and nret=1 contract.

Admit only a valid positively decoded legal BRANCH whose rs1 and/or rs2
matches the advancing valid load's nonzero destination. Capture a pending
source mask with that branch on actual ID acceptance. All other consumers
retain the existing interlock. Older data-memory or divider holds continue
to hold the branch normally; instruction-bus stalls cannot create an
accepted instruction. Preserve the exact fetched predicted_taken bit.

In EX, a marked branch neither verifies its condition nor trains or
redirects. Carry its PC, direct target, comparison operation, prediction,
pending mask and correct fallback operands to a narrow sidecar registered
on the branch's EX advancement. Reuse existing EX/MEM PC, target and
source fields instead of duplicating wide architectural payloads; the
additional logical sidecar fields are the deferred flag, source mask,
prediction and comparison operation. Reusing source/target fields still
makes formerly RVFI-only registers and routes part of the timed circuit;
account for that area and routing cost. Exclude the preceding load's effective
address from pending-source forwarding. Retain the freshest older value
for each pending source, including WB forwarding, in case the load traps
and does not write. Ordinary branches and jumps still resolve in EX.

When the sidecar is valid, the older load is in MEM/WB. Select its actual
sign/zero-extended value only if that load writes the matching nonzero
register; otherwise use the captured fallback. Resolve the condition and
taken-target misalignment with full architectural operands. Patch only
this branch's retiring RVFI source values, actual pc_next and trap fields.
Train the direction table exactly once from the verified outcome.

A verification mismatch produces an older correction that wins over
younger EX corrections, training, load-use and execute_wait. Kill the
younger instruction entering EX/MEM, flush ID/EX and the fetch FIFO, and
redirect to the verified target or PC+4 even if imemReady is low. The
resolving branch and its older load still retire normally. Prevent a
younger divider launch on this edge. No younger instruction can already
have launched division because the unresolved branch was ahead of it in
EX; do not add divider cancellation states or latency.

The essential change from r4s2 is physical separation of correction from
ordinary pipeline payloads in both ID/EX and EX/MEM. Give each a separate
valid and side-effect-control update. A late kill clears validity and memory/
register-write controls, while ordinary PC, ALU-result, store-data and
metadata payload flops capture or retain their normal data independent
of that kill. Never add a late-correction mux or enable to the wide ALU
result or divider-result data cone. Invalid entries must be prevented
from issuing memory requests, forwarding writes, training or retiring;
retaining don't-care payloads must not retain live controls. Keep the
sidecar comparator separate from the ordinary ALU and operand muxes.
Gate ordinary EX redirect/training and divider launch with the older
correction without gating the raw instruction or decode data path.
Apply the same validity/control-only recovery to ordinary EX corrections
and ID load-use bubbles so neither correction source restores the wide
flush mux. Payload enables depend only on the pre-existing older hold
conditions, not on correction; clearing validity makes any concurrently
captured payload harmless. Keep WB's existing forwarding retention during
dmem holds: its cleared retirement-valid bit must not hide a previously
completed load value still needed by a held instruction. The new invalid
forwarding prohibition applies to killed/bubble EX/MEM entries, not to
that deliberately retained MEM/WB bypass state.

Serialize predictor training by registering ordinary EX branch feedback
into the MEM boundary and selecting the sidecar's verified feedback for
deferred branches. There is at most one training event per advancing
MEM instruction. Preserve pre-edge counter lookup and current-counter
saturation semantics; never train a held, killed, invalid or trapping
branch. Clear sidecar validity on reset and hold it consistently with
its associated EX/MEM instruction. Keep all pending metadata associated
with its instruction across arbitrarily long memory stalls.

Forecast a low-confidence 6% fitness improvement, with approximately
3% fewer cycles plus modest clock recovery from the isolated squash
controls. Neither component is measured on this champion. A cycle
saving alone may miss the 4.6% acceptance threshold, and the new feedback
control could instead lower Fmax. Acceptance requires measured median
Gowin Fmax in Hz times 10/Cnew above 126.07438 iter/s. At 3% fewer
cycles this needs more than 49.0414 MHz, versus the champion's 48.333
MHz. The earlier validity-separation attempt r3s1 reached 49.295 MHz,
supporting plausibility but not predicting timing for this new circuit.
The architectural trace gives roughly 128,122 saved issue slots minus
overlap and delayed-training effects, after charging an extra slot for
each late mismatch; it does not establish a 6% cycle saving. Run unchanged unit,
formal, stalled cosimulation, CoreMark CRC/UART and marker checks;
preserve all IO, decoder, trap, ordering and liveness invariants.
