title: Isolate memory address generation to unlock fixed-latency divider lookahead
motivation:
The champion scores 120.53 iterations/s at 48.333 MHz and 4,010,178
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Previous divider lookahead exposed the
register-file/ALU path as the next clock limit: r5s0 reached only
49.850 MHz and gained 3.14 percent. EX/MEM alu_result currently serves
both arithmetic forwarding/writeback and the data-memory address.
Vendor timing consequently includes multiplication on a path ending
at a data-memory BSRAM address input, although MUL never requests
memory. Separating that address cone should remove this ceiling on
the fixed-latency divider optimization.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 120.53 iterations/s at 48.333 MHz and 4,010,178
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Previous divider lookahead exposed the
register-file/ALU path as the next clock limit: r5s0 reached only
49.850 MHz and gained 3.14 percent. EX/MEM alu_result currently serves
both arithmetic forwarding/writeback and the data-memory address.
Vendor timing consequently includes multiplication on a path ending
at a data-memory BSRAM address input, although MUL never requests
memory. Separating that address cone should remove this ceiling on
the fixed-latency divider optimization.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple load/store effective-address generation from the general
ALU result, enabling radix-8/radix-4 divider lookahead to improve Fmax
without immediately hitting the ALU-to-memory-address timing limit.
This is one coordinated micro-optimization of combinational arithmetic
paths and their endpoint mapping. Keep every pipeline stage, service
schedule, predictor, queue, forwarding priority and bus handshake.

Add a 32-bit effective_addr field to the existing EX/MEM bundle.
On the same advancing edge as the normal EX payload, capture the
full-width sum of forwarded rs1 and in.imm. Use a dedicated addition
expression independent of ALU opcode, operand-B selection, arithmetic
result selection and jump-link selection. Apply the existing EX/MEM
reset, bubble and dmem-hold rules. No extra stage or cycle is added.
Computing this sum for non-memory instructions is harmless because
their memory enables remain deasserted.

Use effective_addr in MEM for the bus address, byte offsets, store
masks, load extraction, alignment checks and RVFI aligned memory
address. Continue copying in.alu_result into MEM/WB; retain that
original result for register writeback and EX/MEM forwarding. Never
substitute an effective address for an arithmetic register value.
Preserve full 32-bit addition without address-range assumptions or
truncation, misaligned-access traps and suppression of memory enables.

Pair this address-cone isolation with the prior fixed-latency
radix-8/radix-4 divider recurrence. Retain the two narrow launch
steps and all six recurrence states. On launch, capture unsigned
35-bit 3D, 5D and 7D from the NEW divisor magnitude using independent
widened expressions D+(D<<1), D+(D<<2), and (D<<3)-D. Derive 2D,
4D and 6D by wiring/shifts. Widen before shifting, avoid general
constant multipliers, and never initialize from the old divisor.

Each recurrence first forms the 35-bit trial T={R,Q[31:29]}.
Subtract kD for k=1..7 in parallel using explicit 36-bit unsigned
differences. With fit[k] equal to inverse borrow, form exclusive
enables e0=!fit[1], ek=fit[k]&&!fit[k+1] for k=1..6, e7=fit[7].
Select T[31:0] for digit zero or the selected difference[31:0]
through a masked-OR mux, then append the three-bit quotient digit.
Follow with a radix-4 step using a 34-bit trial, exact 34-bit
D/2D/3D and 35-bit differences, selecting two more quotient bits
identically. Register the final quotient/remainder in the existing
registers. Six groups still consume 30 bits after the two-bit
prologue, preserving corrected acceptance on service edge eight.

For nonzero divisors, R<D ensures selected remainders fit 32 bits.
Preserve original operands, signed magnitudes, quotient/remainder
sign correction, zero-divisor overrides and INT_MIN/-1 results.
Keep DONE stable under arbitrary backpressure, reset cancellation
and once-only acceptance. Keep exact ALTOPS formulas and the same
handshake schedule, compiling real arithmetic out under ALTOPS.
Preserve the multiplier, decoder, nret=1 IO, RVFI order, formal
depths and all existing correctness checks.

Validate the real sequential divider, every load/store width and
alignment, addresses dependent on forwarded arithmetic results,
held requests and alternating M/ALU/memory traffic. Run unchanged
formal and RVFI cosimulation gates and canonical stalled CoreMark
CRC/UART/marker checks. Expected cycles remain 4,010,178. Acceptance
requires fitness above 126.07438 iterations/s, about 50.56 MHz at
that count. Additional address flops, trial-subtractor routing and
the remaining arithmetic-to-writeback path are physical risks.

An isolated scratch RTL prototype of these exact changes used the
unchanged vendor flow, wrapper, constraints and stall generator.
Placement options 0/1/2 achieved 50.412/51.124/51.124 MHz, median
51.124 MHz. Option-0 area was 3,807 LUT4 and 1,019 FF, six DSPs,
six BSRAMs and eight LUT-RAMs. Its worst reported path ends at
EX/MEM alu_result instead of the memory BSRAM address. The unchanged
CoreMark evaluator accepted canonical CRCs, UART validation text,
completion, in-bounds execution and timing markers, reporting exactly
4,010,178 cycles for ten iterations with both bus stall streams.
Their product is 127.48561 iterations/s, a 5.77086 percent gain.

The final prototype passed all 27 existing pipeline cocotb tests
in both real and ALTOPS builds. Selftest and all three random
programs passed full RVFI comparison against the unchanged ISS
with both instruction and data bus stalls. The same divider
datapath separately passed its three existing unit tests in both
real and ALTOPS builds, including exact latency, held results and
reset cancellation. Formal proofs were not rerun for this proposal
and remain required implementation gates. This is prototype evidence,
not official tournament acceptance; the margin above the 4.6 percent
threshold is modest. Implementation must rerun timing and correctness
gates. Only this hypothesis file is delivered; prototype files remain
outside repository RTL.

and reset behavior. Preserve arithmetic results and forwarding.

extraction and RVFI aligned memory address. Propagate the
original alu_result for register writeback and retain memory
enable gating, trap behavior and held WB forwarding payloads.

parallel-trial radix-8 then radix-4 selection, using registered

title: Register M-extension partial results while keeping divider launch shallow
motivation:
The champion scores 120.53 iterations/s at 48.333 MHz and 4,010,178
CoreMark bracket cycles. Prior structural attempts successfully isolated
division, but timing now alternates between its five-step recurrence
and the register-file/ALU path. The r5s0 divider-only experiment reached
49.850 MHz with the worst path in the ALU and unchanged cycles. The
r5s1 attempt to pipeline both M datapaths instead fell to 37.905 MHz:
its worst path ran from a forwarding selector into divider launch,
where signed magnitude conversion was followed by six restoring trials.
This suggests that arithmetic register placement must preserve a shallow
launch boundary as well as shorten the repeated recurrence. The r5s1
CoreMark cycle increase was only 27,360 cycles, so multiplier latency
was much less damaging than the newly lengthened divider launch path.
A fresh champion Gowin placement-option-0 run reproduced 49.099 MHz:
its divider recurrence and register-file-to-multiplier paths arrived
at 25.661 and 25.642 ns respectively. The latter actually traverses
the multiplier DSP, confirming that both arithmetic cones need work.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rebuild the M-extension backend around registered partial results,
with a two-service-edge multiplier and the existing eight-service-edge
divider. This is one structural execution-path hypothesis: bound all
three boundaries (operand launch, recurrence, completion) instead of
moving arithmetic work onto the already deep forwarding path.
Ordinary integer execution, the fetch queue, predictor and nret=1
remain as in the champion.

Remove real multiplication statically from the core's combinational
ALU and instantiate a blocking multiplier. On service edge one capture
four signed 17-by-17 limb products, operation flags and original forwarded
operands. Low limbs are zero-extended 16-bit values; high limbs are
sign-extended only when that operand is signed for MULH or MULHSU.
Specifically, sign-extend a's high limb for MULH/MULHSU and b's high
limb only for MULH; MUL and MULHU use unsigned limbs for both operands.
On edge two EX/MEM accepts the recombined low or high result. Sign-extend
the 34-bit products before aligning them at bit offsets 0, 16, 16 and
32; combine with carry-save compression and one final carry propagation.
Keep the standalone ALU defaults and exact real RV32M/ALTOPS semantics.
A busy multiplier must retain partials and operand snapshots until its
result is accepted, including arbitrary downstream backpressure.

For division, retain the champion's two narrow quotient trials at
launch, followed by six five-bit recurrence edges and corrected
acceptance on edge eight. Do not move any additional quotient trials
onto launch or completion. Inside each five-bit recurrence, replace
serial bit-by-bit restoring dependencies with two combinational trial
groups: one radix-8 group followed by one radix-4 group. This takes the
divider-only r5s0 mechanism into a backend whose multiplier is now
registered, rather than repeating r5s1's six-bit launch prologue.

In parallel with the two narrow launch trials, register the unsigned
35-bit odd multiples 3D, 5D and 7D from the new magnitude divisor D,
using independent expressions D+(D<<1), D+(D<<2) and (D<<3)-D.
Widen D before these shifts; do not cascade odd-multiple adders.
During recurrence derive D, 2D, 4D and 6D by wiring shifts of the
registered divisor or registered 3D. No multiple-generation adder
belongs in a recurrence's subtraction/selection chain. The extra
launch work consists of parallel magnitude-to-multiple additions,
not r5s1's six dependent quotient trials. For a radix-8 group form
T=(R<<3)|next_three_quotient_bits; subtract kD in parallel for k=1..7
and select the largest nonnegative candidate.
Update the quotient by three bits and feed the chosen remainder into
the radix-4 group's parallel trials for k=1..3 and next two bits.
Use 36-bit radix-8 differences and 35-bit radix-4 differences, explicit
unsigned extension and genuine borrow tests; do not truncate large
multiples. Decode mutually exclusive digit enables from monotonic
fits: e0=!fit1, ek=fitk&&!fit(k+1), and elast=fitlast. Select remainders
and quotient digits with balanced masked-OR trees, avoiding a cascade
of wide priority muxes. With D=0 the largest digit wins in each group;
the final architectural divide-by-zero override still applies.
The six recurrence edges still consume exactly 30 bits after launch's
two. All multiple registers are frozen during execution and DONE.
DONE performs only the existing result selection,
sign correction and divide-by-zero override. Preserve the original
exception results and the same real/ALTOPS control schedule.

Generalize execute_wait to the selected M unit. Capture RVFI source
operands once before older forwarding producers drain. During a wait,
hold ID/EX, allow older work to drain and clear consumed EX/MEM entries
to zero-control bubbles; an older dmem hold retains highest priority.
Accept each completed result once, use normal downstream forwarding,
preserve retained WB forwarding across stalls, and cancel pending work
on reset. Invalid or squashed instructions cannot launch an operation.
Preserve top-level IO, single-channel retirement, trap discipline and
all existing bounded-progress assertions and formal depths.

The prior measured 4,037,538 cycles would require over 50.904 MHz to
beat the champion by 4.6 percent; approximately 53.531 MHz would yield
the forecast. These are analytical thresholds; the scratch prototype
measurements below are separate from official tournament evaluation.

remaining integer paths are the main uncertainties. Validate complete
real arithmetic, ALTOPS routing and latency, unchanged formal/cosim and
canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks. Score median vendor
Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle, and inspect all M boundaries
to confirm launch has not become the new critical path.

used the unchanged single-channel FPGA wrapper, stall generator,
constraints and vendor flow. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured

993 FF, eight LUT-RAMs, six BSRAMs and two DSPs. The worst paths moved
to ordinary ALU/forwarding and control logic rather than divider launch
or multiplication. Stalled CoreMark completed in 4,037,538 bracketed
cycles for ten iterations; validate_coremark_uart accepted all five
canonical CRCs and validation text, with no out-of-bounds accesses.

title: Load-to-branch prediction with parallel validation and registered recovery
motivation:
The champion's 64-counter predictor and two-entry fetch queue deliver
120.53 iter/s at 48.333 MHz and 4,010,178 timed CoreMark cycles. The
r4s2 trace study found 135,320 immediately load-dependent branches out
of 529,588 conditional branches; improving direction history saved only
4,109 misses, and return prediction has little dynamic opportunity.
The r5s2 predictor instead removed load-to-branch issue bubbles, cutting
cycles to 3,909,350, but its 48.605 MHz median clock produced only a
3.15% fitness gain, below the 4.6% acceptance threshold. It verified
speculative branches in MEM from WB data, placing a load-value mux and
comparator before the late squash controls. Retiming that verification
beside the completing load offers a focused way to retain the measured
cycle benefit while shortening the predictor's recovery feedback.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict through immediately load-dependent conditional branches, but
validate the prediction in parallel with the older load's MEM access
and register the correction decision before applying it. This is one
branch-prediction mechanism with a retimed verification path. Preserve
the champion's 64-counter direction policy, direct-target formation,
two-entry fetch queue, divider schedule, ordinary ALU and nret=1 IO.

Exempt only positively decoded legal conditional branches from the
immediate load-use interlock. On actual ID acceptance record which
sources depend on the advancing valid load's nonzero destination and
retain the exact fetched predicted_taken bit. Other consumers retain
their interlocks. A memory or divider hold still prevents advancement;
unavailable fetches cannot create speculative instructions.

When this branch reaches EX, its producer load is in MEM. Expose the
already existing sign/zero-extended MEM load result and its effective
nontrapping write qualification to a dedicated branch comparator.
Select that result only for marked sources matching the valid older
load's destination. For a trapping/nonwriting load, select the freshest
architectural fallback, including older WB forwarding, never the load's
effective address. Unmarked operands use their normal forwarded values.
Compute the actual condition, target misalignment, actual successor and
mismatch against predicted_taken in parallel with the load completing.
On the branch's EX advance, register these verification results with
its EX/MEM token. Capture exact resolved operands for RVFI. The load
data may feed this narrow comparator and RVFI metadata, but must not
enter the ordinary ALU operand mux or combinational redirect/flush cone.

In particular, do not directly redirect from the new load-data compare
during EX. Issue continues using the prediction. In the following
cycle the branch in MEM presents a REGISTERED mismatch bit and a
registered actual successor. A match permits the younger EX instruction
to advance normally. A mismatch redirects fetch, empties its FIFO,
clears ID/EX validity and kills the younger instruction entering
EX/MEM before any younger store, register write or retirement. It also
suppresses a younger divider launch and younger EX redirect/training.
This older correction overrides load-use and a younger execute_wait;
it must work when imemReady is low. The resolving branch and older
load retire normally and exactly once. No new replay state or extra
pipeline stage is needed: verification occurs on the edge that moves
the producer load into WB and the predicted branch into MEM.

Separate squash validity/side-effect controls from wide payload writes
in ID/EX and EX/MEM. A correction clears validity and live memory and
register-write controls; ordinary ALU, operand, immediate, instruction
and store-data payloads retain normal capture/hold behavior independent
of correction. Preserve existing MEM/WB data retention for forwarding
during dmem stalls. No killed or bubble EX/MEM token may forward, train,
issue memory requests or retire. Older dmem stalls hold both the load
and its dependent branch; perform verification once when they advance,
never from an unaccepted bus value. Reset cancels pending verification.

Delay ordinary conditional-branch training by one stage to merge it
with the registered verified outcome at the MEM boundary. At most one
advancing branch trains per cycle. Use current-counter saturation,
pre-edge lookup, and the resolving PC index; never train invalid,
squashed, held or trapping branches. A younger branch killed by the
registered correction must not enqueue feedback. Ordinary nondeferred
branches and jumps still resolve in EX. Preserve all decoder legality,
target-range checks, architectural misalignment behavior, JAL/JALR
semantics, load widths, RVFI source values, order and liveness checks.

The forecast is an unmeasured 6% fitness gain with low confidence:
approximately the previous 2.5% cycle saving plus enough clock recovery
to pass the threshold. At 3,909,350 cycles the required median clock is
greater than 49.29 MHz to exceed 126.07438 iter/s. The reported r5s2
worst path was the register-file/ALU path, not an established sidecar
critical path; therefore shortening recovery is a physical hypothesis,
not evidence of a guaranteed clock gain. The new memory-to-comparator

formal, stalled cosimulation, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART and marker
checks, then judge median Gowin Fmax times iterations/cycle. Do not
change arithmetic, wrappers, tests' architectural assertions or eval.

title: Flatten EX operand and result muxes with exclusive source enables
motivation:
The champion scores 142.52 iterations/s at 57.541 MHz with 4,037,538
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its registered M-extension backend has moved
the timing limit onto the ordinary register-file/forwarding/ALU path.
Earlier micro_opt divider trials repeatedly hit this same limit; the
r6s0 address isolation changed the endpoint without removing operand
selection depth. A fresh unchanged Gowin option-0 run reproduced
53.956 MHz and the recorded 23.828 ns worst-path arrival. That path
crosses three rs1 forwarding LUTs followed by an alu_a selection LUT
before reaching the ALU. A nearly equal 23.824 ns path crosses rs2
forwarding, branch resolution and the ID/EX flush controls. Reducing
operand selection depth can therefore help both limiting cones, while
parallel final-result selection removes another serial mux boundary
on the arithmetic-to-memory path. Operand changes alone measured only
a 0.91 percent median Fmax gain; the proposed complete EX selection
rewrite measured a 7.53 percent fitness gain in the scratch prototype.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the serial data-selection network around the existing EX
arithmetic with mutually exclusive enables and parallel masked-OR
selection, at both its operand inputs and final result output.
This is one combinational mux-factoring micro-optimization. Preserve
all pipeline boundaries, instruction latencies,
issue and retirement width, branch policy, queue and bus handshakes.

For each source register compute independent EX/MEM and MEM/WB hits
using the existing write-control, nonzero destination and address
comparisons. Produce three one-hot enables: ex=ex_hit,
wb=wb_hit&&!ex_hit, and rf=!ex_hit&&!wb_hit. Preserve EX/MEM's younger
producer priority. A concrete vector layout is {wb, ex, rf}, replacing
the existing two-bit encoding with three source-enable bits throughout
forward_unit, core and ex_stage. Do not qualify the MEM/WB hit with
retirement valid: the existing retained WB payload must remain usable
during dmem holds after its instruction has retired. Keep x0 excluded
through the nonzero destination checks and existing register-file zero.

Form raw forwarded rs1/rs2 as ORs of the three masked data sources.
Separately form alu_a directly from four exclusive sources: PC when
is_auipc, otherwise the three sources gated by !is_auipc. Likewise
form alu_b directly from the immediate when alu_src, otherwise the
three rs2 sources gated by !alu_src. Do not feed the raw forwarded
value through another PC/immediate data mux. Gate the small source
enables before the wide data selection, and express balanced ORs of
masked words so the intended hardware has no wide priority cascade.
Raw forwarded values still feed branch comparisons, JALR, stores,
M-unit launch and captured RVFI operands; immediate and PC overrides
affect only ALU operands. Keep the existing alu.sv arithmetic and its
internal case selection, both M units and register-file mapping.

At the same EX/MEM acceptance edge, replace the nested is_div/is_mul/
is_jump result ternary with four independently masked words ORed
together. Use enables ed=is_div, em=!is_div&&is_mul,
ej=!is_div&&!is_mul&&in.ctrl.is_jump, and
ef=!is_div&&!is_mul&&!in.ctrl.is_jump. Compute the captured value as
(div_result & {32{ed}}) | (mul_result & {32{em}}) |
((in.pc+32'd4) & {32{ej}}) | (alu_result & {32{ef}}).
These enables preserve the original priority for every control
combination. Keep the existing reset, dmem-hold, execute-wait and
invalid-bubble branches around this register assignment. This final
mux rewrite is necessary to the measured improvement; replacing only
operand selectors did not clear the tournament acceptance threshold.

Preserve held-operand behavior, reset, invalid-instruction suppression,
dmem priority, load-use bubbles and once-only M completion. Retain all
decoder legality, trap, full-width address, RVFI order and nret=1 IO
contracts. This does not change register-file storage or enable a
load result to forward early. The expected benefit is fewer LUT and
routing stages before both arithmetic and branch resolution, with
exactly the existing CoreMark instruction/cycle schedule.

title: Retiming register-file reads and bypass selection at the decode boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 142.52 iterations/s at 57.541 MHz and 4,037,538
CoreMark bracket cycles. The latest structural winner removed the major
M-extension timing limits; the remaining worst path starts in the
register file and crosses forwarding and the ordinary ALU. A fresh
Gowin option-0 run reproduced 53.956 MHz and its 23.828 ns path, showing
that the inferred register file uses BSRAM. A scratch banked-flop file
alone reduced median Fmax to 55.748 MHz because register-number
comparison through forwarding became critical. Registering dependency
matches and using parallel operand selection with the original file
instead reached 60.173 MHz, but its 4.57 percent gain falls just short
of the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. Both paths therefore need the same
structural treatment of operand delivery at the decode/execute boundary.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the integer operand-delivery boundary so register storage
and dependency comparison both finish before EX's data selection and
arithmetic. Use a banked flop register file with balanced read trees,
register forwarding matches alongside ID/EX, and drive parallel one-hot
operand muxes from those matches. Preserve the existing pipeline depth,
throughput, load-use interlock, memory protocol and M-unit schedules.
This is one structural operand-delivery hypothesis, with no added stage.

Implement x1..x31 as independently enabled 32-bit flop words, grouped
into four banks of eight architectural register numbers; x0 is constant
zero. Use constant-index word storage, per-word decoded write enables,
and one-hot masked-OR read trees balanced within and between banks.
Avoid dynamically indexed inferred memory reads and priority read muxes.
Keep the existing two combinational read ports, synchronous zero reset,
write-first bypass and ID/EX operand-capture edge. Check mapped storage
and the retained operand-register boundary in vendor reports.

Move source/destination equality comparisons from EX into the preceding
ID cycle. For each incoming source register, latch two nonzero-destination
match bits: one against the current ID/EX destination, which becomes
EX/MEM on that edge, and one against the current EX/MEM destination,
which becomes MEM/WB. The four match bits travel with the instruction.
Qualify these matches in EX with the actual current producer reg_write
controls, preserving EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority. Register matches, not
speculatively assumed producer write permission: misaligned accesses or
control transfers can still suppress a producer's architectural write.

Reset or a permitted ID/EX flush clears the match state. On normal ID/EX
capture recompute it from the selected fetch-queue head and pre-edge
producer destinations. A dmem hold retains both sets of match bits,
matching the held EX/MEM and retained MEM/WB forwarding payload. When
ID/EX is held for an M operation but older stages advance, transfer the
old EX-match bits into the WB-match bits and clear EX matches as EX/MEM
becomes a bubble. Never recompute a held instruction's matches from a
changing queue head. Load-use bubbles, redirects, invalid instructions,
and simultaneous hold/flush priorities must mirror ID/EX exactly.
Keep retained WB forwarding qualified by its stored reg_write, not by
retirement-valid, which intentionally clears during a dmem hold.

Produce mutually exclusive RF, EX/MEM and MEM/WB enables for each source,
with three-bit encoding bit 0 = RF, bit 1 = EX/MEM, bit 2 = MEM/WB.
Select source data with parallel masked-OR logic, avoiding encoded
priority-mux cascades. Form ALU operands directly from those sources
plus PC or immediate with mutually exclusive enables, so AUIPC/immediate
selection does not add another serial data mux after forwarding.
Keep separate correct raw rs1/rs2 selections for branch comparisons,
stores, JALR, M-unit launch and RVFI; immediate or PC substitution must
not change architectural source reporting. Preserve M-unit captured
operands, reset cancellation, once-only completion and downstream bypass.

Preserve nret=1, all top-level ports, the fetch queue and predictor,
decoder legality, memory alignment traps and side-effect gating,
contiguous retirement, and every formal/progress/arithmetic assertion.
Forecast a 10 percent fitness gain at unchanged bracket cycles; this
requires about 63.30 MHz. Acceptance requires over 149.07592 iterations/s,
or about 60.19 MHz at 4,037,538 cycles. Additional flop/read-tree area,
write fanout and the remaining arithmetic paths are the main risks.
Measure median vendor Gowin Fmax times the actual bracketed cycle rate.
Run unchanged formal, full RVFI cosimulation, real/ALTOPS pipeline tests,
and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks. A scratch prototype of the combined design used the unchanged FPGA
wrapper, stall generator, constraints and vendor flow. Gowin placement
options 0/1/2 measured 62.665/64.003/64.003 MHz, median 64.003 MHz.
It used 5,213 LUT4, 1,924 FF, zero LUT-RAM, four BSRAM and two DSPs,
compared with the champion's 3,979 LUT4, 989 FF, eight LUT-RAM, six
BSRAM and two DSPs. The worst option-0 path moved from the register-file
BSRAM output to WB result selection through EX, with arrival reduced
from 23.828 ns to 21.253 ns. This is a changed storage and operand-route
network, not a circuit-neutral placement perturbation.

The prototype completed the canonical stalled ten-iteration CoreMark
run in exactly 4,037,538 bracket cycles; the unchanged validator accepted
its CRCs and UART text and the harness reported no out-of-bounds access.

142.52. Keep the forecast at 10 percent with medium confidence because
implementation details and placement can reduce this margin.

modes, and selftest plus three random programs with complete reference-ISS

An additional register-file test passed all 1,024 source-address pairs
after distinct per-register writes, 2,048 randomized read/write cycles
including simultaneous two-port bypass, and reset of populated state.
The unchanged full formal suite passed all 53 checks, including reg,
liveness, illegal instructions, ordering and PC consistency. These
scratch results do not replace implementation-phase correctness gates.
Deliver only the hypothesis, leaving repository RTL unchanged.

title: Register branch prediction recovery outside the execute feedback path
motivation:
The champion scores 142.52 iterations/s at 57.541 MHz and 4,037,538
measured CoreMark cycles. Its existing 64-counter predictor already
handles most direct transfers. Prior trace studies found only 51,857
direction misses among 529,588 conditional branches, and larger local
history saved only 4,109 misses. A fresh architectural replay of the
canonical binary reproduced all five CRCs and the validation message:
203,959 immediately load-dependent consumers included 135,320 branches
and 59,270 loads. A 64-entry tagged last-value predictor requiring three
consecutive matches offered only 1,458 confident predictions, of which
676 were correct; a similarly qualified stride predictor offered 4,218,
with 1,905 correct. These optimistic sequential replays do not model
pipeline stalls, and argue against adding general load-value prediction.
Prior deferred load-branch proposals
saved about 2.5% of cycles but did not meet the fitness threshold once
physical timing was included. The current implementation still sends
forwarded operand comparisons through combinational redirect to fetch
control and the reset/flush mux on the entire ID/EX bundle. A prediction
recovery boundary offers a distinct timing-focused predictor experiment
without another memory-data verification path. The reported worst path
is the register-file/ALU path, so recovery is not a proven clock limit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Register all branch-prediction corrections alongside the resolving
instruction's EX/MEM entry. Use that older registered correction to
redirect fetch and squash the younger EX instruction on the following
cycle. Keep the current direction predictor, immediate-derived direct
targets, fetch queue, load-use interlocks and M-extension units. This
is one predictor recovery mechanism: trade an extra recovery cycle on
a miss for a shorter operand-comparison-to-global-control path.

In EX, retain the existing full-width target arithmetic, forwarded
comparison, target alignment checks and architectural next-PC rules.
When a valid instruction advances, capture a mismatch bit comparing
actual_taken with its saved predicted_taken, and capture the actual
successor as the correction target. JALR remains predicted not taken.
Do not drive fetch, ID flush or ordinary branch training from that
cycle's raw EX mismatch. Correctly predicted instructions continue at
unchanged throughput; only a mismatch adds one recovery cycle.

The correction becomes visible from the registered resolving token in
MEM. Before the younger EX token can enter EX/MEM, it discards that
younger token, clears ID/EX validity and live side-effect controls,
empties the fetch
queue and resets ID/EX validity, while sending the registered actual
successor to fetch. It must override a younger load-use indication,
execute_wait, branch result, M-unit start and result acceptance, and
an unready instruction bus. A wrong-path store or load has not yet
reached MEM and must never issue a request. A younger multiply/divide
must be prevented from launching on the correction cycle; do not let
its wait signal block correction. No architectural rollback is needed.

Service a pending correction for exactly one cycle while retaining
its resolving instruction in EX/MEM. On that edge, clear only its
correction-pending bit, issue the redirect, kill the younger EX/ID
work, and insert a WB bubble while retaining the previous WB data for
forwarding. On the following edge the retained resolving instruction
enters WB exactly once; it must not redirect again. This recovery
service cycle replaces admission of the killed EX token, so it adds
no extra fetch delay beyond the registered correction itself. It also
shifts the correcting branch's retirement one cycle later, preserving
the existing nine-cycle branch-to-divider retirement-gap assertion
rather than increasing it to ten. Preserve that assertion unchanged
and test branch-to-DIV, DIV-to-branch and consecutive corrections.

Register correction validity only on true EX advancement, clear it on
bubbles/reset or correction service, and preserve it with its token
under older dmem holds. A correcting control-transfer token has no
memory request. Keep recovery service distinct from dmem backpressure:
it holds the older resolving token while actively discarding younger
work, regardless of the younger execute_wait. Qualify every correction
with the valid resolving token. Move conditional-branch training to
acceptance into WB, excluding the correction-service cycle, so every
legal nonfaulting branch trains exactly once from registered PC/outcome.
A killed younger branch never trains. Preserve current-counter
saturation and pre-edge lookup semantics, including same-index fetch
and training. Preserve JAL/JALR link-result forwarding while the
correcting jump is retained and when its target reaches EX.

Keep recovery off wide payload capture. Split ID/EX and EX/MEM validity
and side-effect controls from instruction, PC, operand, immediate,
ALU-result and store-data payload registers. On a squash, payloads may
retain or capture don't-care values, but invalid entries must not
forward, initiate M execution, request memory, train or retire. Use
qualified validity/control signals for every such consumer. Preserve
existing MEM/WB retained forwarding data during dmem stalls; do not
gate that special retained forwarding solely with retirement valid.
Do not add a wide predicted-next-PC comparison or reintroduce a mux
that replaces the raw fetched instruction on a correction.

The unmeasured forecast is a 6% fitness gain with low confidence.
Roughly 52,000 additional conditional-miss cycles plus unpredicted
JALR recovery suggest about 1.5-2% more CoreMark cycles; fetch-queue
and bus overlap require actual measurement. At 2% more cycles the
median Gowin clock must exceed approximately 61.40 MHz to beat the
champion by 4.6%, and approximately 62.22 MHz to gain 6%. This requires
a physical clock improvement, not an accuracy claim. The existing
ALU-to-memory path may remain critical and defeat the hypothesis.

CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks, then compare median vendor Fmax times
iterations/cycle. Preserve nret=1, IO, decoder legality, trap/link
semantics, contiguous RVFI order and the unchanged formal progress
window, including a corrected transfer followed by DIV/REM.

ALU and EX result selection into data-memory BSRAM. Other prototypes
expose the WB load/ALU mux on the same feedback path. The r7s1 winner
removed register-read and dependency-comparison limits, but address
generation and forwarding still traverse result selection unnecessary
for their individual consumers. Prior r6s0 address isolation and
r7s0 mux flattening each left another path limiting the clock.

Combine a dedicated effective-address register, exclusive parallel
EX result selection, load/ALU writeback selection before MEM/WB,
and retention of inactive EX result payloads. These are one coordinated combinational result-routing optimization:
preserve every stage boundary, instruction latency, forwarding priority,
predictor, fetch queue, M-unit schedule and bus handshake.

Capture forwarded raw rs1 + in.imm on the same edge as the other EX
payload. This sum must be independent of ALU opcode, ALU operand-B
substitution, jump-link selection and MUL/DIV result selection.
Keep reset and dmem-hold priority; handle bubbles as below. Do not truncate

Leave general EX/MEM alu_result available for EX forwarding and

DIV result enabled by is_div; MUL result by is_mul; PC+4 by

An isolated prototype of these result-routing changes used the
unchanged vendor flow, FPGA wrapper, constraints and stall generator.
Placement options 0/1/2 achieved 71.318/73.284/73.284 MHz, median
73.284 MHz, with 5,152 LUT4, 1,923 FF, zero LUT-RAM, four BSRAM

The prototype passed all 34 pipeline tests in both real and ALTOPS

The unchanged CoreMark validator accepted completion, canonical CRCs,

The measured product is approximately 181.507 iterations/s, a 4.58
percent gain, narrowly below the required 181.54376 acceptance score.
Forecast five percent with medium confidence: this is a near-threshold
hypothesis, not a claim of acceptance. Further implementation must
exceed about 73.30 MHz at unchanged cycles. Extra address routing and
the remaining divider/control paths are the principal timing risks.
Full formal was not rerun for this proposal and remains a required
implementation gate. Deliver only this hypothesis; prototype RTL stays
outside the repository RTL.

title: Retime the complete producer-to-memory bypass path
motivation: The champion scores 173.56 iterations/s at 70.074 MHz and 4,037,538 CoreMark bracket cycles. Its reported worst path starts at EX/MEM producer write control and reaches data-memory BSRAM through forwarding and the general ALU. The previous structural winner moved register-file reads and dependency matches before ID/EX, but producer qualification, WB result selection and address generation still share the same downstream timing cone. Scratch isolation experiments show that removing just one segment exposes another: separate address generation alone reached 62.905 MHz, registered forwarding enables 65.910 MHz, and registered enables plus WB data 67.723 MHz on placement option 1. Combining those register-boundary changes with a dedicated address register reached 71.148 MHz on option 1. This identifies a coordinated bypass-path restructuring rather than a new pipeline stage as the promising structural angle.

Its reported worst path starts at EX/MEM producer write control and reaches data-memory BSRAM through forwarding and the general ALU. hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the producer-to-memory bypass path at its existing register boundaries: compute final one-hot source enables before ID/EX, and select the architectural writeback value before MEM/WB. EX then receives registered RF/EX-MEM/MEM-WB source enables and a directly registered WB value. Add a dedicated memory-address result path, completing the removal of serial producer-control and general-result selection from the memory endpoint. Keep the pipeline depth, all instruction service schedules and the load-use interlock unchanged. Do not add a predictor, cache, extra execute stage or change arithmetic algorithms.

For each incoming ID source, form an EX hit using the current ID/EX destination and EX's final write permission after its existing control-transfer alignment/trap checks. Form a WB hit using the current EX/MEM destination and MEM's final write permission after its existing memory alignment/trap checks. Qualify both by the corresponding producer's valid and nonzero destination. At the ordinary ID/EX capture edge register the mutually exclusive source vector {WB_hit && !EX_hit, EX_hit, !(EX_hit || WB_hit)}. These are final priority-resolved enables, not address matches subsequently qualified by EX/MEM or MEM/WB controls. Preserve the existing one-hot operand data networks and all raw source values for stores, branches, M-unit capture and RVFI.

Expose internal combinational producer-write eligibility signals from EX and MEM; do not add top-level ports. Use the controls that will actually enter the next producer register, so a trapped or illegal producer never overrides an older architectural register value. Registering decoded reg_write alone is insufficient. Ordinary ID capture happens only when those stages can advance. Preserve the instruction pipeline reset/flush/hold/invalid priorities. Reset and invalid capture select RF. Source-selection registers need not clear on a squash: ID/EX already becomes a zero-control invalid bubble, so stale source enables cannot execute or retire anything. Remove flush from forwarding-vector reset/enable logic; a subsequent valid ID capture must always recompute the complete vector. Keep the actual ID/EX squash and all zero-control bubble checks unchanged. A dmem hold retains both complete vectors. During an M wait while older stages drain, translate an EX-selected source to WB and every other source to RF, matching the existing producer-stage movement. M-unit source snapshots already retain operands after launch. Never recompute a held instruction's enables from the changing fetch-queue head, and never gate retained WB data by retirement valid.

Add a unified writeback_value field to MEM/WB. In MEM compute it from load_data versus EX/MEM alu_result using the existing mem_to_reg control, and register the selected word on the existing MEM/WB edge. WB w_data becomes a direct wire from this field for register-file write-first bypass, EX forwarding and RVFI rd_wdata. Hold writeback_value with every other payload field when dmem stalls clear only retirement valid; reset initializes it. Preserve raw memory data and other RVFI metadata. The existing per-instruction write permission still controls actual writes, including misaligned loads. The legacy split result fields may remain only where needed; synthesis must not leave the old post-register result mux in the timed WB data path.

Partition load/store address execution from the general ALU result. Compute the full-width sum of raw forwarded rs1 and the decoded immediate and capture a dedicated EX/MEM.effective_addr on the existing edge. This removes the ALU opcode, operand-B and MUL/DIV/link result muxes from the memory endpoint. Keep one address adder; a scratch three-adder select-after-add version regressed to 69.507 MHz median. Preserve alu_result for register writeback and forwarding, and drive the bus address, alignment checks, lane masks, load extraction and RVFI aligned address from effective_addr. Preserve 32-bit carries, signed immediates, dmem-hold stability and existing reset/zero-control bubble priorities. This is the final segment of the same bypass-path restructuring, with no speculative memory requests.

Preserve nret=1, top-level IO, contiguous retirement, default-illegal decoding, memory side-effect gating, M-unit real and ALTOPS arithmetic, and every existing progress/latency check. Expected bracket cycles remain 4,037,538. Acceptance needs over 181.54376 iterations/s, approximately 73.30 MHz at this count. The forecast is six percent, requiring approximately 74.28 MHz. Risks are moving exception qualification into the ID capture cone, longer memory-to-WB capture timing, and another arithmetic or branch path becoming limiting. Run unchanged formal, full RVFI cosimulation, real/ALTOPS pipeline suites and canonical stalled CoreMark validation, then compare median Gowin Fmax times the measured bracketed cycle rate. The registered-enable/unified-WB subset passed all 53 unchanged formal checks. The 71.148 MHz intermediate version is below the acceptance margin. The final proposal additionally removes the unnecessary redirect-to-forwarding-register squash path exposed by timing. Its full timing and correctness validation are still required; this is a low-confidence research forecast, not a demonstrated winning score.

title: Predict forwarding sources and WB result kind before execute
motivation:
The champion reaches 173.56 iterations/s at 70.074 MHz and 4,037,538
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at
EX/MEM ctrl.reg_write and traverses forwarding and the ALU to data
memory. The last winning design registered dependency matches but
still qualifies and prioritizes them with actual producer write
permission in EX. Prior predictor studies found only 51,857 direction
misses among 529,588 conditional branches, and a larger local-history
predictor saved only 4,109 misses. Delayed branch recovery added 1.64%
cycles for only 0.73% higher Fmax. Instead, predict operand forwarding
permission early and verify exceptional write cancellation separately.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion reaches 173.56 iterations/s at 70.074 MHz and 4,037,538
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at
EX/MEM ctrl.reg_write and traverses forwarding and the ALU to data
memory. The last winning design registered dependency matches but
still qualifies and prioritizes them with actual producer write
permission in EX. Prior predictor studies found only 51,857 direction

cycles for only 0.73% higher Fmax. Instead, predict operand forwarding

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Register complete one-hot operand-source predictions alongside
ID/EX, rather than registering only register-number matches. Predict
that a positively decoded register-writing producer will complete
without an alignment fault. Resolve EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB-over-captured-RF
priority in ID using both register matches and the producers' existing
decoded write controls. Feed these registered selectors directly to
the existing parallel operand masks in EX, removing actual producer
reg_write qualification and priority logic from the arithmetic path.
This is one operand-source prediction mechanism with precise replay,
not a change to the branch-direction policy or arithmetic units.

Include the WB result kind in that registered source choice. Give EX
separate registered MEM/WB alu_result and read_data inputs instead of
forwarding the output of WB's late mem_to_reg mux. For each raw operand,
use four one-hot choices: captured RF, EX/MEM ALU, MEM/WB ALU, MEM/WB
load. Feed those sources into the existing parallel raw/ALU operand
masks, retaining local PC/immediate substitution in EX. Keep separate
raw operands for branches, stores, JALR, M launch and RVFI. Do not add
a stage or another register-file access. WB's architectural write mux
is unchanged. This completes the same forwarding-source prediction;
it does not predict operand values or change operation semantics.

Predict only a valid, legal, nonzero-destination producer's write.
Decoder-negative instructions never become predicted writers. For the
older producer currently in MEM, use its already-resolved memory
alignment/write permission at the ID capture boundary, so a faulting
load is not predicted to write WB. Keep the ordinary load-use interlock.
The remaining uncertain permission is a producer currently in EX whose
control-transfer alignment check can cancel its decoded link write.
Preserve youngest-writer priority in the registered one-hot choice.
No predictor table or benchmark-specific PC is needed.

In parallel with the fast operand datapath, compare each selected
EX/MEM or MEM/WB producer's predicted permission with its actual
registered write permission. WB permission should already be resolved
before capture; keep its validation term separate from the source
masks. If a selected write was canceled, prevent this consumer
from entering EX/MEM, launching MUL/DIV, redirecting as a branch,
training the predictor, issuing memory, or retiring. Let older work
drain, flush the consumer and younger fetch/decode tokens, and redirect
to the consumer's own PC for replay. This correction takes precedence
over any branch result computed from the speculative operands and
over an unstarted M instruction's execute_wait. Its later refetch reads
the committed older value, including an older same-register writer.
Replay must be independent of io_imemReady and must not cancel or
replay the older faulting producer. Reset has highest priority;
an older dmem hold defers verification and replay until EX can advance.

Do not put the actual write-permission check back into the operand
selection masks, arithmetic inputs, or a combinational fallback mux.
Route it only to validity, side-effect suppression and replay control.
Keep exact architectural raw operands for RVFI; replay applies to
both raw sources, including fields not consumed by a particular ALU
operation. Invalid tokens cannot forward or initiate any operation.
Preserve retained MEM/WB forwarding payload during dmem holds without
qualifying it by retirement-valid, which intentionally clears.

Match selector state to instruction and producer movement: reset and
flush invalidate it; dmem holds preserve it; normal acceptance captures
fresh one-hot predictions; while an M operation holds ID/EX and older
stages drain, migrate any EX source to WB consistently with the data.
Once an M unit has captured validated operands, subsequent producer
movement must not trigger replay of that in-flight operation. Keep its
existing operand snapshots and completion protocol unchanged. Do not
recalculate a held instruction's prediction from a changing queue head.

On normal aligned programs this should preserve every instruction's
service schedule and CoreMark cycle count while shortening the measured
forwarding-control-to-ALU path. Forecast 5% fitness improvement with
low confidence. At unchanged 4,037,538 cycles, acceptance requires
median Gowin Fmax above approximately 73.30 MHz; a 5% gain needs about
73.58 MHz. Measure the actual product, not selector depth.

A scratch prototype of this four-source design measured
70.082/73.121/73.121 MHz over the unchanged vendor placement options,
median 73.121 MHz, at the same 4,037,538 canonical stalled CoreMark
cycles. Its approximate 181.10 iterations/s is a 4.35% improvement,
BELOW the required 4.6% threshold. This is evidence for the mechanism,
not a demonstrated acceptance result; the forecast's remaining margin
is uncertain and must come from the final circuit and measured timing.
The prototype used 5,251 LUT4, 1,928 FF, four BSRAM and two DSPs.
It passed all 53 unchanged formal checks, all 34 existing pipeline
tests in each real/ALTOPS mode, and an additional cancellation-to-MUL/DIV
progress test in each mode. The canonical stalled CoreMark validator
accepted every CRC and UART requirement and reported no out-of-bounds
access. Replay, pipeline and exception correctness still need the
implementation phase's complete gates.

Keep the measured four-source boundary. A three-source prototype that
still forwarded WB's merged write-data mux reached only 67.719 MHz;
registering additional PC/immediate ALU masks reached only 70.187 MHz.
Removing the WB verification term and removing prediction-register
flush controls also failed to improve on the four-source result.
These observations favor the stated bounded design over adding more
prediction state or removing the existing mask reset/flush discipline.

Preserve nret=1, all IO, exact trap/write suppression and RVFI operands,
contiguous order, canonical CRCs/UART/markers and bounded addresses.
Replay must make progress under arbitrary symbolic instructions within
the unchanged formal window. In particular, avoid a WB-stage prediction
failure on a faulting load by incorporating its known alignment result
before capturing selectors; test canceled-link-write replay followed
immediately by DIV/REM. Keep the existing branch-to-divider nine-cycle
assertion and all liveness checks unchanged. Run full real/ALTOPS unit
tests, formal, stalled RVFI cosim and canonical CoreMark validation,
followed by median vendor timing. Do not modify evaluation files.

title: Local saturating-counter updates remove shared predictor feedback
motivation: The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538 CoreMark bracket cycles. The latest timing path crosses EX recovery and frontend control; local scratch variants also expose EX-to-direction-counter paths. In if_stage, a variable-index read, saturating arithmetic and variable-index write describe the training update. Expressing each counter as independently enabled local state can remove the shared old-counter selection and arithmetic from this feedback network. The r7s2 recovery retiming lost throughput, and r8s0 result specialization did not improve the accepted score. This proposal changes only counter circuit topology, with identical prediction and training behavior.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement the existing 64 two-bit bimodal counters as 64 constant-index generated register words, each with its own training enable and explicit Boolean saturating transition. Preserve the same table size, indexing, state encoding, initialization, lookup and training edge. This is a micro-optimization of the existing state-update circuit, not a predictor-policy change, a new predictor or delayed training.

For entry i, use enable_i = branch_train && (branch_index == i), comparing at exactly six bits. Let h=counters[i][1], l=counters[i][0] and t=branch_outcome. On an enabled update, assign next_h = (h && l) || (t && (h || l)); next_l = (h && !l) || (t && (h || !l)). Each next-state bit is a three-input Boolean function of this entry's old state and outcome. Use elaboration-time constant indexing so there is no counters[branch_index] old-state read in the update datapath. Reset each entry synchronously to 01 with priority over training; otherwise hold every nonselected entry. Keep the dynamic counters[pc[7:2]][1] fetch lookup unchanged.

These equations implement taken transitions 00->01, 01->10, 10->11, 11->11 and not-taken transitions 00->00, 01->00, 10->01, 11->10. Preserve nonblocking assignment semantics: fetch and ID/EX must observe the pre-edge prediction on simultaneous same-index training. Every update uses the current entry state at resolution, never the counter value sampled when the instruction was fetched. Do not add write-through, reset scrubbing, forwarding of a newly trained direction, or an extra training register.

Keep branch_train qualification, alias behavior, direct-target derivation and its full-width bounds/alignment checks exactly as today. Preserve the two-entry queue, fall-through bypass, redirect priority, stalls, raw decode, forwarding/replay, ALU and M units. Maintain nret=1, all public IO, exact traps, monotonic retirement, memory side-effect suppression, arithmetic correctness and symbolic progress. No evaluation or contract files change.

The intended benefit is replacing a global read/modify/write selection network with local LUT-sized next-state functions and decoded enables. This can shorten training feedback and reduce routing pressure without changing cycles. Gowin may already implement part of this transformation, and outcome/enable fanout or the divider and ALU paths may cap the gain; the estimate therefore has low confidence.

Validate all eight old-state/outcome combinations, both saturation endpoints, reset versus simultaneous training, every table index, alias collisions, back-to-back updates and simultaneous fetch/training of the same entry. Check prediction sequences and accepted tokens against the original counter model with independent instruction/data stalls and redirects. Preserve existing tests and run unchanged formal, RVFI cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks. At identical inputs and stall streams, expect exactly 4,037,538 bracket cycles. Judge median vendor Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle. Acceptance requires more than 191.37616 iterations/s, approximately 77.268 MHz at unchanged cycles; a speculative five-percent forecast is not a claim that this threshold has been measured.

title: Precompute conditional-branch recovery before the ID/EX boundary
motivation: The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz with 4,037,538 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Reproducing Gowin placement option 1 confirms a critical path from a forwarding selector through operand selection, a branch comparison carry chain, redirect qualification and the ID/forwarding reset network. Earlier operand retiming removed late bypass qualification, leaving this branch-control feedback path exposed. Registering recovery after EX previously added cycles without sufficient clock benefit. Instead, move operand-independent branch resolution work before the existing ID/EX edge while retaining the current EX resolution cycle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Partition conditional-branch resolution into registered static control in ID and dynamic operand comparisons in EX. At the existing ID/EX capture edge, register one-hot controls for the six legal branch predicates, one-hot controls for the predicate that means the captured prediction is wrong, branch-training eligibility derived from direct target alignment, and the single correction destination implied by the captured prediction. This is one structural retiming of the branch-control boundary; it neither adds a pipeline stage nor changes prediction policy, fetch buffering, forwarding selection, ALU/M service schedules or retirement width.

For a validated branch, form six outcome enables for EQ, NE, signed LT, signed GE, unsigned LT and unsigned GE. For an aligned direct target, form the corresponding six recovery enables after XORing branch_op bit zero with this token's predicted_taken bit. Thus a predicted-not-taken BEQ requests correction on EQ, while a predicted-taken BEQ requests correction on NE; the same complementary pairing applies to signed and unsigned comparisons. All other recovery enables are zero. For a misaligned direct target, actual_taken must be false whether or not the comparison succeeds, so record a separate forced-fallthrough recovery bit equal to predicted_taken. Keep default-illegal decoding unchanged; nonbranches and invalid decode entries must not acquire branch enables.

Also register two mutually exclusive training classes for legal branches: aligned target, which can train for either outcome, and misaligned target, which may train only if the condition is false. The latter preserves the existing rule that an untaken branch does not fault merely because its encoded target is misaligned. Compute the target alignment from the full-width PC-plus-immediate semantics in ID. Do not truncate architectural targets or wrap addresses. Register one branch_recovery_target alongside this metadata: predicted_taken ? PC+4 : PC+branch_immediate. A direction correction for a conditional branch necessarily selects the opposite direction from its captured prediction. Consequently its correction destination is known in ID, before the actual comparison. Select this registered destination for a branch correction instead of using late actual_taken to select a 32-bit recovery target in EX. This is the essential data half of the same branch-recovery retiming. Do not register two separate target and PC+4 payloads. Keep the full existing architectural target/next-PC calculation for trap and RVFI purposes, and keep JALR's dynamic target computation.

In EX retain the current forwarded raw rs1/rs2 operands and compare them once for equality, signed less-than and unsigned less-than. Form complementary predicates and use parallel masked-OR selection with the registered outcome controls. Independently select the prediction-error predicate with the registered recovery controls. This bypasses the current serial branch-op selection, taken qualification, misalignment qualification and predicted_taken XOR on the common aligned-branch recovery path. Use the outcome for branch_taken and RVFI next-PC/trap semantics, and use the separate error result only to request the existing correction. Training uses its registered eligibility classes and the actual condition. Preserve pre-edge counter lookup, same-index training behavior and once-per-advancing-branch updates.

Qualify branch correction by the valid token, reset, older dmem hold and operand-prediction verification. Since the recovery controls are nonzero only for legal conditional branches, do not serialize branch correction through an unrelated M-unit completion cone. Keep ordinary JAL/JALR and nonbranch prediction correction separate, including JALR bit-zero clearing and target alignment. Factor nonbranch actual-taken logic from jump legality/alignment directly, without depending on a conditional-branch comparison that cannot belong to that instruction. Canceled selected producer writes retain highest correction priority: replay the consumer PC and suppress its branch training, memory effects, arithmetic launch and retirement. Correction-target selection gives consumer replay highest priority, then the registered conditional-branch recovery destination, then the existing jump/fallthrough destination. All targets remain architectural and full-width.

Move the metadata with exactly the existing ID/EX reset, flush, hold, invalid-capture and normal-capture priorities. Retain zero-control bubbles and zero forwarding selectors where the existing tests require them. Hold captured predicted_taken and the new controls together through dmem and execute holds. Preserve source snapshots, retained MEM/WB forwarding and every existing side-effect qualification. No delayed branch recovery, early speculative memory operation or extra replay mode is introduced.

Forecast five percent fitness improvement with low confidence, at unchanged 4,037,538 bracket cycles. Acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax above approximately 77.27 MHz; a five percent gain needs approximately 77.56 MHz. This is an unproven forecast. Partial scratch variants passed all 37 existing pipeline tests in each real/ALTOPS mode but did not clear the acceptance margin: registering recovery controls plus wide target/PC4 payloads measured 72.057 MHz median, and the smaller recovery-only variant measured 68.839 MHz. Those partial variants are not winning evidence. Retiming outcome/training controls without the preselected recovery destination also measured only 68.947 MHz. These failures show that control retiming alone is insufficient. The final proposal also removes the late comparison from the wide correction-target data path using the single preselected registered recovery destination, and separates jump correction qualification. This complete branch-recovery boundary is the proposed structural mechanism. Its timing benefit remains uncertain. Its final implementation must be judged by measured median vendor Fmax times actual iteration/cycle rate; ordinary ALU/divider timing and extra control fanout may prevent a win.

Run the unchanged formal checks, full real/ALTOPS pipeline suites, stalled RVFI cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker validation. Preserve the existing nine-cycle ready-bus branch-to-divider gap assertion and formal liveness window. Test every legal branch predicate and prediction direction, signed/unsigned boundaries, all forwarding sources, misaligned targets for taken and untaken outcomes, illegal branch encodings, JAL/JALR faults, canceled-write replay, independent bus stalls and reset. Require exact RVFI operands, trap/PC/order and once-only memory effects. Preserve nret=1, all public IO, every decoder/trap rule and bounded address requirement; do not change evaluation files or weaken checks. Deliver only this hypothesis with repository RTL unchanged.

title: Predecode prediction recovery predicates before execute
motivation:
The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
bracketed CoreMark cycles. A fresh unchanged Gowin placement-option-0
run reproduces 68.070 MHz and the reported worst path: EX/MEM forwarded
operand, a full-width comparison carry chain, five redirect logic levels,
then fetch/decode control and the forwarding-selector reset. Prediction
verification now lies on the measured critical path. Earlier delayed
recovery (r7s2) added 1.64% cycles for only 0.73% median clock improvement;
larger direction tables also showed little remaining accuracy benefit.
Shortening same-cycle verification targets this bottleneck without
changing the prediction policy or adding a misprediction penalty.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the existing 64-entry bimodal predictor and same-cycle EX recovery,
but move prediction-dependent recovery decoding to the ID/EX boundary.
Register four mutually exclusive verification enables: expect equality,
expect inequality, expect less-than, and expect not-less-than. Derive the
expected primitive result as predicted_taken XOR branch funct3 bit 0;
BEQ/BNE use equality and the four ordered branches use less-than. Enable
these checks only for a positively decoded legal conditional branch with
an aligned direct target. Target alignment is exactly the low two bits
of PC plus immediate; retain full-width target arithmetic everywhere
that actually constructs an address. Capture a separate direct-JAL
correction bit for legal aligned JAL whose captured prediction is false.
This is predecoded prediction verification, with no new prediction table,
branch latency, deferred recovery, or speculative architectural result.

In EX, use exact existing forwarded operands to compute one equality
and one unsigned less-than relation. Signed ordering uses rs1[31] when
signs differ and unsigned less-than otherwise; branch funct3 selects the
signed versus unsigned interpretation. Let the registered verification
enables directly select the violated primitive relations with parallel
AND/OR terms. OR this result with the registered JAL-correction bit and
the legal, aligned JALR correction, then apply a specialized control-transfer acceptance qualification and
operand-permission replay priority. The specialized qualification is
in.valid AND !stall AND !prediction_failed AND !reset. The verified
instruction classes cannot be MUL/DIV/REM, so the generic execute_wait
and M-busy-dependent operands_invalid terms are unnecessary in this
particular correction path. Retain the original generic EX advancement,
M-start validation and replay logic elsewhere. Prove equivalence under
reachable pipeline states; do not add assumptions about busy or decode. Remove the generic
actual_taken-versus-predicted_taken comparison from the global correction
cone. Instruction classification, expected outcome, direct-target
alignment and direct-JAL eligibility must not be decoded serially after
the operand comparison. Retain native full-width comparison mapping:
a scratch byte-sliced comparator instead reached only 62.743 MHz median
at unchanged cycles, so the proposal does not prescribe that topology.

Derive actual branch condition, training outcome and RVFI next PC from
the same exact relations with the original funct3 inversion. Architectural
outcome/trap logic remains fully checked but does not feed the redundant
late generic correction comparison. The fetch design already guarantees
that predicted_taken is true only for legal aligned direct transfers
whose complete target lies in main memory; JALR always arrives predicted
false. Prove and test these metadata invariants rather than introducing
an assumption into formal. They justify treating JALR as an always-missed
aligned legal jump and suppressing direct checks for misaligned targets.
A taken misaligned branch/JAL/JALR still traps and suppresses link writes
as today; its architectural successor is PC+4. Never redirect to a
misaligned target or change the existing full-width fetch range checks.

Capture all verification bits from the selected queue token and that
token's saved predicted_taken, never a fresh counter lookup. Hold them
with the entire ID/EX token across dmem and M-unit waits, and preserve
existing reset, flush and invalid-bubble clearing exactly. Keep current
forwarding masks, canceled-write replay, load-use interlocks, complete
ID/EX squash, EX/MEM advancement and M schedules. Replay overrides branch
recovery and forbids training and M launch as today. Only valid legal
advancing branches train, exactly once; keep training in EX, including
pre-edge lookup/update semantics. Correct predictions retain younger
work; correction flushes on the current EX edge even with imem unready.

This specifically avoids the earlier all-branch deferred recovery cost
of 1.64% extra cycles. A scratch selective ordered-branch deferred design
still reached only 66.751 MHz despite reducing that cost to 0.49%, so
no delayed-verification mechanism is included in this proposal. Focus
instead on moving recovery eligibility and expected-relation selection
before the existing register boundary, at an unchanged cycle schedule.

Forecast 6% fitness improvement with low confidence, from higher Fmax.
At the champion's 4,037,538 cycles, acceptance requires median vendor
Fmax above approximately 77.27 MHz and fitness above 191.37616 iter/s;
6% requires about 78.30 MHz. Prediction accuracy is unchanged. Placement,
new control registers and the next arithmetic critical path are material
risks; a shallower recovery cone is not itself evidence of acceptance.
Measure all three prescribed placement options and the actual product.

Preserve nret=1, external IO, default-illegal decode, exact traps, RVFI
operands/next-PC/order, bounded addresses, all canonical CoreMark CRCs,
UART validation and marker timing. Keep all existing unit assertions,
including cleared ID/EX and zero source masks after squash, the original
branch-to-divider latency bound and formal liveness window. Run unchanged
real/ALTOPS pipeline tests, formal, stalled cosimulation and canonical
CoreMark validation. Add focused relation/prediction coverage without
weakening checks or modifying evaluation files.

A scratch version with the predecoded predicates but still using generic
EX-advancement qualification passed all 53 unchanged formal checks,
all 37 existing pipeline tests in each real/ALTOPS mode, and canonical
stalled CoreMark validation at 4,037,538 cycles. It measured
71.018/72.154/72.154 MHz, median 72.154 MHz, with 5,304 LUT4 and 1,933
registers. This is approximately 178.71 iterations/s, BELOW the champion
and acceptance threshold; it is not evidence of a demonstrated gain.
The specialized control-transfer qualification is an additional concrete
refinement beyond that tested version. The forecast is uncertain and
requires the implementation phase's full correctness and timing gates.

title: Sign-biased parallel halfword branch comparison
motivation: The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path passes through execute, fetch and decode, while other placements expose the divider. Recent branch-recovery predecoding and retiming candidates regressed. The proposed local change targets the comparison datapath feeding same-cycle branch resolution. It leaves recovery controls, predictor policy and pipeline timing intact.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path passes through execute, fetch and decode, while other placements expose the divider. Recent branch-recovery predecoding and retiming candidates regressed. The proposed local change targets the comparison datapath feeding same-cycle branch resolution. It leaves recovery controls, predictor policy and pipeline timing intact.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the EX branch comparison network with one signedness-biased comparator built from two parallel 16-bit comparisons. For ordered branches, branch_op[1] distinguishes signed BLT/BGE (zero) from unsigned BLTU/BGEU (one). Form high operands HA={rs1[31] XOR !branch_op[1],rs1[30:16]} and HB={rs2[31] XOR !branch_op[1],rs2[30:16]}. Inverting both sign bits maps signed order exactly into unsigned order; leave them unchanged for unsigned branches. Calculate hi_lt=(HA<HB), hi_eq=(rs1[31:16]==rs2[31:16]), and lo_lt=(rs1[15:0]<rs2[15:0]) independently with native short unsigned comparisons. Then ordered_lt=hi_lt OR (hi_eq AND lo_lt). Equality is hi_eq AND (rs1[15:0]==rs2[15:0]). No full-width carry-dependent comparison or late signed-versus-unsigned result mux is needed.

Select primitive = branch_op[2] ? ordered_lt : equality. Compute branch_cond = (primitive XOR branch_op[0]) AND (branch_op[2] OR !branch_op[1]). The final guard preserves the original false default for reserved branch_op values 2 and 3; inversion implements BNE/BGE/BGEU. This exactly reproduces all eight branch_op cases. Keep the complete comparison and predicate computation in the existing EX cycle with no new state. Do not add prediction-verification bits, alter source masks or qualify the wide operands with branch validity.

Use exact post-forward rs1/rs2, preserving four-way source selection, producer priority and canceled-write replay. Keep branch_taken, alignment faults, actual_taken, redirect qualification and target selection, training, PC arithmetic and RVFI next-PC logic unchanged. The single micro-optimization is the branch comparator and its relation-selection circuit. It changes neither the predictor nor recovery latency.

Leave alu.sv unchanged, including SLT/SLTU, addition, subtraction, shifts and all M-extension arithmetic. The change is confined to the exact post-forward branch comparison network in ex_stage.sv. Do not merge branch and ALU operand streams, narrow architectural operands or insert a register.

Preserve all reset, flush, invalid-bubble, dmem hold, load-use, M-unit service and completion behavior, nret=1 external IO and RVFI retirement ordering. Decoder legality, misalignment traps, suppression of memory side effects, full-width targets and all evaluation contracts remain unchanged. Every comparison is exact for arbitrary 32-bit values, including opposite signs and equal high halves.

Add independent-reference checks for all branch predicates and SLT/SLTU/SLTI/SLTIU. Exercise equal operands, differences confined to either half, first differing bit at positions 15/16/30/31, 0x0000ffff versus 0x00010000, INT_MIN, INT_MAX, negative immediates and opposing signed/unsigned order. Cover every forwarding source, retained WB data during memory holds, taken/not-taken saved predictions, misaligned taken and untaken targets, cancellation replay, reset and once-only retirement. Retain all existing assertions and run unchanged real/ALTOPS pipeline, ALU, formal and stalled RVFI cosimulation checks plus canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker validation.

Expect unchanged 4,037,538 bracket cycles with identical instruction and stall streams. Forecast five percent fitness improvement with low confidence, entirely from Fmax. Acceptance requires more than 191.37616 iterations/s, approximately 77.27 MHz at that cycle count. Gowin may already optimize full-width comparisons, the high-equality merge may add routing delay, and the divider or ALU-result paths may cap the benefit. The earlier eight-bit-sliced comparator mentioned in r9s2 measured only 62.743 MHz median; this deliberately uses two larger halves to avoid its multi-group merge depth, but that negative evidence still limits confidence. Judge the complete prescribed vendor median, not RTL operator counts or a single favorable placement. No gain is claimed before those measurements.

A precursor with parallel 16/16 comparisons followed by a late signed-result mux measured 75.402 MHz in vendor placement option 1, with 5,258 LUT4 and 1,929 registers. Its unchanged CoreMark validator passed canonical CRCs, validation text, bounded accesses, markers and exactly 4,037,538 cycles. This precursor is below the acceptance threshold and is not evidence of a win. The final proposal moves signedness handling to the high-half input and folds branch inversion into the common primitive, removing further late selection logic. Timing of this complete refinement remains to be established; the five-percent estimate is speculative. All experiments use scratch RTL outside the repository; only this hypothesis is delivered.

Preserve all branch/replay/trap/redirect/training controls, forwarded operands and pipeline behavior.

title: Replace serial divider digit stages with a parallel radix-32 recurrence
motivation:
The champion reaches 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior structural divider changes delivered
substantial gains, while the r8s1 producer-to-memory retiming and r9s1
branch-recovery retiming regressed. The divider still appears as the
worst path in r8s1 and r9s0. Its current five-bit recurrence serializes
a radix-8 subtract/select and a radix-4 subtract/select. Parallelizing
that arithmetic dependency offers a distinct structural timing change
without increasing division stalls or changing branch recovery.
