hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the divider's cascaded radix-8/radix-4 recurrence with one
radix-32 digit-selection stage. Preserve the current eight service
edges: launch consumes the first two magnitude bits, six recurrence
edges consume five bits each, and EX/MEM accepts the corrected result.
Keep the existing blocking interface, operand snapshots, DONE holding,
reset cancellation, sign correction, and real/ALTOPS control schedule.
This is solely a restructuring of the registered divider datapath.

On launch, independently compute and register the odd divisor multiples
D, 3D, 5D, ..., 31D from the new unsigned divisor magnitude, using fully
widened arithmetic before shifts. Derive even multiples by wiring shifts
of the appropriate registered odd multiple. Every positive multiple
needs 37 magnitude bits because 31*(2^32-1) is below 2^37. Compute each
launch multiple directly from the new magnitude; do not cascade all
multiples through a long chain of additions or read stale registers.
Avoid inferred multiplication hardware for these constant multiples.

Each recurrence forms T={remainder,quotient[31:27]}, a 37-bit trial.
In parallel compute the 31 unsigned differences {0,T}-{0,kD}, k=1..31,
with 38-bit subtraction so the top bit reliably indicates borrow.
Select the largest fitting digit using the monotonic fit vector:
enable[0]=!fit[1], enable[k]=fit[k]&&!fit[k+1] for 1..30, and
enable[31]=fit[31]. Use explicit balanced masked-OR trees to select
the next remainder and encode the five quotient bits. Do not infer
a serial priority encoder, a quotient-dependent second subtractor,
or a subtract-compare-subtract cascade. Register the low 32 bits of
the selected remainder and {quotient[26:0],digit}; for nonzero D the
selected remainder is strictly below D and therefore fits 32 bits.
For D=0 every fit is true, digit 31 wins, and the existing original-
operand result override still produces exact DIV/REM zero semantics.

Preserve the existing shallow two-bit launch, signed magnitudes
including INT_MIN, all four DIV/REM signedness and result choices,
exact ALTOPS formulas, and stable completion under arbitrary holds.
No change to multiplication, normal EX, forwarding, predictor, queue,
issue width, nret=1 ports, decode/trap rules, or evaluation machinery.
Never add an extra multiple-generation or completion cycle: unchanged
formal liveness and branch-to-divider progress bounds remain required.

Forecast a six percent fitness improvement from Fmax
at unchanged bracket cycles, with low confidence. Acceptance requires
more than 191.37616 iterations/s, approximately 77.27 MHz at the
champion cycle count. The extra parallel subtractors, multiple registers
and wider selection network may increase area and routing enough to
negate the shorter dependency depth; EX recovery may become limiting.
Inspect the mapped recurrence and launch paths and compare the actual
median vendor Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle. A shorter
divider path alone is insufficient evidence of a fitness improvement.

formal checks, stalled RVFI cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC,

and exact schedule/hold tests for the new implementation. Preserve all
existing correctness and progress assertions and every protected file.

68.362/75.025/75.025 MHz across the three unchanged Gowin placement
options, median 75.025 MHz, using 7,264 LUT4 and 2,353 registers with
four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Canonical stalled CoreMark validated all CRCs,

champion and BELOW the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold. This supports

Keep the launch-generated, frozen multiples and parallel remainder

Deliver only this hypothesis, leaving repository RTL unchanged.

title: Speculate narrow ordered-branch verification with selective correction
motivation: The champion's reported worst path includes forwarded EX operands, branch verification and fetch/decode recovery. Delaying every branch correction in r7s2 increased cycles without enough clock benefit, and r9s2's predecoded recovery predicates still regressed. An ISA profile of the canonical marker-bounded CoreMark run counts 151,852 ordered branches; 135,261 (89.1 percent) have identical upper 24 operand bits. Their exact signed or unsigned ordering is therefore determined by an 8-bit unsigned comparison. Predict this narrow ordering in the fast recovery path and register exact full-operand validation for selective correction.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one static operand-width predictor for BLT/BGE/BLTU/BGEU verification. Speculate that rs1[31:8] equals rs2[31:8], so unsigned rs1[7:0] < rs2[7:0] predicts less-than for both signed and unsigned ordered branches. Apply funct3 bit-zero inversion for BGE/BGEU. Use this speculative branch condition, legal instruction qualification and direct-target alignment to perform the existing same-cycle comparison against the saved fetch predicted_taken bit. Correct fetch immediately if the narrow condition disagrees with that bit. BEQ/BNE retain exact equality verification; JAL/JALR retain their existing behavior. Keep the fetch table, instruction-derived direct targets and queue unchanged.

In parallel compute the exact branch condition from full architectural forwarded operands. Use the original native full-width equality and signed/unsigned comparisons in this validation path; do not require a serial upper-equality/upper-order/low-order selection network. The low-byte comparator supplies speculation only. Register a correction-pending bit with EX/MEM when the speculative effective transfer direction differs from the exact effective direction. Effective direction includes existing illegal/misaligned-target suppression: compare actual next-path choices, not raw relations. Capture the exact architectural outcome, source operands, trap and pc_next in the branch's EX/MEM entry. An unequal upper word alone is not a failure: if narrow and full comparisons give the same direction, no extra recovery occurs.

Only the narrow comparison feeds the same-cycle branch redirect. The full comparison and upper equality must not qualify execute_wait, fast redirect, fetch acceptance or ID flush. A guarded prototype that waited in EX whenever upper bits differed passed existing pipeline tests, all 53 formal checks and CoreMark CRCs, but measured only 61.549 MHz median because the validation guard lengthened stall feedback. This proposal specifically removes that guard from common-path advancement and registers recovery instead. Move conditional-branch training for ALL branch kinds to EX/MEM, using the already registered exact branch_taken, PC and effective trap status. Train once when that branch transfers from EX/MEM to MEM/WB, excluding correction_service, reset and holds. A retained correcting branch trains on its later normal transfer, not on the service edge. Never train on a younger squashed branch or from the narrow speculative result. This removes the full comparison from counter-update feedback as well as immediate redirect. Prediction table size and policy stay unchanged, but training arrives one cycle later; carry the original fetched predicted_taken bit, and preserve pre-edge lookup semantics. Update cycle-accurate predictor scoreboards to model this explicitly, retaining every architectural and table-transition assertion.

On the following cycle a registered correction-pending branch is the oldest instruction in MEM. Its registered actual pc_next overrides every younger EX correction or operand replay and redirects fetch even when imemReady is low. Flush ID/EX and empty both fetch-queue entries. Prevent the younger EX instruction from entering EX/MEM, launching or accepting an M operation, redirecting, training or making memory effects. Suppress a younger execute_wait so it cannot block this older correction. A wrong-path store has not reached MEM and must never issue a request. Reset cancels correction state.

Service this correction for exactly one edge while retaining the resolving branch's EX/MEM entry and clearing its pending bit. During this edge, make MEM/WB clear valid while retaining its old payload, using the existing forwarding-retention behavior. On the next edge the retained branch retires exactly once. This moves the branch retirement with its rare extra recovery cycle and preserves the established branch-to-divider retirement-gap bound. Do not retire the branch twice or leave a pending correction recurring. Normal branches, including correct width predictions, keep the existing stage schedule. A branch is not a memory operation, so its correction-service cycle cannot itself depend on dmemReady.

Capture correction state only on valid EX advancement with validated operand-source permissions. Source-prediction replay must precede width prediction for an instruction whose operands are invalid. Existing older dmem holds retain the complete branch and prevent advancement, training and correction capture. Gate younger M launch and completion acceptance on the registered older correction before state changes. Leave load-use interlocks, ordinary forwarding, divider/multiplier schedules and all arithmetic outputs unchanged.

Bound every new speculative taken path. Reuse IF's full-width PC-plus-direct-immediate eligibility calculation, independently of the direction counter, and carry one direct_target_eligible bit with the exact token through both queue entries, if_id_t and id_ex_t. Eligibility requires word-aligned source and target PCs in [0, 0x00100000), after full-width addition. An ordered branch may use a speculative taken narrow result only when this saved bit is true; otherwise speculate fall-through and let registered exact validation repair any real transfer. Do not compute this bounds predicate after the EX comparator, truncate targets, or confuse eligibility with predicted_taken. This prevents an actually untaken branch with an out-of-range target from causing a new speculative out-of-bounds fetch.

Use actual full-operand outcomes for RVFI and traps, including taken misaligned branches. A speculative taken choice must be suppressed for a misaligned direct target even if the actual branch is untaken; both architectural and speculative next paths then fall through, with the actual trap bit determined only by the true condition. Preserve full 32-bit target addition, all fetch range checks, nret=1, exact default-illegal decode, retirement order, bounded memory accesses and all canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks.

The profile also found ideal sequential branch misses of 51,857 for the current bimodal table versus 38,052 for a much larger 1,024-entry gshare table. Those counts omit queue timing and are not RTL cycle measurements; they motivate targeting verification timing rather than table size. The proposed width speculation is program independent and must not contain benchmark PCs, operand constants or profiling-derived exception tables.

Forecast 6 percent higher fitness with low confidence, from shorter common branch verification. Selective correction adds cycles only when the speculative effective direction is wrong; arbitrary code may fail the width prediction much more frequently. Placement, validation/training routing and the remaining divider/ALU paths are material risks. Measure actual bracket cycles and all three vendor placement options. Acceptance requires more than 191.37616 iterations/s. Preserve all existing liveness and retirement-gap assertions; do not weaken checks to accommodate the new schedule.

Experimental limits: an 8-bit speculative prototype retaining EX-stage exact training passed all 53 unchanged formal checks and existing pipeline suites, validated canonical CoreMark, and measured 4,055,597 bracket cycles at 71.136/72.268/72.268 MHz (median 72.268), approximately 178.19 iter/s. A 16-bit version with saved target eligibility measured 4,056,188 cycles and 69.816 MHz median; it passed all 53 formal checks and existing pipeline/fetch suites after only updating their packed-field offsets. BOTH are below the 182.96 champion. Neither demonstrates the forecast. The final proposal retains the more promising 8-bit fast path, adds mandatory target eligibility, restores native full-width validation mapping and moves exact training to the registered branch boundary. This final combination has not been measured or fully verified. Its clock advantage is uncertain because the prototype's next limiting paths were the divider and ALU-to-memory paths. Implementation must pass the unchanged gates and demonstrate the required fitness gain; do not present the scratch measurements as an improvement.

title: Remove squash control from decode payload and forwarding-mask registers
motivation:
The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
bracket cycles. Its reported worst path runs from an EX/MEM result
through execute recovery and decode to a forwarding-select register.
Registered source prediction shortened operand selection, but its
eight source-mask flops still clear on flush_id, and ID/EX still clears
its complete payload on flush or invalid fetch. This broadcasts late
branch recovery into state whose contents are irrelevant for bubbles.
Earlier r3 validity-only work preceded the registered forwarding masks
and achieved gains below that round's winner. Recent comparator,
counter-update and divider changes failed to beat the current champion.
Revisit the specific control fanout at the new measured endpoint.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Factor ID/EX squashing into the instruction-valid bit alone, removing
flush and fetch validity from decode payload and registered forwarding
source-mask updates. This is one local control-fanout optimization.
Preserve all stage boundaries, instruction latencies, fetch behavior,
branch recovery timing, source priority and M-unit schedules.

In id_stage split valid from the remaining payload assignments. For
valid preserve exactly reset/flush priority, then stall hold, otherwise
capture in.valid. For every other field reset to zero, hold on stall,
otherwise capture the raw decoded instruction, register values and
metadata regardless of flush or in.valid. Do not clear payload on a
bubble and do not gate its enable with decode_accept: that would restore
the redirect dependency. A load-use flush with stall retains the old
payload but invalidates it; an unstalled redirect may capture wrong-path
payload with valid zero. Neither is an executing instruction.

In forward_unit reset source masks as before, but remove flush_id and
id_valid from their sequential update conditions. On stall_id retain
the existing behavior: dmem hold retains masks; an M/load-use hold
without stall_ex_mem performs the existing EX-to-WB source aging.
Otherwise capture the existing four-way one-hot dependency prediction
from the selected raw decode token. Masks accompanying an invalid
ID/EX entry may be nonzero and must be ignored. Never qualify the masks
with current valid or flush on their way to EX. Retain exact youngest
producer priority, separate WB ALU/load enables, retained WB forwarding
permission and the existing canceled-write replay mechanism. Remove
obsolete flush_id/id_valid ports and their core connections if unused.

This is mandatory because an invalid ID/EX payload may now retain load
control and a nonzero rd. The ID/EX write-intent input to forwarding
already includes valid and must retain that qualification. Audit all

execute_wait, ex_advance, redirect and branch training must remain
unable to act on an invalid entry. Keep EX/MEM's existing zero-control
bubble injection, including on operand replay and execute wait; memory

title: Pipeline multiply completion through MEM with load-style dependencies
motivation: The champion executes every multiply as a blocking two-edge EX operation, although its four partial products are already registered. Completion then passes through the general EX result mux and EX/MEM. Retiming the same arithmetic across EX and MEM can remove that global execution hold, remove the multiplier completion input from the EX/address-result cone, and let independent instructions follow a multiply. Recent divider and branch-recovery changes have exposed competing ALU/address and branch-feedback timing limits, so a change to the existing execution-stage ownership is more promising than another branch-comparator rewrite.

Completion then passes through the general EX result mux and EX/MEM. Retiming the same arithmetic across EX and MEM can remove that global execution hold, remove the multiplier completion input from the EX/address-result cone, and let independent instructions follow a multiply. hypothesis.hypothesis:
Turn multiplication into a two-stage pipelined execution path using the existing EX and MEM boundaries. EX captures the four signed 17-by-17 partial products on the same edge that the MUL instruction enters EX/MEM. In the following cycle the existing carry-save recombination produces the architectural product and MEM/WB captures the selected low or high half. The instruction retires through the unchanged single WB boundary. Independent younger instructions may enter EX immediately; only a true dependent consumer needs the existing one-cycle load-style interlock. Keep division's blocking eight-service-edge schedule and all ordinary instruction stage boundaries unchanged.

Allow the multiplier to accept a new operation on the same edge its previous result is accepted by MEM. Register partial products, signedness/result selection and ALTOPS operands as one token; the pre-edge old result belongs to the older MEM instruction, while new partials belong to the younger EX instruction after the edge. An unaccepted result remains stable. The core launches only on valid, legal, advancing EX work with verified forwarding sources and no older dmem hold. Match launch exactly to EX/MEM insertion; wrong-path, replayed, reset and held instructions must not launch. Reset cancels pending work. Preserve the standalone multiplier's current blocking handshake through a default-off pipelining parameter, or an equivalent separate internal pipeline implementation, so existing unit assertions are not weakened.

Associate multiplier completion with the corresponding valid legal MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU in EX/MEM. Accept it exactly when that instruction transfers to MEM/WB, never from the younger ID/EX instruction's opcode. There is at most one multiply result awaiting MEM because dispatch and EX/MEM are in order. If MEM cannot advance, retain both its instruction token and multiplier partials. An older stalled load/store prevents the multiply from launching; once the multiply reaches MEM it is not itself a dmem transaction. Consecutive independent multiplies can exchange old completion and new launch on every edge without overwriting either result.

Route the completed product into the existing MEM/WB read_data result bank, selecting it instead of load extraction only for the valid multiply in MEM. title: PC-only direct-target prediction with decode identity validation
motivation: The current predictor feeds fetched instruction bits through a full-width target adder and eligibility checks into the fetch PC. Prior r2s2 cached targets but required general next-PC comparison in EX; r3s2 instead gained from exact direct targets and direction-only recovery. Recent changes to EX verification and recovery latency have regressed. Use a cached direct-target prediction independent of instruction data, with precise target-identity validation in decode, so EX retains its established direction-only check.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 64-entry direct-mapped direct-target predictor indexed by fetch PC[7:2]. Each entry holds valid, source tag PC[19:8], target[19:2], a signed immediate identity key imm[20:1], and conditional-versus-JAL kind. Only aligned source PCs and full-width targets in [0,0x00100000) may be installed. Keep the current 64-entry two-bit direction table and its EX training schedule. On a tagged hit, predict the cached target for JAL or when the conditional direction counter predicts taken. On a miss predict PC+4. JALR is never installed. Source range/alignment, PC tag, entry validity, cached kind and the direction counter determine the IF prediction; raw imem_data must not qualify the fetch target selection. Remove the IF immediate-target adder entirely, including miss fallbacks.

Carry the cached immediate identity key and cached kind with the exact fetched token through both queue entries and the empty-queue bypass, alongside predicted_taken. A token's metadata must use the same pre-edge cache contents as its PC decision, including simultaneous lookup and replacement. Unpredicted tokens need no valid identity key. Do not add a stage, disable the fall-through bypass, or hold fetch for validation. Use resettable valid bits with unreset payload arrays and a banked memory-friendly implementation. The logical cache state is 3328 bits (64 times 52), excluding the unchanged direction counters.

In ID validate every predicted-taken token against its actual instruction. Positively recognize a legal conditional branch or JAL, verify the cached kind, and compare the actual sign-extended B/J immediate[20:1] to the saved key. The immediate must be fully represented: a B immediate is sign-extended to the same 21-bit signed domain as JAL before dropping its implicit zero bit. Source PC identity was checked in IF. Equal source PC, immediate and direct-transfer kind guarantee the exact same target; changes to branch source registers or legal branch funct3 do not require a miss because they cannot change that target. Illegal branch funct3, JALR and non-control instructions fail validation. This avoids both a target adder and a full next-PC comparator in decode; it also keeps a general target comparison out of EX.

When a predicted-taken token fails identity validation AND is actually accepted into ID/EX, redirect IF to that token's full 32-bit PC+4 and invalidate both younger queue entries. Accept the current instruction normally, but store predicted_taken=0 in its ID/EX entry. Do not replay the current instruction or reread its instruction memory: accepting it once prevents stale entries or symbolic changing instructions from causing an endless refetch loop. EX then resolves this instruction using the original direction-only machinery. A real taken branch, JAL or JALR can produce a later normal EX redirect; a non-control or illegal instruction follows its normal sequential/trap behavior. A successful validation retains the fetched predicted_taken bit exactly.

This decode correction is NOT an EX flush. Separate the two recovery sources: an older EX redirect or operand replay has priority, kills ID acceptance and retains its existing ID/EX flush behavior. A decode identity correction flushes IF occupancy and corrects the fetch PC while allowing that same accepted instruction and its forwarding selectors to enter EX. Qualify decode correction with actual decode acceptance, so load-use interlocks, older data-memory stalls and M-unit holds defer it. The combined redirect sent to IF must not feed back into hazard_unit's decode_accept or flush_id; otherwise it would suppress the very acceptance that authorizes the decode correction and form a loop. Compute decode correction after the existing EX-only acceptance decision. Reset wins over everything. IF correction still overrides an unready instruction bus.

Train the target predictor once from a valid legal direct transfer advancing from EX/MEM to MEM/WB. Use its existing registered PC, instruction, branch_target and final trap-qualified control. branch_target is the full PC+immediate sum for both branches and JAL. Decode the immediate identity key from this registered instruction with wiring only. Check source and target high bits and alignment before narrowing the stored target; never wrap an out-of-range target into memory. Install eligible untaken conditional branches as well as taken ones. Exclude JALR, bubbles, illegal/faulting transfers, reset and held entries. A branch already in MEM is older than a younger EX or ID redirect and must still train when advancing. Existing exact EX direction-counter training remains unchanged. No second cache write port or decode-side invalidation is needed for correctness: stale entries are always checked against the actual accepted instruction, and subsequent legal direct transfers refresh them.

Preserve full architectural arithmetic and trap handling in EX, actual RVFI pc_next and operands, single-channel nret=1 IO, retirement order, load-use behavior, forwarding replay, M schedules, bounded addresses and all canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks. A cached speculative target is always aligned and bounded even when its instruction identity is stale. A wrong-path store must be removed before it reaches EX/MEM. The new ID correction must not suppress the older resolving instruction, train a squashed token, lose a queue entry, duplicate retirement or block forward progress under arbitrary symbolic code.

The expected benefit is shorter fetch prediction timing without the full EX next-PC comparison of r2s2. The main risks are the new decode-correction path through the empty-queue bypass, cache lookup routing, cold/conflict misses, and unchanged divider/ALU timing limits. Forecast 6 percent higher fitness with low confidence. The final arrangement is unmeasured; acceptance still requires more than 191.37616 iterations/s, approximately 77.27 MHz at the champion's 4037538 bracket cycles, with the clock requirement increasing proportionally if cycles rise.

Evidence and limits: a scratch cache with full instruction equality gating prediction directly in IF validated canonical stalled CoreMark but measured 4044158 bracket cycles and only 69.247/68.725/68.725 MHz across Gowin placements. It is a regression and is not the proposed validation boundary. It shows modest miss overhead but no clock advantage. The final proposal moves a compact immediate/kind identity check to accepted decode and makes the speculative IF target independent of imem_data; that combination has not been built or verified. Do not claim measured improvement from the scratch result. Run unchanged formal and real/ALTOPS unit suites, stalled RVFI cosim, canonical CoreMark validation and all vendor placements on the final implementation; preserve existing liveness and retirement-gap assertions.

title: Remove squash and bubble control from wide pipeline payload updates
motivation: The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz with 4,037,538 CoreMark bracket cycles. Vendor timing reproduced the 73.869 MHz result and shows forwarding-mask to branch-recovery to ID/EX clear feedback; nearby candidates also become limited by ALU-to-memory paths. The r11 validity-only decode proposal changed ID/EX and forwarding masks but left EX/MEM's wide bubble clearing in place and regressed 1.32 percent. The r8 result-routing proposal retained inactive EX payload, requiring a bubble-dependent payload enable, and bundled other routing changes. The remaining opportunity is to remove bubble-dependent data gating at BOTH existing payload boundaries without changing the forwarding-mask implementation.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Separate validity and side-effect controls from the wide fetch-queue, ID/EX and EX/MEM payload update conditions. Let payload data capture whenever its stage is not held, even when the token is invalid, flushed or waiting for an M result. This is one control-fanout and input-mux micro-optimization applied consistently to the existing payload register boundaries. There is no extra pipeline stage, changed instruction latency, new speculation policy or altered branch comparator.

In id_stage retain synchronous reset of the complete bundle. Otherwise update valid with the exact existing priorities: flush clears it even when stalled; stall retains it; ordinary capture takes in.valid. All other fields, including decoded controls, capture the current raw selected token whenever !stall, independent of flush and in.valid. During stall they retain their previous values. Never introduce decode_accept or a bubble-dependent payload enable, since those would restore the late recovery path. Qualify the core hazard connection's id_ex_mem_read with id_ex_w.valid, because invalid ID/EX payload may contain a load. Retain the existing valid qualification on producer write intent and all executing-instruction consumers.

In ex_stage retain reset clearing and dmem-stall holding of the complete EX/MEM register. On every other edge capture ALL non-control payload fields unconditionally using their existing expressions: PC, ALU/M/link result, raw store operand, register addresses, forwarded RVFI operands, resolved PC/branch metadata and instruction. Independently, clear ctrl and valid when operands_invalid || execute_wait || !in.valid; otherwise capture ctrl_with_trap and in.valid. Do not retain inactive payload on a bubble: that would put execute_wait, replay or validity back on its write enable. Valid and side-effect controls must still become zero on every bubble, replay and incomplete M operation. Early captures of an incomplete M result are harmless only with those controls and valid cleared; the actual completion edge still captures the correct held result and operand snapshots.

Apply the same separation to IF queue payloads. The queue already invalidates tokens through occupancy, but its payload assignments are still inside the reset/redirect branch and depend on redirect-qualified fetch_accept/dequeue. Export a payload_dequeue permission from hazard_unit equal to head_valid && !load_use_hazard && !dmem_stall && !execute_wait, without redirect. This permission is ONLY a payload-write hint; it must never pop occupancy, advance PC, acknowledge a fetch, or admit a real instruction by itself.

No payload write is gated by redirect, reset, imem_ready or true decode_accept. For each token that becomes live, the unchanged occupancy transition guarantees that the correct ready-bus token or old tail was captured. title: Use replicated distributed-RAM register storage with reset-valid tags
motivation:
The champion's banked flop register file removed the old inferred-BSRAM
read bottleneck in r7s1, but it stores 992 resettable data bits and reads
them through two wide selection trees. The core now uses 5,310 LUT4 and
1,929 registers. Preserve r7/r8's registered operand and four-source
forwarding boundaries while replacing only register storage with small
replicated asynchronous LUT RAMs. Separate reset validity from data so
RAM inference does not reintroduce either data-reset flops or synchronous
BSRAM reads. This structural storage alternative has not been evaluated
in the logged structural attempts.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's banked flop register file removed the old inferred-BSRAM
read bottleneck in r7s1, but it stores 992 resettable data bits and reads
them through two wide selection trees. The core now uses 5,310 LUT4 and
1,929 registers. Preserve r7/r8's registered operand and four-source
forwarding boundaries while replacing only register storage with small

RAM inference does not reintroduce either data-reset flops or synchronous

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 31 independently resettable flop words in reg_file with
two identical storage replicas, one for each combinational read port.
Partition each replica into two 16-word by 32-bit banks selected by
architectural address bit 4. Both replicas receive each accepted
nonzero-register write, with the low four address bits selecting a
word and the high bit enabling exactly one bank. Read both banks of
the selected replica asynchronously, then select the required bank.
Use inference-friendly unreset arrays and Gowin's distributed RAM
attribute, and verify that the vendor implementation actually uses
RAM16 resources instead of BSRAM or a large flop/mux implementation.
Keep the synthesizable behavioral arrays as the functional source for
simulation and formal; do not substitute an unrelated verification model.

Add 31 resettable written-valid bits, one per architectural register
x1..x31. Synchronous reset clears only those bits. It also suppresses
data-array writes on the reset edge. A permitted write sets its valid
bit and updates both storage copies atomically. Reads of an invalid
register return zero regardless of stale or uninitialized RAM payload.
A second reset must hide all previously written payload without a
scrub loop, added reset latency or assumption about FPGA RAM power-up.
x0 remains a constant zero and cannot acquire a valid bit or a write.

Preserve the existing write-first combinational bypass exactly:
w_en && w_addr != 0 && w_addr == rs_addr selects w_data, ahead of
stored-data validity, independently on both ports. This includes a
same-cycle write to a previously invalid register and simultaneous
dual-port reads of the write destination. Keep reset behavior aligned
with the existing interface, whose combinational bypass is not gated
by reset even though the reset edge suppresses architectural writes.
Implement the final read selection as three mutually exclusive lanes:
bank0 enabled by !bypass && valid[rs] && !rs[4], bank1 enabled by
!bypass && valid[rs] && rs[4], and w_data enabled by bypass. Combine
the enabled words in a balanced parallel OR; do not cascade a bank
mux, a zero-validity mux and a final WB mux on the 32-bit data path.
Qualify each bank word with a conditional expression that returns
literal zero when disabled, rather than X & 0 masking, so uninitialized
payload never leaks during four-state simulation. The bypass wins
without depending on the stored valid bit.

Keep both asynchronous read ports and the existing ID/EX operand
capture edge. No extra pipeline stage, synchronous read conversion,
multi-pumping, clock-domain change, altered WB timing, or new hazard
is permitted. Retain the current four-way predicted forwarding masks,
EX/MEM versus WB priority, separate registered WB ALU/load values,
canceled-write replay, retained forwarding during dmem holds and
captured operands during blocking M execution. The storage change
must be architecturally and cycle-for-cycle transparent.

This is one structural register-storage hypothesis. Leave the ALU,
divider recurrence, multiplier schedule, branch predictor, fetch queue,
load-use policy and bus handshake unchanged. Preserve nret=1, all core
ports, decoder legality, trap discipline, memory bounds, contiguous
RVFI retirement, all arithmetic and bounded-progress assertions, and
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/MMIO-bracket checks. Do not change any
protected evaluation file or use synthesis-only architectural behavior.

The opportunity is lower storage/read-selection area and shorter
local operand reads, with less routing pressure around EX forwarding
and the divider. Unlike the original BSRAM-backed register file, these
shallow LUT RAM banks have asynchronous reads before the existing
ID/EX boundary. Inspect mapped RAM type and the retained boundary;
fewer RTL registers alone is not evidence of a better implementation.
RAM placement, valid-bit selection and the write-first mux may instead
hurt timing, and the unchanged divider/branch paths may cap the gain.

Forecast six percent fitness improvement with low confidence. Expect
exactly 4,037,538 bracket cycles for ten iterations under the existing
stall streams. Acceptance requires more than 191.37616 iterations/s,
approximately 77.27 MHz at that cycle count; the forecast is not a
measured winning score. Judge the complete vendor placement median and actual
CoreMark throughput. Run existing register-file tests, full real and
ALTOPS pipeline suites, unchanged formal and RVFI cosimulation gates,
and canonical stalled CoreMark validation on the final implementation.
Prototype evidence: the replicated-RAM storage with a serial bank,
validity and bypass output selection passed the unchanged canonical
CoreMark validator at exactly 4,037,538 cycles, no out-of-bounds access
and all expected CRCs. It mapped to 4,180 LUT4, 968 registers, 32 RAM16
resources, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Its placement frequencies were
66.848/68.209/68.209 MHz, a regression. That prototype is not evidence
of a fitness gain. The final proposal additionally flattens the output
selection as described above; its timing and full formal validation
remain unestablished. The six-percent forecast is low confidence and
requires a substantial clock recovery, not just the proven area saving.
Deliver only this hypothesis; repository RTL remains unchanged.

title: Predict load/store address-region stability with precise carry repair
motivation:
Critical paths include forwarded operands through EX arithmetic to the
memory address port. The r6s0 history showed that isolating effective
addresses from general ALU results can expose timing headroom. Branch
direction accuracy offers little remaining throughput headroom: trace
modeling reduced conditional misses from 51857 to 39799 with a larger
hashed table, insufficient alone for the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.
Instead predict that a load/store's signed 12-bit offset leaves its
base address's upper 16 bits unchanged, verify the carry, and repair
uncommon region crossings before any memory request.

hypothesis.motivation:
Critical paths include forwarded operands through EX arithmetic to the
memory address port. The r6s0 history showed that isolating effective
addresses from general ALU results can expose timing headroom. Branch
direction accuracy offers little remaining throughput headroom: trace
modeling reduced conditional misses from 51857 to 39799 with a larger

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one static address carry predictor for legal LOAD and STORE
instructions. Predict that effective_addr stays in the same 64 KiB
region as forwarded rs1. Compute the 17-bit unsigned low sum
L = {0, rs1[15:0]} + {0, imm[15:0]}, using the existing fully
sign-extended I/S immediate. Capture {rs1[31:16], L[15:0]} as the
predicted effective_addr in EX/MEM, plus address_carry_miss =
L[16] XOR imm[31] and address_correction_negative = imm[31].
A signed 12-bit displacement crosses at most one region boundary.
On a miss the exact upper half is base[31:16]-1 for a negative
displacement, or base[31:16]+1 otherwise. Arithmetic wraps only at
the architectural 32-bit boundary, never at the one-megabyte limit.
Use post-forward rs1 and preserve canceled-producer operand replay.

Add a distinct effective_addr field to EX/MEM and use it for all MEM
addresses, alignment checks, byte-lane selection and RVFI memory
address reporting. Keep ordinary ALU and M results in alu_result.
For loads/stores alu_result may be zero: loads obtain rd data through
mem_to_reg and stores do not write rd. Structurally exclude the full
general ALU result from the memory address cone; a mux that retains
the old wide ALU address path would defeat this predictor's timing
purpose. Keep other integer arithmetic, branch/JALR target generation,
branch prediction, forwarding latency and M schedules unchanged.

A valid legal aligned memory instruction with its registered carry
miss set requests one internal repair cycle in MEM. Suppress BOTH
dmem read enable and all write enables on that cycle regardless of
io_dmemReady. Treat repair as a memory wait through the existing
hazard machinery: hold ID/EX and the EX/MEM instruction, clear only
MEM/WB.valid while retaining its forwarding payload, and prevent
younger advancement, redirects, training and M launches. No
speculative memory transaction is sent to the external bus.

On the repair edge permit exactly one special update to the held
EX/MEM entry: increment/decrement effective_addr[31:16] according to
the saved correction sign, preserve its low half and all other
instruction fields, and clear address_carry_miss. The repair adder
consumes registered state and is separated from the low-half sum
by a clock edge; never put it combinationally on the normal memory
address output. Clearing the miss bit prevents repeated repair
even if io_dmemReady stays low. The corrected instruction subsequently
follows the original bus handshake and retires once. Reset overrides
repair. A younger branch or operand replay waits behind this older
held instruction. Correction is permitted during an external bus
stall because all memory request enables are suppressed.

Low address bits are exact before repair. Misaligned accesses must
take the original alignment trap without issuing a request or
requiring repair; preserve suppressed load writeback and zero RVFI
memory masks. Invalid, illegal and nonmemory entries never request
repair. Do not hide an architectural out-of-range effective address,
truncate it to main memory, or consume io_dmemRData during repair.
An unrequested speculative value may appear on io_dmemAddr during
repair; only the corrected address may be used for a transaction
or retiring nonzero RVFI memory masks. Preserve exact once-only
training, memory effects, retirement and source-operand reporting.

The common address path becomes forwarding plus a 16-bit sum, with
its upper half copied from the base. No learned table or program-
specific address assumption is required. A correct prediction adds
no cycle; a crossing costs one internal cycle before the normal
handshake. Clock improvement must exceed repair overhead and added
register/routing costs. Other ALU/divider paths may cap Fmax, so the
forecast has low confidence. This final address-predictor RTL has
not been built or timed during hypothesis generation.

Preserve nret=1, public IO, exact traps, x0, retirement order,
wrong-path suppression and every bounds/CRC/UART/marker requirement.
Run unchanged formal including liveness and pc_fwd, real and ALTOPS
pipeline tests, stalled RVFI cosim and canonical CoreMark validation.
Check that repairs still meet the existing symbolic progress window;
do not alter formal depths or retirement-gap assertions. Measure
all Gowin placements and marker-bracketed cycles. Acceptance requires
fitness above 191.37616 iterations/s: approximately 77.27 MHz at
4037538 cycles, increasing proportionally with additional cycles.

title: Select PC updates through exclusive redirect and fetch data lanes
motivation:
The champion reaches 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
CoreMark bracket cycles. Its recorded timing path runs from an EX/MEM
result through EX and IF back to decode forwarding controls. Recent
comparator, register-file and wide-payload-clearing changes regressed.
The current redirect destination also depends on late actual_taken,
even though a direction correction necessarily reverses the saved
prediction. This redundant late data selection is a smaller remaining
opportunity than changing the branch comparison or pipeline boundary.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion reaches 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
CoreMark bracket cycles. Its recorded timing path runs from an EX/MEM
result through EX and IF back to decode forwarding controls. Recent
comparator, register-file and wide-payload-clearing changes regressed.
The current redirect destination also depends on late actual_taken,
even though a direction correction necessarily reverses the saved
prediction. This redundant late data selection is a smaller remaining
opportunity than changing the branch comparison or pipeline boundary.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Remove actual_taken from the correction-target data mux. Retain the
existing replay, ex_advance, actual_taken, redirect, branch comparison,
target arithmetic, traps and training equations exactly. Change only
the destination expression to:
  replay ? in.pc :
  in.predicted_taken ? (in.pc + 32'd4) :
  in.ctrl.is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target.

On every non-replay redirect, the existing condition proves
actual_taken != in.predicted_taken. Therefore !actual_taken equals
in.predicted_taken precisely whenever IF consumes this destination.
Both the fallthrough and taken destinations can be selected before
dynamic branch operands resolve. The existing redirect signal still
performs the final same-cycle PC selection and queue/decode squash.
When redirect is false this internal destination is not consumed and
need not equal the old unused value. No predicted target is trusted,
no new speculation is introduced, and no new register is required.

In IF, flatten the remaining redirect-versus-fetch target mux into
  three mutually exclusive word lanes. Define er=redirect && !reset,
  ed=fetch_accept && predict_taken, and el=fetch_accept && !predict_taken.
  Form next_pc=(redirect_target & {32{er}}) |
               (direct_target & {32{ed}}) |
               ((pc+32'd4) & {32{el}}).
  Keep reset as the first PC-register priority; otherwise capture next_pc
  when redirect || fetch_accept and retain PC on every other edge.
  fetch_accept already excludes redirect and reset, so the three lanes
  are exclusive. Preserve fetch_accept, occupancy, queue payload updates,
  predictor lookup/training and all other IF equations exactly. This and
  EX's saved-prediction substitution optimize one PC destination-selection
  cone. Keep EX's replay/target ternary; do not expand it into another
  masked-OR network, which regressed in a scratch trial.

Keep consumer replay as the highest-priority destination, independent
of the saved direction. Preserve JAL/JALR selection, JALR bit-zero
clearing, full 32-bit PC arithmetic, misaligned-target traps, illegal
instruction behavior and exact RVFI pc_next. Use the prediction bit
carried with the current ID/EX instruction, never a fresh table read.
Preserve its existing reset, flush and hold behavior and every M-unit,
forwarding, memory-handshake and retirement rule. Do not change the
predictor, stage boundaries, queue policy or nret=1 public interface.

This is solely a combinational correction-target mux optimization.
The earlier r9s1 proposal registered a wide correction target together
with multiple outcome/recovery/training controls and regressed to
70.837 MHz. This proposal uses the existing prediction register and
existing adders, without that extra state or control restructuring.
The intended gain is removal of the operand-comparison-to-wide-target
data path, not fewer instructions or altered prediction accuracy.

Check equivalence of the consumed redirect destination for all
prediction/actual/replay combinations. Exercise every conditional
branch predicate and direction, predicted and unpredicted JAL, JALR,
taken/untaken misaligned targets, canceled-producer replay, independent
bus holds, queue occupancy and reset. Require identical accepted fetch
PCs, squashes, RVFI operands/traps/next-PC/order and once-only memory
effects. Preserve all existing assertions and run unchanged formal,
real/ALTOPS pipeline, reference-ISS cosimulation and canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART/marker validation. Expect exactly 4,037,538 bracket cycles for
the same inputs and stall sequences.

Forecast five percent fitness improvement with low confidence, solely
from Fmax. Acceptance requires more than 191.37616 iterations/s, about
77.27 MHz at unchanged cycles. Gowin might already exploit this
conditional equivalence, or the redirect control fanout, divider and
ordinary ALU paths might dominate. Measure the prescribed vendor
placement median; the forecast is not a measured gain.

A scratch prototype of this exact EX substitution and three-lane IF
selection measured 73.689 MHz in vendor placement option 1, using 5,418
LUT4, 1,929 registers, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. This is slightly BELOW
the champion and below the acceptance threshold, not a demonstrated gain.
The simpler EX-only precursor reached 73.283 MHz and passed the existing
real/ALTOPS pipeline suites, all eight selftest/random reference-ISS
comparisons with and without bus stalls, and canonical CoreMark at
4,037,538 bracket cycles. That correctness evidence applies only to the
precursor. Extra EX target flattening, comparator rewrites, broad result
predecode and a separate address register were slower and are excluded.
The five-percent estimate is a low-confidence goal for final physical
mapping; the measured prototype does not establish it. Full prescribed
median timing and unchanged correctness gates remain mandatory.

title: Absorb fetch stalls with an eight-entry instruction queue
motivation:
The two-entry fall-through instruction queue improved fitness in r4s1,
but it can retain only two instructions during an eight-cycle division
or other backend holds. Later instruction-bus stalls still starve decode.
Recent structural attempts at multiplier pipelining, register storage,
branch retiming and divider parallelism did not exceed the acceptance
margin; their timing frequently moved between EX recovery and division.
Increasing instruction buffering instead targets cycles at the existing
pipeline boundaries, without lengthening instruction service schedules.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the two-entry fetch queue with exactly eight complete instruction
tokens, retaining the existing empty-queue fall-through path. Store PC,
instruction and the fetch-time predicted_taken bit together. Preserve the
registered head and use constant-index shift-register storage behind it:
a dequeue advances stored tokens by one slot, and an accepted fetch writes
the slot selected by occupancy minus the simultaneous stored dequeue.
When an empty queue's accepted bus token is consumed directly, do not
store a duplicate. Decode sees the oldest stored token whenever nonempty.

Preserve independent fetch acceptance: occupancy < 8 && imem_ready,
qualified by reset and redirect exactly as today. A full queue does not
accept a replacement on its dequeue edge. In particular, do not introduce
decode_accept or EX readiness into the fetch-PC advance enable. Advance
PC and run direct prediction only for accepted bus tokens. Keep the
predictor, full-width target calculation, target bounds, pre-edge counter
lookup, same-index training and raw instruction visibility unchanged.
The queue may fill during load-use, dmem and blocking M holds. Redirect
invalidates every buffered token and overrides an unready instruction
bus; reset cancels all buffered work. Payload need not reset, but validity
must prevent stale or unknown tokens from executing after reset/squash.

This is solely a structural increase in elastic fetch capacity. Preserve
all EX/MEM/WB stages, four-source forwarding and canceled-write replay,
real and ALTOPS arithmetic, existing M service schedules, nret=1 and all
public ports. Preserve decoder legality, traps, memory bounds, contiguous
RVFI order, once-only effects, and the existing formal progress window.
Do not add a cache, predictor policy, instruction specialization or
benchmark-dependent behavior. Keep the empty bypass so ready-bus recovery
and the nine-cycle branch-to-divider retirement bound remain unchanged.

Forecast six percent fitness improvement with low confidence. The
champion uses 4,037,538 bracket cycles and 73.869 MHz; at unchanged Fmax,
acceptance requires fewer than about 3,859,979 cycles for ten iterations.
Measure actual canonical stalled CoreMark cycles and the median Gowin
placement frequency, requiring fitness above 191.37616 iterations/s.
More capacity may only rarely help, and occupancy control, payload
enables or added routing may lower Fmax. Fewer cycles alone is not a win.
Run unchanged arithmetic, decoder, formal and RVFI cosimulation gates,

title: Train a compact bimodal predictor from fetched counter snapshots
motivation: The current direction table reads counters at both the fetch PC and the resolving branch index: training performs an asynchronous read-modify-write of the current entry. This adds selection and feedback logic and inhibits a simple one-read/one-write memory implementation. Prior recovery restructuring regressed and the PC-only target cache timed out in formal, so preserve instruction-derived targets and same-cycle EX correction. A scratch 32-entry folded-PC two-bit table reduced canonical CoreMark cycles to 4,034,312 but reached only 72.658 MHz in placement option 1. A one-bit version removed the training read, inferred six RAM16 resources and reached 75.191 MHz in that option, but loses hysteresis. The proposed single predictor mechanism removes the training read while retaining two-bit direction state.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 64-entry bimodal table with a 32-entry, two-bit snapshot-trained direction predictor. Index fetch and training with PC[6:2] XOR PC[11:7]. At fetch capture the complete raw two-bit counter alongside the existing predicted_taken bit in the exact bus token, both queue entries and the empty-queue bypass. Propagate this snapshot through IF/ID and ID/EX. It is separate from predicted_taken: target eligibility and instruction class can suppress predicted_taken even when the raw counter MSB is one.

At the existing valid, legal, nonfaulting EX branch advancement, saturate the saved counter toward the exact branch outcome and unconditionally write that resulting two-bit value to the resolving branch's hashed index. For taken use min(snapshot+1,3); for not-taken use max(snapshot-1,0). Write saturation endpoints too: suppressing an endpoint write based on the saved value would leave a potentially different aliased current entry unchanged. Do not read counters[training_index], compare current and saved states, forward a newer update, or add a second read port. The deliberate microarchitectural prediction is that the fetched counter remains a useful estimate of its current state. Intervening branches can make the snapshot stale; accepting this approximate learning is safe because predictor state never authorizes architectural effects. Every actual instruction still resolves against its own saved predicted_taken with exact forwarded operands and full architectural target arithmetic.

Use one asynchronous lookup port and one synchronous training write port, explicitly implemented as two banks of sixteen entries. Split the two state bits into independent unreset one-bit memory planes in each bank (four 16x1 arrays total). Index[4] chooses the bank and index[3:0] the word; enable writes to exactly one bank and write both planes atomically. Use a separate 32-bit resettable valid bitmap. Logical lookup is stored state when valid, otherwise 01; reset clears all validity in one edge and suppresses training. First training initializes both data planes before their validity becomes visible. Saturating writes use the saved logical snapshot, so they never consult uninitialized storage. No data-array reset or reset mux may remain on the memory write path. This concrete organization is intended to map to distributed RAM16, not BSRAM or resettable counter-word flops. Check the vendor mapping; do not assume inference from RTL size. Do not scrub entries over extra cycles or weaken reset checks. No new state is tied to benchmark PCs, operands, marker activity, or stall-generator phase.

Both next-PC selection and the counter snapshot captured with a fetched token use the same pre-edge lookup. A simultaneous same-index training write affects later fetches only; a stored queue token never refreshes its snapshot. If the queue is full or imem is unready, no new fetch token is accepted. A held ID/EX branch retains all metadata. Reset and corrections discard snapshots with their tokens. Train exactly once on the existing branch_train event; no training on invalid, illegal, misaligned, replayed, held, squashed or incomplete-M instructions. No rollback is needed for table writes from advancing older branches. Aliasing and stale learning may change prediction accuracy but must never change instruction identity or actual retirement.

Keep JAL prediction unconditional when its full instruction-derived target is eligible, keep JALR unpredicted, and preserve the complete full-width source/target range and alignment checks. Keep the two-entry queue, recovery edge, forwarding prediction/replay, load-use interlocks, memory handshake and M schedules unchanged. Do not introduce a cached target or a general predicted-next-PC equality check. Preserve nret=1, public IO, default-illegal decode, traps, RVFI operands/next-PC/order, bounded memory accesses, progress and all canonical CRC/UART/timing-marker gates.

The intended benefit is eliminating the indexed training-state read and enabling a compact one-read/one-write direction memory while retaining hysteresis. A sequential reference trace gave 50,576 conditional misses for the 32-entry folded two-bit policy versus 51,857 for the current table; this model does not include stale snapshots, queue timing or bus stalls and is not a prediction of final RTL cycles. Stale updates, extra token metadata, memory inference and unchanged divider/ALU/recovery paths are the main risks. Forecast six percent higher fitness with low confidence. The scratch measurements above are below the acceptance threshold and do not establish a win. Measure the final snapshot policy's actual bracket cycles and all three Gowin placements. Acceptance requires fitness above 191.37616 iterations/s; the required Fmax is 191.37616 times measured cycles divided by 10,000,000 in MHz.

Add independent cycle-accurate tests of the explicitly changed learning rule, including deliberate alias overwrite between fetch and EX, two in-flight instances of the same branch, saturation endpoints and same-edge lookup/write. Update only predictor-policy expectations and necessary packed-field offsets in existing tests; retain every architectural, progress, latency, squash and memory assertion. Run unchanged formal, real and ALTOPS pipeline tests, stalled RVFI cosimulation and the canonical CoreMark validator. No repository RTL is delivered during hypothesis generation; the hypothesis is the implementation request.

Experimental limit: a snapshot-trained precursor using a resettable 32x2 array passed the canonical CoreMark validator with all CRCs, no out-of-bounds access and 4,034,312 bracket cycles. Placement option 1 reached only 70.947 MHz, using 5,114 LUT4, 1,871 registers and zero RAM16 resources. It did not achieve the intended storage inference and is a regression, not evidence of the forecast. The final proposal therefore requires the unreset banked bit planes and reset-valid lookup above. That final storage implementation has not been timed or formally checked during hypothesis generation. Full formal and the three-placement median remain required. Do not claim acceptance from any reported scratch result.

title: Select divider remainders directly with balanced fit-bit mux trees
motivation:
The champion reaches 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
CoreMark bracket cycles. Recent r13s0 timing exposes a 68-cell divider
quotient-to-remainder path. The existing radix-8/radix-4 recurrence
computes parallel differences, decodes adjacent fit bits into one-hot
enables, masks every 32-bit candidate and ORs the words. Earlier full
radix-32 expansion failed to improve fitness. Keep the successful radix
and native subtraction mapping, and target only remainder selection.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion reaches 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
CoreMark bracket cycles. Recent r13s0 timing exposes a 68-cell divider
quotient-to-remainder path. The existing radix-8/radix-4 recurrence

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the two wide one-hot masked-OR remainder muxes in div_unit
with explicitly balanced two-way decision trees driven directly by the
already-computed fit bits. Preserve every subtraction, its width and
borrow interpretation, registered divisor multiple, digit encoder,
state transition and service edge. This is one local combinational mux
micro-optimization, not a change of divider radix or pipeline structure.

For the radix-8 result, use exactly this balanced selection topology:
  r_after8 = fit8[4]
    ? (fit8[6] ? (fit8[7] ? difference8[7][31:0] : difference8[6][31:0])
                : (fit8[5] ? difference8[5][31:0] : difference8[4][31:0]))
    : (fit8[2] ? (fit8[3] ? difference8[3][31:0] : difference8[2][31:0])
                : (fit8[1] ? difference8[1][31:0] : trial8[31:0]));
For the radix-4 result use:
  r_next = fit4[2]
    ? (fit4[3] ? difference4[3][31:0] : difference4[2][31:0])
    : (fit4[1] ? difference4[1][31:0] : trial4[31:0]);

These are three-level and two-level balanced trees, respectively; do
not write descending priority chains. Because the unsigned multiples
kD are correctly widened, fits are a monotonic thermometer vector:
fit[k+1] implies fit[k]. Each tree therefore selects precisely the
largest fitting digit, including digit zero when no multiple fits.
For D=0 every fit is true and each tree selects its largest digit.
No approximate comparison or assumption about typical operands is used.

Keep enable8/enable4 and the existing quotient-digit encoding unchanged.
Remove the now-unused masked8/masked4 declarations and assignments so
only the remainder selection topology changes. The intended physical
benefit is to bypass adjacent-fit one-hot decoding before wide data
selection and expose regular mux trees to Gowin's LUT/mux mapping.
RTL ternaries alone do not guarantee better placement; inspect the
mapped circuit and judge measured fitness.

Retain the full 36-bit and 35-bit trial subtractions, 35-bit odd
multiples, launch magnitude conversion and two narrow initial steps.
Keep six five-bit recurrence cycles and corrected EX/MEM acceptance
on service edge eight. Preserve original-operand capture, modular
INT_MIN magnitudes, all DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU signs, INT_MIN/-1, divide-by-zero
results, ignored starts while busy, stable DONE under arbitrary holds,
result acceptance and reset cancellation. Preserve ALTOPS expressions
and their control schedule exactly; real arithmetic remains excluded
under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS.

Leave ALU, multiplier, forwarding, predictor, queue, memory handshakes,
issue/retirement width and all public ports unchanged. Maintain nret=1,
decoder legality, traps, RVFI operands and order, memory side-effect
rules and every correctness/progress assertion. No protected files or
evaluation assumptions change.

Validate both trees against the existing largest-fit reference for all
nine radix-8 thermometer patterns and five radix-4 patterns, including
all-false/all-true. Exercise real recurrence thresholds kD-1/kD/kD+1,
large unsigned multiples, every quotient digit, signed extremes and
zero divisors. Compare registered quotient/remainder boundaries with
the original arithmetic and final results with an independent RV32M
integer reference. Retain exact latency and completion-hold tests.
Run real/ALTOPS divider and pipeline suites, unchanged formal and ISS
cosimulation, and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/marker validation.
Expected bracket cycles are exactly 4,037,538 for identical inputs and
bus stalls. Full formal remains an implementation-phase requirement.

Forecast five percent fitness improvement with low confidence, entirely
from Fmax. Acceptance requires more than 191.37616 iterations/s, about
77.27 MHz at unchanged cycles. Gowin may refactor both expressions into
the same network, mux routing may be slower, or branch/ALU paths may
limit the clock. No accepted gain is claimed before complete median
vendor timing. Only this hypothesis file is delivered; repository RTL
remains unchanged.

title: Register execute recovery with same-cycle target fetch
motivation:
The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
CoreMark bracket cycles. Its reported path starts at EX/MEM.alu_result
and traverses branch recovery to forwarding-register control. Registered
recovery previously failed in r7s2: it added 1.64 percent of cycles while
register-file/ALU timing limited clock improvement. The later register
and forwarding changes removed those old bottlenecks. Revisit the control
pipeline boundary, but bypass the registered correction target directly
into fetch so the extra recovery register need not cost a ready-bus cycle.
This differs from adding fetch capacity, changing prediction policy or
merely delaying recovery with another pipeline bubble.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
CoreMark bracket cycles. Its reported path starts at EX/MEM.alu_result
and traverses branch recovery to forwarding-register control. Registered
recovery previously failed in r7s2: it added 1.64 percent of cycles while
register-file/ALU timing limited clock improvement. The later register
and forwarding changes removed those old bottlenecks. Revisit the control
pipeline boundary, but bypass the registered correction target directly
into fetch so the extra recovery register need not cost a ready-bus cycle.
This differs from adding fetch capacity, changing prediction policy or
merely delaying recovery with another pipeline bubble.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Introduce a one-cycle registered EX event boundary carrying correction
valid, the complete 32-bit correction target, branch-training valid,
training index and actual outcome. Resolve operands, branches, target
alignment and canceled-write replay in EX exactly as today, but capture
the event rather than driving IF/ID/forwarding control from the current
comparison. Capture only advancing, valid, verified execution; canceled
source replay independently captures its consumer PC without admitting
that consumer to EX/MEM. Registers reset invalid, each event is delivered
once, and a recovery cycle cannot generate events from the killed younger
EX instruction. Register training as well as correction so the comparator
no longer drives the direction table's write network combinationally.

In the following recovery cycle, use the saved target as the instruction
bus address immediately: fetch_pc = recovery_valid ? recovery_target : pc.
The two-entry queue's wrong-path head is unavailable in this cycle; select
the target bus token directly, with availability determined by imemReady.
Its PC, branch-table index, immediate-derived target, prediction and PC+4
all use fetch_pc. If the target fetch is accepted, let that token enter
ID/EX on the same edge that kills the younger wrong-path EX instruction.
Advance the stored fetch PC to that target token's predicted successor.
If the bus is unready, latch recovery_target into PC, clear ID/EX to an
invalid zero-control bubble and fetch it later. Never increment past an
unaccepted target. Reset takes priority over all of this.

Flush every old queue token on recovery, but do not discard a newly
accepted target token. If accepted and consumed directly, leave occupancy
zero; if accepted but not consumed, retain exactly that complete token as
the sole queue entry. Outside recovery preserve the current fall-through
queue, conservative full refusal and fetch acceptance independent of
decode readiness. The recovery address comes only from registered state,
not from the current EX comparison. Retain full-width target arithmetic,
alignment checks and executable-range prediction checks.

Separate killing the old EX token from admitting the new target into ID.
Recovery overrides hazards and execute_wait belonging to the discarded
younger instruction; it must not flush the newly accepted target. Clear
EX/MEM controls and valid for the killed token, suppress its M launch,
completion acceptance, branch training, correction and memory effects,
and let the older resolving EX/MEM instruction advance normally to WB.
Do not hold the resolving branch for an extra retirement-service cycle.
A pending recovery must correspond to a memory-free resolving branch/jump
or to a replay whose EX/MEM entry is a bubble; assert this invariant so
recovery cannot discard an unrelated stalled memory transaction.

For target-token forwarding capture, exclude the killed current ID/EX
instruction from EX-producer write intent. The older EX/MEM instruction
advances to WB on this edge, so retain the existing MEM-permission-based
WB source prediction, including a legal JAL/JALR link value. Preserve
write-first RF bypass, youngest-writer priority, separate WB ALU/load
banks, retained WB forwarding under dmem holds and independent canceled-
write verification. Replay has priority over a branch correction when
forming an event. A killed M instruction must never start even if its
busy/result flags would otherwise request a hold.

Keep the 64-counter predictor policy and instruction-derived direct
targets. Training now applies once from the registered event, one cycle
later, using the table's current counter and normal pre-edge read/update
semantics. This timing can slightly change alias behavior and measured
cycles; it is not a new predictor. Keep ordinary integer/M execution,
load-use interlocking, M service schedules, nret=1, all public ports,
decoder legality, trap/link rules, memory bounds and ordered RVFI intact.
With ready buses, correction-target decode occurs on the same edge as in
the champion: the target-address bypass compensates for the event register.
The existing branch-to-divider and formal liveness bounds remain required.

This is a single structural retiming of recovery from EX through fetch
and target admission. The target bypass is essential to avoid the cycle
penalty of the earlier registered-recovery attempt. Its costs are a new
registered-source address mux and recovery-aware token admission; the
unchanged divider or ordinary ALU may still limit Fmax. Forecast five percent
fitness improvement with low confidence. Acceptance requires more than
191.37616 iterations/s, about 77.27 MHz if bracket cycles stay near 4,037,538.
Use actual stalled cycles and the full prescribed Gowin placement median.

Run unchanged formal, real/ALTOPS arithmetic checks, RVFI cosimulation and
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/MMIO-bracket validation. Update internal
cycle-reference models to describe registered event delivery and direct
target admission with exact cycle equality, not relaxed timing bounds.
Preserve every architectural, once-only-side-effect and progress assertion.
Cover all branch predicates, both prediction directions, target-fetch
ready/unready transitions, full-queue recovery, replay, misaligned jumps,
link forwarding, target loads/stores/M operations, wrong-path M launch
suppression, same-index training and reset around event delivery. Deliver
only this hypothesis; implementation remains a separate phase.

A scratch prototype with a wide EX/MEM kill passed canonical stalled
CoreMark at exactly 4,037,538 bracket cycles and reference-ISS cosimulation
for selftest and three random programs, with and without bus stalls.
Gowin placement frequencies were 68.415/73.878/73.878 MHz, median 73.878,
with 5,317 LUT4 and 1,970 registers. This is approximately unchanged
fitness and does NOT clear the acceptance threshold. The measured paths
moved to the ordinary ALU/address cone and divider. Thus registered
recovery plus target bypass has demonstrated latency preservation, not

title: One-hot pipelined learning for a compact agree predictor
motivation:
The current 64-entry two-bit table stores 128 state bits and performs an
indexed read-modify-write at branch resolution. Recent snapshot-trained
RAM mapping saved only 0.08% of CoreMark cycles and regressed Fmax to
67.967 MHz. A smaller one-bit predictor removes the training read and
saturation logic without snapshot metadata or validity arrays. Encoding
disagreement with the fetched branch's backward/forward bias lets
branches with opposite common directions share a useful table state.
The intended benefit is a smaller, simpler predictor circuit rather
than an assumed increase in direction accuracy.
A scratch version with immediate EX training exposed a 36-cell path
from forwarding selectors into predictor state and reached only
69.388 MHz. The proposed version therefore registers the complete
training update before the table write to break that feedback path.

hypothesis.motivation:
The current 64-entry two-bit table stores 128 state bits and performs an
indexed read-modify-write at branch resolution. Recent snapshot-trained
RAM mapping saved only 0.08% of CoreMark cycles and regressed Fmax to
67.967 MHz. A smaller one-bit predictor removes the training read and
saturation logic without snapshot metadata or validity arrays. Encoding

branches with opposite common directions share a useful table state.
The intended benefit is a smaller, simpler predictor circuit rather

from forwarding selectors into predictor state and reached only

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the existing bimodal predictor with one 32-entry one-bit agree
predictor. Its state bit means disagreement with backward-taken,
forward-not-taken bias. Index with PC[6:2] XOR PC[11:7]. Reset all 32
disagreement bits to zero in one edge. For a positively decoded legal
conditional branch, raw_direction = instruction[31] XOR disagreement[index].
For B instructions, instruction[31] is the sign of the displacement.
Keep JAL's existing unconditional taken prediction and JALR's unpredicted
behavior. Apply all existing source and full-width target range and
alignment checks after the raw direction decision; a rejected target
predicts fallthrough. Continue deriving targets from the actual fetched
instruction, never a cached target, truncated sum or aliased table entry.

On the existing valid, legal, nonfaulting advancing EX conditional-branch
training event, decode the folded index into a 32-bit one-hot update mask
and register that mask together with outcome XOR immediate sign inside
IF. Register an all-zero mask when no branch trains. On the following
edge, each entry with its registered mask bit set writes the registered
disagreement bit. Accept a new update while writing the old one, so
consecutive advancing branches never overwrite a pending update. This is a one-bit overwrite,
with no training-index state read, increment/decrement, saturation or
confidence counter. Use the resolving branch's own sign bit and PC,
never the live fetch instruction. Add one scalar EX-to-IF training-bias
connection, while retaining branch_outcome as the exact outcome for
observability. EX training outputs keep their current-cycle meanings;
only IF table updates are delayed. Existing branch_index wiring may retain six bits with
bit 5 tied to zero, or consistently use five bits internally. No new
predictor metadata is needed in IF/ID or ID/EX: the existing captured
predicted_taken bit already records the actual fetch choice.

Implement 32 separately declared resettable one-bit state flops in
constant-index generate blocks. Each flop has its own registered update
enable; there is no variable-index write statement. Select prediction
through constant-index masked terms and a balanced OR tree, with the
folded-PC equality decodes evaluated in parallel. Together with the
32-bit update mask and one data bit this uses 65 state bits. Avoid the
inferred RAM/reset-emulation topology observed in the scratch version. Do not add RAM validity bits, stale
counter snapshots, tags, an initialization sweep, or vendor primitives.
A same-edge fetch and update use the old table value for both next-PC
selection and captured predicted_taken; subsequent fetches observe the
new value. A stored queue token must never refresh its prediction after
table updates. Preserve reset precedence, once-only training, exact
queue/bypass token coherence and existing hold/squash behavior. Updates
to aliased entries may hurt accuracy but cannot affect architectural
correctness, because EX still checks each saved prediction using exact
forwarded operands and its own full-width target.

Reset clears the update mask, update data and table state. After
capture, an update describes an already resolved nonsquashed branch;
its own redirect or a later younger redirect must not cancel it. Write
it independently of current imem readiness, queue occupancy, EX holds
and dmem readiness, then clear the update mask unless another branch
advances. Never recalculate eligibility from the current EX token or
repeat an update during a pipeline hold. Keep branch correction
immediate: the new register delays only learning, not verification,
instruction execution, recovery or retirement. Delayed learning can
change subsequent direction guesses; precise EX recovery remains intact.

Keep the entire existing same-cycle recovery boundary, two-entry fetch
queue, load-use interlocks, forwarding-source prediction/replay, memory
handshakes, multiplier/divider schedules and decoder untouched. Preserve
nret=1 and every public port, exact RVFI operands/traps/next-PC/order,
memory bounds, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker validation, and all
existing formal and forward-progress requirements. This proposal changes
only branch direction learning and its compact state representation.

A sequential reference trace measured 51,857 conditional misses for the
current 64-entry bimodal policy and 70,745 for this 32-entry agree policy;
an ordinary folded-PC 32-entry one-bit policy had 71,035. These counts
exclude pipeline timing, overlapping instances, bus stalls and speculative
fetches. They establish an accuracy cost, not a measured cycle count.
The hypothesis is that deleting the second state bit, indexed training
read and saturation network reduces clock period enough to outweigh
that cost. It must not be presented as an accuracy improvement over
the champion. Forecast 6% higher fitness with low confidence. At a
0.6% cycle increase, clearing the 4.6% acceptance margin requires about
77.73 MHz. The unchanged branch recovery, ALU and divider paths, loss
of hysteresis and physical placement may prevent a win.

Preserve all architectural test assertions. Adapt only expectations
that explicitly encode the old predictor policy, including reset
prediction, index mapping, counter transitions and warm-loop timing.
Keep the existing nine-cycle branch-to-divider progress bound and
unchanged formal liveness window. Test opposite-bias aliasing: a taken
backward branch and an untaken forward branch sharing an index both
train disagreement zero. Also test two branches with conflicting
disagreement, all legal predicates, both correction directions, target
eligibility overrides, same-edge training/lookup, repeated-PC tokens,
queue-full holds, reset after training, reserved encodings, misaligned
targets, canceled-write replay and independent bus stalls. Require exact
retirement order, operands, traps and once-only memory effects.

Run the unchanged formal suite, real/ALTOPS unit and pipeline tests,
reference-ISS cosimulation, canonical stalled CoreMark validation and
prescribed three-placement Gowin median. Acceptance requires more than
191.37616 iterations/s. No implementation or timing claim is implied by
this forecast; report final measured cycles and median clock explicitly.
Experimental limitation: an indexed-array precursor with registered
training mapped to six RAM16 resources, used 5,076 LUT4 and 1,819
registers, validated canonical CoreMark at 4,060,611 bracket cycles
with no out-of-bounds accesses, and reached only 68.509 MHz in placement
option 1. It is a regression, not winning evidence. Its unchanged
branch-to-divider progress test passed. Of 27 selected pipeline tests
in each real/ALTOPS mode, 24 passed and three stopped at reset checks
that still referenced the removed 64-counter array. Those checks must
be adapted to the new reset state without weakening their intent.
The final design preserves current-cycle EX training-event signals
and pipelines only IF learning. The proposed separately enabled state flops, one-hot update
register and balanced lookup are an unmeasured implementation refinement
addressing inferred RAM/reset logic. Full correctness and median timing
remain required; do not report a demonstrated fitness improvement.
