title: Register complete ALU source choices before execute
motivation:
The successful r7s1 and r8s2 changes moved forwarding decisions before
EX, but the champion still combines each registered forwarding bit
with !is_auipc or !alu_src inside EX. Those gates feed wide operand
muxes, and the same raw forwarding controls also drive branch and
M-unit operand selection. Recent recovery and divider-mux experiments
left the ordinary ALU/address cone critical. Completing operand-source
selection at the existing ID/EX edge can remove that remaining control
layer and separate raw-source fanout from ALU-source fanout.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Register the complete five-way ALU source enables alongside the existing
four-way raw forwarding enables. This is one local operand-mux control
optimization. Preserve the pipeline, instruction latencies, predictor,
fetch queue, ALU arithmetic and M-unit schedules. Do not add an operand
data register or a new stage, change the source prediction policy, or
weaken canceled-write verification.

Export the selected ID token's positively decoded is_auipc and alu_src
from id_stage to forward_unit through internal core wiring. Use the
actual decoder outputs, including their existing illegal-instruction
behavior; do not infer them from an incomplete opcode shortcut. Form
the existing next raw mask F={WB_load,WB_ALU,EX_MEM,RF} with precisely
the current dependency comparisons, youngest-writer priority, x0
exclusion and MEM permission qualification. On the same ID/EX edge,
independently capture A={is_auipc, F1 & {4{!is_auipc}}} and
B={alu_src, F2 & {4{!alu_src}}}. Bits 0..3 retain the current source
encoding; bit 4 selects this instruction's PC for A or immediate for B.
Keep the original raw masks unchanged for branches, JALR, stores,
multiplier/divider launches, RVFI operands and permission verification.

The new masks must have exactly the original mask-register priorities:
reset or flush clears all bits; a dmem hold retains them; an invalid
ordinary capture clears them; valid decode captures the new five-way
choices. During stall_id && !stall_ex_mem, apply the existing M-wait
source aging to bits 0..3 if bit 4 is clear: an EX/MEM source becomes
WB-load or WB-ALU according to ex_mem_load, and all other raw choices
become RF, exactly as the existing raw-mask update does. If bit 4 is
set, retain the override-only mask. Never derive a held instruction's
override from the changing live decode token. Flush retains priority
over a load-use stall. Captured M operands and retained WB data continue
to supply their existing consumers exactly as before.

In EX compute alu_a and alu_b directly as balanced ORs of five masked
words driven only by these registered enables. Remove is_auipc/alu_src
qualification from each ALU forwarding lane and drive the PC/immediate
lanes from bit 4. Do not recreate a raw-rs then PC/immediate serial mux.
Keep the original raw rs1/rs2 forwarding muxes and all their consumers.
An override suppresses an ALU operand only; it must not suppress the
original raw-source permission check or change the existing replay
behavior for incidental instruction-field matches.

The intended invariant is that, for each valid held or advancing token,
new_A equals {in.ctrl.is_auipc, raw_F1 & {4{!in.ctrl.is_auipc}}}, and
new_B equals {in.ctrl.alu_src, raw_F2 & {4{!in.ctrl.alu_src}}}.
Both masks are zero on a freshly cleared bubble, and each valid mask
is one-hot. Verify these properties from reachable reset and pipeline
transitions without adding formal assumptions. They establish identical
ALU operands while moving the small override gates before the register.
The new registers carry genuinely different control from the raw masks;
do not rely on preservation attributes or artificial physical constraints.

Preserve nret=1 and all external ports, decoder default-illegal rules,
exact traps, full-width addresses, RVFI operands/next-PC/order, memory
side-effect suppression and all existing progress bounds. Keep ALTOPS
formulas, real arithmetic, eight-edge division and two-edge multiply
unchanged. No evaluation, wrapper, constraint or benchmark files change.

Expect exactly 4,037,538 canonical CoreMark bracket cycles for identical
inputs and bus stalls. Forecast 6% higher fitness with low confidence,
entirely from Fmax; acceptance requires more than 191.37616 iterations/s,
approximately 77.27 MHz at that cycle count. Added ID decode fanout,
extra mask flops and unchanged branch/divider paths may cap the gain.
Judge the prescribed three-placement Gowin median and actual CoreMark
cycles; this forecast is not a measured acceptance result.

title: Capture complete execution operands before the ID/EX boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
CoreMark bracket cycles. Structural queue enlargement and registered
recovery failed to clear the acceptance margin; recent paths still traverse
forwarding and ordinary arithmetic into the memory endpoint. Successful
r7s1/r8s2 retimed dependency controls but kept data selection inside EX.
Move the complete operand-delivery network, including PC and immediate
substitution, before the existing ID/EX edge so execution begins directly
from registered ALU and raw architectural operands. Scratch measurements
show that partial retiming is insufficient; the complete boundary matters.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 182.96 iterations/s at 73.869 MHz and 4,037,538
CoreMark bracket cycles. Structural queue enlargement and registered
recovery failed to clear the acceptance margin; recent paths still traverse
forwarding and ordinary arithmetic into the memory endpoint. Successful
r7s1/r8s2 retimed dependency controls but kept data selection inside EX.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming operand delivery is the single structural change. Capture fully
selected raw rs1/rs2 and dedicated ALU operands exec_a/exec_b at the existing
ID/EX boundary. EX then receives registered operands directly, with no
EX/MEM or MEM/WB forwarding data mux and no PC/immediate substitution mux
before its fast ALU. Preserve pipeline depth, issue rate, load-use bubbles,
M service schedules, predictor, fetch queue and in-order retirement.

Expose the current EX instruction's combinational architectural result
before EX/MEM capture: ordinary ALU result, PC+4 link, completed multiplier
result or completed divider result. Use the same value that would enter
EX/MEM.alu_result, without qualifying its data by a late redirect, trap,
advance or destination-write permission. At decode, compare each source
against the younger current ID/EX producer using its valid, decoded legal
write intent and nonzero rd. Its result has highest capture priority.
This is forwarding from a producer's combinational output into the next
instruction's operand register on the same edge the producer advances.
There must be no combinational loop: EX arithmetic depends only on its
current registered operands, never on decode's next operand values.

If no younger match, capture the current MEM producer when its nonzero
rd matches and MEM's final write permission is true. Select the existing
EX/MEM ALU result or MEM's already extracted, sign/zero-extended load word.
Expose that load word internally without changing the memory protocol or
MEM/WB banks. Otherwise capture the register-file read value, retaining
its existing same-cycle WB write-first bypass. MEM permission includes
valid, legality and alignment; a faulting load must not hide an older
architectural value. x0 never matches a producer. Use mutually exclusive
RF, EX-result, MEM-ALU and MEM-load lanes before raw operand capture.

Register dedicated exec_a and exec_b as part of the same ID/EX token.
For exec_a, substitute PC for AUIPC; otherwise use the same selected raw
rs1 source. For exec_b, substitute the decoded immediate for alu_src;
otherwise use selected raw rs2. Fold substitution into the parallel input
lane enables, adding an exclusive PC or immediate lane. Do not put a
substitution mux after ID/EX, or serially after a completed forwarding mux.
Keep raw rs1/rs2 separately for branches, stores, JALR, M launch and RVFI.
The fast ALU connects directly to exec_a/exec_b. The extra operand storage
is intentional: the version retaining EX PC/immediate muxes was slower.

Retain the existing youngest-producer permission speculation, now only as
provenance tags rather than forwarding data selectors. Register one bit
per raw source identifying capture from the current EX producer. On the
following EX cycle validate these tags against EX/MEM's actual reg_write.
If a predicted producer canceled its write, replay the consumer PC and
suppress its execution, M launch, training, memory effects and retirement,
exactly as today. Do not move final EX trap permission onto the capture
mux control path. A canceled younger writer must cause replay even when
an older matching producer exists; silently using the captured invalid
result is wrong. An older MEM source was fully checked before capture.

Preserve the load-use interlock: an immediate dependent consumer cannot
capture an EX load's address as its data. It captures the real MEM load
on the following eligible edge. An older dmem stall freezes ID/EX and
its entire operand/provenance token; unready load data is never captured
as an advancing consumer. Hold M's original ID/EX instruction until its
existing result-completion edge, so decode cannot capture an unfinished
M result. Preserve launch-time raw operand snapshots and real/ALTOPS
arithmetic. When a launched M instruction holds ID/EX while older stages
drain, clear its EX-producer provenance tags once that producer leaves;
M snapshots remain authoritative and the existing busy-qualified replay
check remains. Never resample a held instruction from the changing queue
head. Reset, redirect, load-use flush and invalid-capture priorities stay
exactly aligned across metadata, raw/ALU operands and provenance tags.

Keep MEM/WB's separate registered ALU/load results, held payload and
once-only retirement/writeback semantics. Remove only their direct EX
data-forwarding connections. Preserve nret=1, all external ports, illegal
instruction defaults, target/alignment traps, memory bounds, stable held
requests, contiguous RVFI order and every existing progress assertion.
No changes to predictor policy, arithmetic algorithms or evaluation files.

The complete scratch design, with parallel operand-input lanes and direct
registered fast-ALU inputs, measured 76.497/76.946/76.946 MHz across the
unchanged Gowin placement options: median 76.946 MHz, 6,132 LUT4, 1,985 FF,
zero LUT-RAM, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Its divider recurrence became the
reported worst path. At the expected unchanged 4,037,538 cycles this is
about 4.17 percent above the champion, BELOW the 4.6 percent acceptance

title: Share hysteresis across a banked 64-entry direction predictor
motivation:
The champion's 64-entry bimodal predictor avoids many branch corrections,
but stores two state bits per direction entry and uses indexed saturating
updates. Recent 32-entry snapshot and one-bit agree predictors regressed
Fmax; the agree variant also increased sequential-reference misses from
51,857 to 70,745. Retain all 64 direction entries and retain hysteresis,
while sharing only the strength bits. This targets predictor area and
training timing without repeating a loss of direction capacity or adding
speculative operand comparisons to the execute stage.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's 64-entry bimodal predictor avoids many branch corrections,
but stores two state bits per direction entry and uses indexed saturating
updates. Recent 32-entry snapshot and one-bit agree predictors regressed
Fmax; the agree variant also increased sequential-reference misses from
51,857 to 70,745. Retain all 64 direction entries and retain hysteresis,
while sharing only the strength bits. This targets predictor area and
training timing without repeating a loss of direction capacity or adding
speculative operand comparisons to the execute stage.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 64 ordinary two-bit counters with a shared-hysteresis bimodal
predictor: 64 prediction bits P and 16 strength bits H. Index P with
PC[7:2], exactly as today. H[j] is shared by P[j], P[j+16], P[j+32] and
P[j+48], where j is the low four index bits. H=1 means strong and H=0
means weak. Reset every P and H bit to zero, giving weakly not-taken
predictions immediately, without an initialization sweep or valid array.
Predict legal conditional branches from P[index]. Keep direct JAL taken
and JALR unpredicted, and retain all existing full-width source/target
bounds and alignment gates after the raw direction choice.

On a training update with actual outcome O, read the CURRENT prediction
bit old_P and its CURRENT shared strength old_H. Update the addressed
prediction bit to old_H ? old_P : O. Update the addressed shared strength
to (old_P == O), using the pre-update prediction. All other prediction
and strength bits hold. Without sharing, this is exactly the ordinary
two-bit saturating state machine recoded as direction and strength.
Sharing introduces interference only in resistance to changing direction;
it never writes another entry's P bit. Do not implement this as a one-bit
last-outcome predictor, arithmetic counter, or stale fetch-state update.

Decouple learning from EX with ONE pending training register containing
valid, six-bit index and actual outcome. Capture the existing branch_train,
branch_index and branch_outcome event each edge. On the next edge apply
the pending event to the current P/H state while independently accepting
the next event. Set pending valid to zero when no new event arrives.
Back-to-back updates, including the same P or H group, must apply in order
to current state; no event may be overwritten, merged or repeated. Reset
clears pending valid and predictor state. A captured event represents an
already advancing, legal, nonfaulting branch: its own redirect, a younger
redirect or subsequent bus/execute hold must not cancel its later update.
Only learning is delayed; verification and recovery remain same-cycle EX.

Organize storage as 16 constant-index groups, each with four separately
enabled P flops and one H flop. In each group, the two high training-index
bits select its old P through a local four-to-one mux for H's equality
update. The low four bits and pending valid enable only the selected
group's H. Each P flop has its own full-index match enable and uses its
group's directly wired H in its two-input update mux. This avoids a global
64-entry training-state read, saturation arithmetic, and a 64-bit pending
one-hot mask. Use ordinary synthesizable resettable flops, not vendor
primitives. Total logical state is 80 predictor bits plus 8 pending-event
bits, versus the champion's 128 predictor bits. Lookup first selects one
of four P bits per group with fetch PC[7:6], then selects the group with
fetch PC[5:2], using a balanced tree. Preserve this local update structure
rather than recreating an indexed two-bit counter array.

Fetch and a simultaneous table write use pre-edge P state consistently
for both the next-PC choice and captured predicted_taken. Preserve that
exact prediction in each queue token and ID/EX, including the empty-queue
bypass and arbitrarily long holds. Never refresh a stored token from the
live table. No new IF/ID or ID/EX metadata is needed. EX's training outputs
retain their current-cycle meanings; the pending register belongs in IF.

Keep exact forwarded branch resolution, direction-only correction, full
instruction-derived targets, immediate recovery priority, canceled-write
operand replay, load-use interlocks, all bus handshakes, and M-unit service
schedules unchanged. Keep default-illegal decode, misalignment traps,
link-write suppression, nret=1 IO, actual RVFI operands/PC/order and all
memory side-effect and forward-progress guarantees. Prediction state may
change performance only. A wrong prediction must never authorize a
wrong-path store, arithmetic launch or retirement.

A sequential reference-ISS trace of the marker-bracketed canonical run
contains 529,588 conditional branches. Immediate current-state training
gave 51,857 misses for the champion and 52,119 for 64 P bits with 16 H
bits, only 262 extra misses. Four, eight and 32 shared H bits produced
59,955, 54,913 and 51,835 misses respectively; 64 independent H bits
exactly reproduced the champion's 51,857. Choose 16 H bits as the compact
point with nearly preserved accuracy. These are policy-model counts,
not RTL cycles: they omit speculative fetches, queue timing, overlapping
branch instances and the proposed delayed learning. They support the
storage tradeoff but do not establish higher fitness or clock speed.

The forecast is 6 percent higher fitness with LOW confidence, driven by
fewer state bits and a shorter, local learner rather than assumed higher
direction accuracy. H sharing and one-cycle-later training can increase
corrections, and unrelated ALU/divider/recovery paths may limit Fmax.
This final circuit has not been measured in RTL or Gowin; no demonstrated
fitness improvement is claimed. At unchanged 4,037,538 bracket cycles,
acceptance requires about 77.27 MHz median Fmax; any cycle increase raises
that requirement proportionally. Require measured fitness strictly above
191.37616 iterations/s with the prescribed median vendor evaluation.

Adapt only policy/state-specific test expectations. Preserve every
architectural assertion, the existing nine-cycle branch-to-divider gap,
formal liveness window and all canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks.
Run unchanged formal, real/ALTOPS pipeline tests, reference-ISS cosimulation
and stalled CoreMark validation before median Gowin evaluation. Include
all state/outcome transitions, strength sharing interference, both miss
directions, same-edge lookup/write, ordered pending events, reset during
a pending update, queue holds, invalid encodings, bounded speculative
targets, source replay and independent bus stalls.
